passages.name: 2026年6月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 私营电力行业是非洲通电的关键
passages.genre: 议论文 · 能源与经济发展
passages.summary: 撒哈拉以南非洲仍有数亿人用不上可靠的电力，生计和前途因此面临风险；接受调查的人当中，不到一半的人说国家电网的电力供应是可靠的，这导致人们采用既昂贵又有害的临时解决办法，例如使用有毒、污染环境的发电机。作者认为，迅速壮大的私营电力行业掌握着以所需的速度和规模缩小非洲能源获取差距的关键，许多政府也已开始接纳私营部门作为合作伙伴。如今，南苏丹的丹尼尔·阿戈克所在的小镇已由一家私营公司通电，他的电脑技能培训生意经营顺利，正日益壮大。

paras.en: On a warm October morning, Daniel Agok woke up to another disappointing day at his school in Wanyjok, South Sudan.
paras.zh: 十月一个温暖的早晨，丹尼尔·阿戈克醒来，在他位于南苏丹万约克的学校，等着他的又是令人失望的一天。

paras.en: The classes he had planned, teaching computer skills to aspiring young professionals, were canceled, due to an unreliable diesel generator and the absence of a municipal power grid in his area.
paras.zh: 他原本计划给有志成为专业人才的年轻人教授电脑技能，但由于柴油发电机不可靠，加上他所在的地区没有市政电网，这些课都取消了。

w.m: adj. 有志成为……的；有抱负的
n. 专业人才；专业人士

paras.en: Now, he would be losing frustrated customers as well as income.
paras.zh: 这下，他既会失去那些恼火的顾客，也会损失收入。

paras.en: Agok is just one of the hundreds of millions of people in sub-Saharan Africa, many of whom are business owners, who still do not have dependable electricity.
paras.zh: 在撒哈拉以南非洲，仍有数亿人用不上可靠的电力，其中许多是企业主，阿戈克只是这数亿人中的一员。

paras.en: This inequitable access to energy continues to put their livelihood and future at risk.
paras.zh: 能源获取上的这种不公平，持续让他们的生计和前途面临风险。

w.m: adj. 不公平的；不平等的

paras.en: The current system keeps a lid on the economic talents of people like Agok and his students.
paras.zh: 现行体制压制着阿戈克和他的学生这类人的经济才能。

paras.en: We must instead unleash their abilities and let Africa reach its true economic potential.
paras.zh: 我们必须转而释放他们的能力，让非洲发挥出真正的经济潜力。

paras.en: That means wiring Africa with clean, dependable energy.
paras.zh: 这意味着要用清洁、可靠的能源为非洲通电。

w.m: v. 为……接通电线；为……通电

paras.en: Historically, national governments on the continent have led electrification efforts, but fewer than half of the people surveyed say that the national grid is providing a reliable supply of electricity.
paras.zh: 从历史上看，非洲大陆的电气化工作一直由各国政府主导，但接受调查的人当中，不到一半的人说国家电网正在可靠地供应电力。

paras.en: This has led to expensive and harmful temporary “solutions”.
paras.zh: 这导致了种种既昂贵又有害的临时“解决办法”。

paras.en: In Nigeria alone experts estimate people spend $13 billion every year on fuel for toxic, polluting generators.
paras.zh: 据专家估计，仅在尼日利亚，人们每年就要花费130亿美元，为有毒、污染环境的发电机购买燃料。

paras.en: That number will only grow as the continent’s population hits 2.5 billion people by 2050.
paras.zh: 到2050年，非洲大陆的人口将达到25亿，这个数字只会随之增长。

paras.en: Deploying modern grid infrastructure with speed and at scale is essential to replacing these temporary solutions with reliable and affordable alternatives.
paras.zh: 要用可靠、价格实惠的替代方案取代这些临时解决办法，快速、大规模地部署现代电网基础设施至关重要。

w.m: adj. 价格实惠的；负担得起的
n. 替代方案；可供选择的事物

paras.en: The rapidly growing private power sector in Africa holds the key to achieving the speed and scale necessary to close the continent’s energy access gap.
paras.zh: 要缩小非洲大陆在能源获取上的差距，就必须达到足够的速度和规模，而非洲迅速壮大的私营电力行业掌握着实现这一点的关键。

w.m: adj. 不断壮大的；日益增长的

paras.en: Private companies today are building world-class infrastructure and driving forward economic growth with sustainable business models.
paras.zh: 如今，私营企业正在建设世界一流的基础设施，并凭借可持续的商业模式推动经济增长。

paras.en: In fact, many governments agree and have begun to embrace the private sector as partners in providing reliable power at scale.
paras.zh: 事实上，许多政府都认同这一点，已开始欣然接纳私营部门，将其视为大规模提供可靠电力的合作伙伴。

paras.en: In South Africa, President Cyril Ramaphosa has streamlined licensing requirements and enlisted the private sector to play a key role.
paras.zh: 在南非，西里尔·拉马福萨总统简化了许可证审批要求，并争取私营部门参与进来，发挥关键作用。

w.m: n. 许可证发放；许可审批
v. 争取（……的参与或帮助）；招募

paras.en: South Africa is just one example.
paras.zh: 南非只是其中一个例子。

paras.en: Across the continent, the private sector has delivered power faster and more reliably, and governments are increasingly turning to private partners.
paras.zh: 在整个非洲大陆，私营部门供电都更快、更可靠，各国政府也越来越多地转而依靠私营合作伙伴。

paras.en: With the right funding and structure in place, the private sector will come together to provide this essential service.
paras.zh: 只要合适的资金和架构到位，私营部门就会联合起来，提供这项必不可少的服务。

w.m: adj. 必不可少的；至关重要的

paras.en: After all, electrifying sub-Saharan Africa is a $350 billion opportunity.
paras.zh: 毕竟，为撒哈拉以南非洲通电是一个价值3500亿美元的机遇。

paras.en: Today, Daniel Agok is steadily growing his business in South Sudan.
paras.zh: 如今，丹尼尔·阿戈克正在南苏丹稳步扩大自己的生意。

paras.en: His town of Wanyjok was electrified by a private company, providing clean, reliable, and affordable power to his business and his neighbors.
paras.zh: 他所在的万约克镇由一家私营公司通了电，这家公司为他的生意和邻居们提供清洁、可靠、价格实惠的电力。

w.m: adj. 价格实惠的；负担得起的

paras.en: Agok now operates his growing computer skills training business smoothly.
paras.zh: 阿戈克现在顺利地经营着他那日益壮大的电脑技能培训生意。

w.m: adj. 日益壮大的；不断增长的

paras.en: His classes are no longer affected by the smell and the constant noise of the diesel generator, and he saves money with more affordable power.
paras.zh: 他的课不再受柴油发电机的气味和持续噪音的影响，而且电力更实惠，他也省了钱。

w.m: adj. 价格实惠的；负担得起的

paras.en: His students are developing hardware and software skills.
paras.zh: 他的学生正在培养硬件和软件技能。

passages.name: 2026年6月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 艺术家指控文生图AI工具侵权
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与法律
passages.summary: 三位艺术家对Stability AI、DeviantArt和Midjourney提起诉讼，指控这些文生图AI工具侵犯了数千名艺术家的权利：诉讼称，这几家公司所使用的Stable Diffusion工具是用从互联网上下载的数十亿张受版权保护的图像训练的，而它们使用这些图像时既没有给予艺术家补偿，也没有征得艺术家的同意。代理此案的律师事务所称，如果允许这类产品继续像现在这样运作，可以预见它们将取代艺术家。许多艺术家也对AI艺术可能存在的侵犯版权行为极为愤怒，并一直试图禁止AI艺术作品进入艺术分享平台；一些匿名的科技支持者则以“合理使用”条款为依据回应了这起诉讼，但由于合理使用的适用情况因案而异，很难笼统地断言一个数据集中的所有作品都受其保护。

paras.en: Three artists have brought a lawsuit against Stability AI, DeviantArt, and Midjourney, alleging that the text-to-image AI tools have infringed the rights of thousands of artists.
paras.zh: 三位艺术家对Stability AI、DeviantArt和Midjourney提起了诉讼，指控这些文生图AI工具侵犯了数千名艺术家的权利。

w.m: v. 指控；声称（尚未证实）
adj. 文生图的；由文字生成图像的

paras.en: The lawsuit claims that the Stable Diffusion tool used by Stability AI, DeviantArt, and Midjourney was trained on billions of copyrighted images downloaded from the internet and used by the companies “without compensation or consent from the artists”.
paras.zh: 诉讼称，Stability AI、DeviantArt和Midjourney所使用的Stable Diffusion工具，是用从互联网上下载的数十亿张受版权保护的图像训练的，而这几家公司使用这些图像时，“既没有给予艺术家补偿，也没有征得他们的同意”。

paras.en: The artists are represented by The Joseph Saveri Law Firm and Matthew Butterick.
paras.zh: 这三位艺术家由约瑟夫·萨韦里律师事务所和马修·巴特里克代理。

paras.en: “If Stable Diffusion and similar products are allowed to continue to operate as they do now, the foreseeable result is they will replace the very artists whose stolen works power these AI products with whom they are competing,” the law firm wrote in a press release.
paras.zh: 该律师事务所在一份新闻稿中写道：“如果允许Stable Diffusion及类似产品继续像现在这样运作，可以预见的结果是，它们将取代的恰恰是这样一些艺术家：这些AI产品靠他们被盗用的作品驱动，又正在与他们竞争。”

w.m: adj. 正是的；恰恰的（用于强调）
adj. 被盗（用）的；被窃取的

paras.en: “AI image products are not just an infringement of artists’ rights; they will eliminate ‘artist’ as a viable career path.
paras.zh: “AI图像产品不只是侵犯艺术家的权利，还会让‘艺术家’不再是一条可行的职业道路。

w.m: 使……不再是（某种选择）；排除……作为……
职业道路；职业发展路径

paras.en: In addition to obtaining compensation for the wrongful conduct, this lawsuit seeks to prevent that outcome and ensure these products follow the same rules as any other new technology that involves the use of massive amounts of intellectual property.
paras.zh: 这起诉讼除了要为这种不法行为获得赔偿，还力求防止出现这一结果，并确保这些产品与其他任何涉及使用海量知识产权的新技术遵守同样的规则。

paras.en: If streaming music can be accomplished within the law, so can AI products.”
paras.zh: 如果流媒体音乐能够在法律允许的范围内实现，那么AI产品也同样可以。”

w.m: 在法律允许的范围内；合法地

paras.en: Since text-to-image generators have increased in popularity in the past year, many artists have been vocalizing their opposition to AI art after seeing their own distorted signatures appear in AI art and finding out that their work was used to train the tools without their permission.
paras.zh: 随着文生图生成器在过去一年里越来越受欢迎，许多艺术家看到自己被扭曲的签名出现在AI艺术作品中，又发现自己的作品未经许可就被用来训练这些工具，此后便一直公开表示反对AI艺术。

w.m: adj. 文生图的；由文字生成图像的
越来越受欢迎；日益流行

paras.en: Not only are many artists furious at the possible copyright violations of AI art, but they have also been frustrated by how AI tools are able to sidestep the labor and art processes they are required to go through.
paras.zh: 许多艺术家不仅对AI艺术可能存在的侵犯版权行为极为愤怒，而且AI工具能够绕开他们必须经历的劳动和艺术创作过程，也一直令他们感到沮丧。

w.m: 不仅……而且（not only 置于句首时句子部分倒装）

paras.en: As a result, many artists have been trying to ban AI art from art-sharing platforms.
paras.zh: 因此，许多艺术家一直试图禁止AI艺术作品进入艺术分享平台。

w.m: 禁止……进入（某处）；不准……参与

paras.en: As AI innovation continues at a rapid speed, it seems that artists and lawmakers are trying to put a brake on further developments before it’s too late.
paras.zh: 随着AI创新持续快速推进，艺术家和立法者似乎正试图趁为时未晚，给进一步的发展踩刹车。

w.m: 趁为时未晚；趁还来得及

paras.en: Many tech enthusiasts are still rallying around the promise of AI tools to create detailed images cheaply and quickly—anonymous tech supporters have already published a response to Butterick and Joseph Saveri’s lawsuit on a website, using the “fair use” clause as the basis for why copyrighted images could be used by the tool.
paras.zh: 许多科技爱好者仍在力挺AI工具，看好它们以低廉的成本快速生成精细图像的前景——一些匿名的科技支持者已在一个网站上针对巴特里克和约瑟夫·萨韦里提起的诉讼发表了回应，以“合理使用”条款为依据，说明该工具为何可以使用受版权保护的图像。

w.m: n. 科技；技术（technology 的简称）
adj. 精细的；细节丰富的

paras.en: Fair use, a legal doctrine that allows for a limited usage of copyrighted materials without permission from the original creators for purposes such as teaching and news sharing, is what a lot of generative model creators claim that their training data is covered by.
paras.zh: 合理使用是一项法律原则，允许出于教学、新闻分享等目的，在未经原创作者许可的情况下有限度地使用受版权保护的材料；许多生成式模型的开发者声称，他们的训练数据受到的正是这一原则的保护。

w.m: n. 创作者；（模型等的）开发者
受（法律、规定等）保护；在……范围内

paras.en: However, since fair use applies differently to each case, it’s hard to make a blanket statement that all works in a dataset are covered.
paras.zh: 然而，由于合理使用的适用情况因案而异，很难笼统地断言一个数据集中的所有作品都受其保护。

w.m: adj. 笼统的；一概而论的
v. 涵盖；（法律、规定等）保护

passages.name: 2026年6月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 智能手机给青少年的父母带来的挑战
passages.genre: 议论文 · 青少年与科技
passages.summary: 智能手机一直给青少年的父母带来挑战：一项新研究显示，在青少年的父母中，约有一半担心孩子在网上接触到露骨内容；青少年花在社交媒体上的时长可能导致焦虑和抑郁，这同样令人忧虑，甚至有过之而无不及。过长的屏幕使用时间有害，不停地消费媒体内容会妨碍与童年相关的健康活动；大量研究也表明，过度使用智能手机会让青少年产生严重的焦虑、抑郁和孤立感。作者自己也一直在为智能手机使用时间和孩子较劲；作者不认为美国政府应该监管社交媒体和青少年使用智能手机的行为，但认为这是一个至关重要的话题，父母需要了解并认真对待。

paras.en: Smartphones have always posed challenges for parents of teens.
paras.zh: 智能手机一直给青少年的父母带来挑战。

paras.en: From social media apps to excessive screen time, the digital world is as threatening as the physical.
paras.zh: 从社交媒体应用到过长的屏幕使用时间，数字世界和现实世界一样充满威胁。

w.m: adj. 构成威胁的；危险的
adj. 现实的；实体的（the physical 指现实世界）

paras.en: A new study shows that about half of parents of teens are worried about their teens being exposed to explicit content online.
paras.zh: 一项新研究显示，在青少年的父母中，约有一半担心孩子在网上接触到露骨内容。

w.m: adj. 露骨的；（色情、暴力内容）不加掩饰的

paras.en: This is a valid concern, of course.
paras.zh: 当然，这是一种合理的担忧。

paras.en: But there are ways to alleviate the spread of explicit content, from changing the settings in their kids’ phones to monitoring such content with apps like Bark.
paras.zh: 但有一些办法可以减少露骨内容的传播，从更改孩子手机上的设置，到用Bark之类的应用监控这类内容，不一而足。

paras.en: Just as alarming, if not more so, is that the amount of time teens spend on social media can lead to anxiety and depression.
paras.zh: 同样令人忧虑、甚至有过之而无不及的是，青少年花在社交媒体上的时长可能导致焦虑和抑郁。

w.m: adj. 令人忧虑的；令人惊恐的
甚至更……；有过之而无不及

paras.en: Excessive screen time has detrimental effects, for a lot of obvious reasons.
paras.zh: 过长的屏幕使用时间会造成有害影响，原因有很多，而且显而易见。

w.m: adj. 显而易见的；明显的

paras.en: Constant media consumption inhibits healthy activities associated with childhood, like spending time outside, exercising, talking to friends and family.
paras.zh: 不停地消费媒体内容会妨碍与童年相关的健康活动，比如待在户外、锻炼身体、和朋友家人聊天。

w.m: adj. 持续不断的；不停的
n. （对媒体内容等的）消费；使用

paras.en: If it interferes with sleep, that’s even worse.
paras.zh: 如果干扰到睡眠，那就更糟了。

paras.en: Ample research shows too much smartphone use produces significant anxiety, depression, and feelings of isolation in teens.
paras.zh: 大量研究表明，过度使用智能手机会让青少年产生严重的焦虑、抑郁和孤立感。

paras.en: Teens log on to social media or spend time online trying to make connections, but end up feeling more alone and sadder than ever.
paras.zh: 青少年登录社交媒体或花时间上网，想与人建立联系，最后却感到比以往任何时候都更孤单、更难过。

w.m: 与人建立联系；结交他人
最后（处于某种状态）；到头来

paras.en: Faceless communication not only produces feelings of isolation and loneliness but increases instances of online bullying and susceptibility to criminal conduct.
paras.zh: 不见面的交流不仅会让人产生孤立感和孤独感，还会增加网络欺凌事件，并使人更容易受到犯罪行为的影响。

w.m: adj. 不见面的；不露面的

paras.en: Though I’ve banned most social media, I’ve still battled smartphone time with my own kids.
paras.zh: 虽然我已经禁用了大部分社交媒体，但我还是一直在为智能手机使用时间和自己的孩子较劲。

paras.en: A lot of the time I wish I could throw my kids’ smartphones into the nearest lake.
paras.zh: 很多时候，我真希望能把孩子们的智能手机扔进最近的湖里。

w.m: 真希望某人能（虚拟语气，表示难以实现的愿望）

paras.en: The convenience of communication—when they need a ride home from school after practice, for instance—often feels like it isn’t worth the battle to keep their screen time low and productive, and continue to encourage “real-life” activities outside and with friends and family.
paras.zh: 通讯上的便利——比如孩子训练结束后需要有人从学校接他们回家的时候——常常让人觉得不值得这番较劲：既要让孩子的屏幕使用时间少而有益，又要继续鼓励他们在户外、和朋友家人一起参加“现实生活”中的活动。

paras.en: I understand the addiction and often tell them I’m not sure how I would have handled having a smartphone as a teen.
paras.zh: 我理解这种上瘾，还常常跟他们说，我不确定自己十几岁的时候要是有一部智能手机，会怎么应对。

w.m: n. 青少年；十几岁的孩子

paras.en: As an adult, I, too, struggle with overuse.
paras.zh: 作为成年人，我自己也苦于过度使用手机。

paras.en: In a recent TV interview to promote a new film about a mother and daughter navigating social media use, actress Kate Winslet expressed her view on teens and social media—and her concern mirrors the trends.
paras.zh: 女演员凯特·温斯莱特最近为宣传一部新电影接受了电视采访，影片讲述一对母女如何应对社交媒体使用问题；她在采访中表达了自己对青少年与社交媒体的看法，而她的担忧反映了上述趋势。

w.m: v. 应对；处理（复杂局面）

paras.en: “I do definitely feel that the world of social media is frightening to parents because we don’t really know what’s there,” she said.
paras.zh: “我确确实实地感到，社交媒体的世界令父母害怕，因为我们并不真正知道那里面有什么。”她说。

w.m: 确实感到（do 加动词原形表示强调）
adj. 令人害怕的；吓人的

paras.en: “We don’t know how our children are using it.
paras.zh: “我们不知道孩子们是怎么使用它的。

paras.en: We don’t know the effects that it’s really having on them.”
paras.zh: 我们不知道它实际上正在对他们产生什么影响。”

paras.en: I don’t think the US government should regulate social media and teen smartphone use, but it is a vital topic for parents to understand and take seriously.
paras.zh: 我不认为美国政府应该监管社交媒体和青少年使用智能手机的行为，但这是一个至关重要的话题，父母需要了解并认真对待。

paras.en: Unfortunately, now, parents don’t just have to worry about real-world dangers, but also about all the ones sneaking online and the effects they have on teenagers and their mental health.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，如今父母不仅要担心现实世界中的危险，还要担心在网上悄然出没的所有危险，以及这些危险对青少年及其心理健康造成的影响。

w.m: adv. 遗憾的是；不幸的是
v. 偷偷摸摸地行动；悄悄溜进

passages.name: 2026年6月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 心态决定你有多自律
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与职场
passages.summary: 工作中的自律，有时是抵制诱惑的能力，有时是在精力和动力似乎不足时坚持把任务做下去的能力。多年来，心理学研究一直表明，自制力是一种会随着使用而耗竭的资源，但近来的研究指出了心态的重要性：把自律看作可消耗的资源，意志力往往会越用越弱；相信运用自制力会增强自制力，就更有可能体验到这一点。作者建议回想自己起初遇到困难、但仍奋力向前完成任务的经历，想象自律的榜样身处自己的境地，并为自己在坚持中能运用更多意志力而自豪；自律就好比肌肉，每一次抵制诱惑或在缺乏动力时仍坚持做任务，都会让它变得更强。

paras.en: What does self-discipline look like at work?
paras.zh: 工作中的自律是什么样的？

paras.en: Sometimes, it’s the ability to resist temptation, such as distractions to avoid a particular task.
paras.zh: 有时，自律是抵制诱惑的能力，比如抵制借分心的事来逃避某项任务的诱惑。

w.m: adj. 某个特定的；特别的

paras.en: Other times it’s the ability to persist with a task when your energy and motivation seem low.
paras.zh: 另一些时候，自律则是在你精力和动力似乎不足时，坚持把任务做下去的能力。

paras.en: What do you believe about the nature of your own self-discipline?
paras.zh: 你认为自己的自律本质上是怎样的？

paras.en: Is it something that runs on internal energy that is spent with use?
paras.zh: 它是不是靠内在能量运转，这种能量会随着使用而消耗掉？

paras.en: Or is it something that is bolstered as you apply it and persist?
paras.zh: 还是说，它会随着你的运用和坚持而得到增强？

paras.en: Your answer matters, as it determines how much self-discipline you experience.
paras.zh: 你的答案很重要，因为它决定了你能体验到多少自律。

paras.en: For years, research in psychology pointed to self-control as a resource that is depleted with use and needs to be restored through breaks, rest, or sleep.
paras.zh: 多年来，心理学研究一直表明，自制力是一种会随着使用而耗竭的资源，需要通过中途休息、休整或睡眠来恢复。

paras.en: More recently, however, research points to the importance of mindset.
paras.zh: 然而，近来的研究则指出了心态的重要性。

paras.en: If you view self-discipline as an expendable resource, your willpower tends to fade with use.
paras.zh: 如果你把自律看作一种可消耗的资源，意志力往往就会越用越弱。

w.m: adj. 可消耗的；消耗性的

paras.en: If you believe that exercising your self-control strengthens and fuels it, that is more likely to be your experience as you resist temptation or push yourself to get something done that is not appealing.
paras.zh: 如果你相信运用自制力会增强它、为它提供动力，那么在你抵制诱惑或逼自己去完成某件并不吸引人的事时，你就更有可能有这样的体验。

w.m: adj. 有吸引力的；吸引人的

paras.en: If you don’t already view self-discipline as a force that feeds itself, what might you do?
paras.zh: 如果你还没有把自律看作一种能自我滋养的力量，你可以怎么做呢？

paras.en: Reflect on times that you had initial difficulty resisting temptation, getting started on something, or sticking with it, but pushed ahead and accomplished the task or met the goal.
paras.zh: 回想一下那些时候：你起初很难抵制诱惑、很难着手做某件事或很难坚持做下去，但还是奋力向前，完成了任务或实现了目标。

paras.en: That’s the kind of experience we’re talking about with this particular belief about self-discipline, and you’ve already had such an experience, so you’ve shown that it’s possible.
paras.zh: 我们在谈论对自律的这种特定看法时，所说的就是这类经历；而你已经有过这样的经历，所以你已经证明了这是可能的。

paras.en: When you feel your willpower and motivation fading, remind yourself of those previous experiences and imagine the same happening now.
paras.zh: 感到意志力和动力逐渐减弱时，就提醒自己想想以前的那些经历，并想象同样的情形此刻正在发生。

w.m: 提醒某人想起；使某人想起

paras.en: What if your experiences have always seemed to indicate that your self-control diminishes with use, and you need breaks to recharge?
paras.zh: 如果你的经历似乎一直表明，你的自制力会随着使用而减少，你需要中途休息来恢复精力，那该怎么办？

paras.en: There’s nothing wrong with that as long as you can afford to take those breaks.
paras.zh: 只要你有条件这样中途休息，这就没什么不对。

w.m: v. 有条件（做）；负担得起

paras.en: If not, remind yourself that not everyone experiences self-discipline as a depletable resource and that your experience might be different if you focus on gathering more energy at this point rather than focusing on how difficult it is to continue or the need for a break.
paras.zh: 如果没有这样的条件，就提醒自己：并非每个人都觉得自律是一种会耗尽的资源；而且，如果你此时专注于积聚更多精力，而不是专注于继续下去有多难或需要休息一下，你的体验就可能会不同。

w.m: adj. 会耗尽的；可耗竭的
专注于；把注意力集中于

paras.en: Also, if you know someone who is a role model of self-discipline, picture that person in your situation, persisting in the task.
paras.zh: 此外，如果你认识某个在自律方面堪称榜样的人，就想象一下此人身处你的境地，坚持做这项任务的样子。

paras.en: Regardless of how you do it, as you push forward to continue to make progress, be sure to mentally reinforce yourself by taking pride in your ability to exert more willpower as you persist.
paras.zh: 无论用什么方法，在你奋力向前、继续取得进展的过程中，一定要为自己在坚持中能运用更多意志力而感到自豪，以此在心理上强化自己。

w.m: adv. 在心理上；在精神上

paras.en: The benefits of exerting willpower are cumulative.
paras.zh: 运用意志力的好处会不断累积。

paras.en: Your self-discipline is akin to a muscle, and each time you resist temptation or persist in a task despite a lack of motivation, you strengthen that muscle, leading to less effort and resistance in similar instances in the future.
paras.zh: 你的自律就好比一块肌肉：每当你抵制诱惑，或者在缺乏动力的情况下依然坚持做一项任务，你都在让这块肌肉变得更强，从而使你今后在类似情况下需要付出的努力更少、遇到的阻力更小。

passages.name: 2026年6月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 遏制利润转移需要全球最低税
passages.genre: 议论文 · 经济与税收
passages.summary: 大约十年前，二十国集团同意严厉打击跨国公司滥用避税天堂的行为，但问题反而越发严重：作者的研究发现，2019年，世界最大的跨国企业把在其他国家所获利润的37%转移到了避税天堂，据作者估计，由此流失的公司税达到了公司税总收入的10%。作者认为，利润转移的根本原因在于其他国家优惠或宽松的公司税率等激励因素，如果各国能就全球最低公司税率达成一致，这一问题就会基本消失。2021年，130多个国家签署同意了这类机制，美国却一直未能通过相关立法。作者的研究表明，要扭转越来越多的公司利润转移到避税天堂的趋势，实施这类税收改革是必要的。

paras.en: About a decade ago, the G-20, a forum of the world’s biggest economies, agreed to crack down on multinational corporations’ abusive use of tax havens.
paras.zh: 大约十年前，由世界最大经济体组成的论坛二十国集团同意严厉打击跨国公司滥用避税天堂的行为。

paras.en: This resulted in a plan that aimed to curb practices that shielded a large chunk of corporate profits from tax authorities.
paras.zh: 这促成了一项计划，旨在遏制那些让很大一部分公司利润避开税务机关的做法。

paras.en: But, instead of the plan reining in the use of tax havens—countries such as the Bahamas and Cayman Islands with very low or no effective tax rates—the problem has only gotten worse.
paras.zh: 但是，这项计划非但没能控制住对避税天堂（巴哈马、开曼群岛等实际税率很低或为零的国家）的利用，问题反而越发严重了。

paras.en: In a new study, we measured the excessive profits reported in tax havens that cannot be explained by ordinary economic activity such as employees, factories and research in those countries.
paras.zh: 在一项新研究中，我们测算了在避税天堂申报的超额利润，这些利润无法用当地员工、工厂、研究等正常经济活动来解释。

paras.en: Our findings show a striking pattern of artificial shifting of paper profits to tax havens by corporations, which has been relentless since the 1980s.
paras.zh: 我们的研究结果显示出一种惊人的模式：公司人为地把账面利润转移到避税天堂，这种转移自20世纪80年代以来从未停歇。

w.m: adj. 惊人的；引人注目的
adj. 持续不断的；不停歇的

paras.en: We found that the world’s biggest multinational businesses shifted 37% of the profits—$969 billion—they earned in other countries to tax havens in 2019.
paras.zh: 我们发现，2019年，世界最大的跨国企业把在其他国家所获利润中的37%（即9690亿美元）转移到了避税天堂。

paras.en: The figure was less than 2% in the 1970s.
paras.zh: 20世纪70年代，这一数字还不到2%。

paras.en: The main reasons for the large increase were the growth of the tax avoidance industry in the 1980s and U.S. policies that made it easier to shift profits from high-tax countries to tax havens.
paras.zh: 这一数字大幅上升的主要原因有两个：一是20世纪80年代避税行业的发展壮大，二是美国的政策使利润更容易从高税率国家转移到避税天堂。

paras.en: We estimate that the amount of corporate taxes lost as a result reached 10% of total corporate tax revenue in 2019, up from less than 0.1% in the 1970s.
paras.zh: 我们估计，由此流失的公司税在2019年达到了公司税总收入的10%，而20世纪70年代还不到0.1%。

paras.en: In 2019, the total government tax loss globally was $250 billion.
paras.zh: 2019年，全球各国政府的税收损失总额为2500亿美元。

paras.en: U.S. multinational corporations alone accounted for about half of that, followed by the U.K. and Germany.
paras.zh: 仅美国的跨国公司就占了其中约一半，其次是英国和德国。

paras.en: How do policymakers fix this?
paras.zh: 政策制定者如何解决这个问题呢？

w.m: n. 政策制定者；决策者

paras.en: So far, the world as a whole has been trying to solve this problem by cutting or scrapping corporate taxes in a very gradual way.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，全世界总体上一直在试图解决这个问题，办法是以非常渐进的方式削减或取消公司税。

paras.en: In the past 40 years, the global effective corporate tax rate has fallen from 23% to 17%.
paras.zh: 在过去40年里，全球实际公司税率已从23%降至17%。

paras.en: At the same time, governments have relied more heavily on consumption taxes.
paras.zh: 与此同时，各国政府已更加依赖消费税。

w.m: adv. 在很大程度上；严重地

paras.en: But the root cause of profit-shifting is the incentives involved, such as generous or lenient corporate tax rates in other countries.
paras.zh: 但利润转移的根本原因在于其中涉及的激励因素，比如其他国家优惠或宽松的公司税率。

paras.en: If countries could agree on a global minimum corporate tax rate of, say, 20%, the problem of profit-shifting would largely disappear, as tax havens would simply cease to exist.
paras.zh: 如果各国能就全球最低公司税率（比如20%）达成一致，利润转移问题就会基本消失，因为避税天堂将干脆不复存在。

w.m: adv. 基本上；在很大程度上

paras.en: This type of mechanism is exactly what more than 130 countries signed on to in 2021, with implementation of a 15% minimum tax set to begin soon in the EU, U.K., Japan, Indonesia and many other countries.
paras.zh: 2021年，130多个国家签署同意的正是这类机制，欧盟、英国、日本、印度尼西亚以及其他许多国家即将开始实施税率为15%的最低税。

paras.en: The U.S. has notably not been able to pass this legislation.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，美国一直未能通过这项立法。

w.m: adv. 值得注意的是；尤其

paras.en: Our research suggests implementing this type of tax reform is necessary for reversing the shift of ever-greater amounts of corporate profits to tax havens—instead of these profits being taxed by the governments where the corporations operate and create value.
paras.zh: 我们的研究表明，要扭转这样一种趋势，就有必要实施这类税收改革：越来越多的公司利润转移到避税天堂，而不是由公司经营和创造价值所在地的政府来征税。

w.m: adj. 越来越大的；越来越多的

passages.name: 2026年6月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 儿童使用社交媒体：不应禁止，但须监管
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与健康
passages.summary: 儿童使用社交媒体是个问题，但这并不意味着应该加以禁止；设想一个不让青少年使用成年人所用平台的世界，既不现实，也不可取。研究发现，英国少女高得惊人的抑郁症患病率与她们花在社交媒体上的时间密切相关；这项研究虽未证明社交媒体会导致抑郁症，但这种关联的重要性不应低估。卫生大臣希望出台时长和年龄限制方面的官方指南，今年预计还将出台《适龄设计规范》，作者认为这两项举措都值得欢迎，但对数字媒体巨头的法定监管早就该实行了。当然，社交媒体公司并非我们一切弊病的根源，年轻人抑郁症发病率上升还有其他原因。

paras.en: Children’s use of social media is a problem.
paras.zh: 儿童使用社交媒体是个问题。

paras.en: That doesn’t mean it should be stopped.
paras.zh: 这并不意味着就应该加以禁止。

paras.en: While younger children should not be on platforms where 13 is the minimum age, it is neither practical nor desirable to imagine a world in which teenagers are prevented from accessing the platforms and messaging systems that the adults around them use to organise their lives.
paras.zh: 虽然年龄更小的孩子不应该使用最低年龄要求为13岁的平台，但青少年身边的成年人用平台和通讯系统来安排生活，设想一个不让青少年使用这些平台和系统的世界，既不现实，也不可取。

w.m: adj. 现实的；切实可行的
adj. 可取的；值得拥有的
阻止某人做；使某人不能做

paras.en: But the pleasure and stimulation that people of all ages find on their screens and smartphones must not blind us to the harm that spending time in this way can cause.
paras.zh: 但是，各个年龄段的人都能从屏幕和智能手机上获得乐趣和刺激，这绝不能让我们对以这种方式消磨时间可能造成的危害视而不见。

paras.en: The finding that the alarmingly high rate of depression in British teenage girls is closely correlated to time spent on social media is extremely concerning.
paras.zh: 研究发现，英国少女高得惊人的抑郁症患病率与她们花在社交媒体上的时间密切相关，这一发现令人极为担忧。

w.m: adv. 惊人地；令人担忧地
adj. 十几岁的；青少年的

paras.en: Research found that two in five girls are on social media for at least three hours a day—with half as many boys engaged to the same extent.
paras.zh: 研究发现，五分之二的女孩每天使用社交媒体至少三小时，而以同等程度投入其中的男孩人数是女孩的一半。

w.m: adj. 投入的；参与其中的
以同等程度；在同样程度上

paras.en: More than a third of depressed girls have experienced online harassment.
paras.zh: 在患抑郁症的女孩中，超过三分之一遭受过网络骚扰。

w.m: adj. 患抑郁症的；抑郁的

paras.en: About half of affected girls suffered disrupted sleep, compared with 20% of depressed boys.
paras.zh: 在患病的女孩中，约有一半睡眠受到干扰，相比之下，患抑郁症的男孩中这一比例为20%。

w.m: adj. 患病的；受（疾病）影响的
v. 遭受；经历（不好的事）
adj. 受到干扰的；被打乱的
adj. 患抑郁症的；抑郁的

paras.en: Although the research does not prove that social media causes depression, the importance of the finding that there is a connection should not be underestimated.
paras.zh: 尽管这项研究并未证明社交媒体会导致抑郁症，但二者之间存在关联这一发现，其重要性不应低估。

paras.en: Schools have done important work in communicating key messages about the risks of online abuse.
paras.zh: 在传达网络侵害风险的关键信息方面，学校已经做了重要的工作。

paras.en: But when it comes to broader questions about “screen time”, many professionals as well as parents are confused and uncertain.
paras.zh: 但一谈到“屏幕时间”方面更宽泛的问题，许多专业人士和家长都感到困惑，心里没底。

w.m: 屏幕时间（使用电子屏幕的时间）
adj. 不确定的；拿不准的

paras.en: The health secretary, Matt Hancock, wants official guidelines on time and age limits.
paras.zh: 卫生大臣马特·汉考克希望出台有关时长限制和年龄限制的官方指南。

paras.en: This idea has the virtue of simplicity, though some experts question its effects and call for a greater degree of differentiation, arguing that time online by itself is not a bad thing and it all depends on what you are doing.
paras.zh: 这一想法的优点在于简单，不过一些专家质疑其效果，呼吁在更大程度上加以区分，他们认为，上网时间本身并不是坏事，一切都取决于你在做什么。

paras.en: Also due this year is information commissioner Elizabeth Denham’s Age Appropriate Design Code, covering the use of children’s personal data.
paras.zh: 今年预计还将出台信息专员伊丽莎白·德纳姆的《适龄设计规范》，该规范涉及儿童个人数据的使用。

w.m: adj. 预定的；预计（某时）到来的

paras.en: Both initiatives are welcome.
paras.zh: 这两项举措都值得欢迎。

w.m: adj. 值得欢迎的；受欢迎的

paras.en: But the government is playing catch-up.
paras.zh: 但政府是在追赶落下的进度。

paras.en: Statutory regulation of the digital media giants is long overdue.
paras.zh: 对数字媒体巨头的法定监管早就该实行了。

w.m: 早就该实行的；早该到来的

paras.en: The failure to protect children from data harvesting and targeted advertising thus far is as shocking as the lack of concern shown by the companies themselves with regard to children’s psychological health.
paras.zh: 迄今为止都未能保护儿童免受数据采集和定向广告的侵害，这与这些公司本身对儿童心理健康缺乏关心一样令人震惊。

w.m: 数据采集；（大规模）数据收集
adj. 定向的；有针对性的

paras.en: Of course, social media companies are not the source of all our ills, and can offer a too-easy target for politicians keen to divert attention from inadequately resourced schools and health services.
paras.zh: 当然，社交媒体公司并非我们一切弊病的根源，而且对于那些急于把人们的注意力从资源不足的学校和医疗服务上转移开的政客来说，它们可能是一个过于容易的攻击目标。

paras.en: There are other reasons for the rising incidence of depression in young people, with increasing pressure to succeed in education and in life more broadly—to be famous, beautiful, rich—often cited as a source of unhappiness or anxiety which can, if aggravated by other factors, and not managed, tip into ill health.
paras.zh: 年轻人抑郁症发病率不断上升还有其他原因：要在学业上、乃至更广泛地在人生中取得成功——要出名、要漂亮、要富有——这种压力与日俱增，常被列为不快乐或焦虑的一个根源；而如果其他因素使这种不快乐或焦虑加剧，又没有加以控制，就可能演变为疾病。

w.m: adj. 不断上升的；增长的

paras.en: Safeguarding means more than the avoidance of physical threat.
paras.zh: 保护儿童不只意味着避免身体上的威胁。

w.m: n. （对儿童等弱势群体的）保护

passages.name: 2025年12月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 从验证码看数字技术对人的驯化
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科技与社会
passages.summary: 作者登录一项网络服务时被要求完成验证码测试，事后才意识到，自己是在无偿扩充一个数据集，这个数据集用于训练引导自动驾驶汽车的机器学习软件。验证码被称作“自动化图灵测试”，如今却是机器让我们表演把戏来证明自己是人类，而这一前所未有的转变很少有人讨论。两位学者认为，我们已被驯化得接受一个由“智能”技术主宰的世界，变得有点像机器；作者对此表示赞同，并指出如今相当一部分数字技术把人类视为（并用作）手段，去实现并非我们自己的目的。

paras.en: The other day I had to log into a service I hadn’t used before.
paras.zh: 前几天，我得登录一项以前没用过的服务。

w.m: （过去完成时）在那之前没有做过

paras.en: Since I was a new user, the website decided that it needed to check I wasn’t a robot and so set me a Captcha test to determine whether the user is a person or a machine.
paras.zh: 由于我是新用户，网站认定需要核实我不是机器人，于是给我出了一道验证码测试题，以确定用户是人还是机器。

w.m: n. 验证码（区分人与机器的测试）

paras.en: I was presented with an image of a roadside scene over which was laid a grid.
paras.zh: 呈现在我面前的是一张路边场景的图片，图上铺着一层网格。

paras.en: My “challenge” was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign.
paras.zh: 我的“挑战”是点击网格中每一个含有交通标志的格子。

paras.en: I did so, a bit irritated.
paras.zh: 我照做了，心里有点恼火。

paras.en: Then I was presented with another image and another grid—also with a request to identify road signs.
paras.zh: 接着，呈现在我面前的又是一张图片和一个网格，同样要求我识别出道路标志。

paras.en: Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.
paras.zh: 我像羔羊一样乖乖照办，随后网站接受了我输入的信息。

w.m: 像羔羊一样温顺地；乖乖地

paras.en: And then I realised what I had been doing was adding to a dataset for training the machine-learning software that guides self-driving cars.
paras.zh: 这时我才意识到，我刚才一直在做的，是扩充一个数据集，这个数据集用于训练引导自动驾驶汽车的机器学习软件。

paras.en: So, to gain access to an automated service that will benefit financially from my input, I first have to do some unpaid labor to help improve the performance of autonomous vehicles.
paras.zh: 所以，一项自动化服务将从我输入的信息中获得经济利益，而我为了获准使用它，首先得做一些无偿劳动，帮助提升自动驾驶车辆的性能。

w.m: 获准使用；获得……的使用权
adv. 在经济上；在金钱方面
adj. 自动驾驶的；自主的

paras.en: Neat, eh?
paras.zh: 挺巧妙的，是吧？

w.m: int. （用于句末征求同意）是吧；对吧

paras.en: But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an “automated Turing test”.
paras.zh: 不过还要注意另一层绝妙的讽刺：验证码被称作“自动化图灵测试”。

w.m: adj. 绝妙的；令人愉快的

paras.en: The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn’t tell whether it was a human or a robot.
paras.zh: 你也许还记得，图灵测试当初被构想为一种方法，使人类能够判断一台机器能否回应得让人分辨不出它是人还是机器人。

paras.en: So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!
paras.zh: 这么说来，我们已经不知不觉走进了这样一个世界：机器让我们表演把戏，来证明自己是人类！

paras.en: The strangest aspect of this unparalleled shift is how under-discussed it has been.
paras.zh: 这一前所未有的转变最奇怪的地方，在于人们对它的讨论一直如此之少。

w.m: adj. 前所未有的；无与伦比的
adj. 讨论不足的；很少被讨论的

paras.en: The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind.
paras.zh: 我脑海中浮现出“温水煮青蛙”这个比喻。

w.m: 温水煮青蛙（喻指在缓慢变化中丧失警觉）
浮现在脑海中；（使人）想到

paras.en: Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don’t see what’s been happening to us?
paras.zh: 数字技术是否已经如此潜移默化地驯化了我们，以至于我们看不到自己身上一直在发生什么？

w.m: adv. 潜移默化地；不易察觉地

paras.en: Have we been conditioned to accept a world governed by “smart” tech, trading for convenience to the point where we become a bit like machines ourselves?
paras.zh: 我们是否已经被驯化得接受了一个由“智能”技术主宰的世界，用其他东西换取便利，到了自己都变得有点像机器的地步？

paras.en: In a recent startling and thoughtful book, two scholars—Brett Frischmann, a law professor, and Evan Selinger, a philosopher—argue that the answer to that question is “yes”.
paras.zh: 在最近一本令人震惊又发人深思的书中，两位学者——法学教授布雷特·弗里施曼和哲学家埃文·塞林格——认为，这个问题的答案是“是的”。

w.m: adj. 令人震惊的；惊人的
adj. 发人深思的；深思熟虑的

paras.en: And they’re right.
paras.zh: 他们说得没错。

paras.en: There’s nothing technophobic (技术恐惧的) about that.
paras.zh: 这么说丝毫没有技术恐惧的意味。

w.m: adj. 技术恐惧的；惧怕新技术的

paras.en: We shape our tools and then our tools shape us.
paras.zh: 我们塑造工具，然后工具又塑造我们。

paras.en: Technology is supposed to provide tools that serve human ends.
paras.zh: 技术本应提供工具，服务于人类的目的。

paras.en: But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours.
paras.zh: 但正如这个用于机器学习的验证码所表明的，如今相当一部分数字技术把人类视为（并用作）手段，去实现并非我们自己的目的。

w.m: 相当一部分；相当大比例的

paras.en: In the process, it reduces us to the status of cheery rats running on treadmills (踏车) designed by people who do not have our interests at heart.
paras.zh: 在此过程中，它使我们沦为欢快的老鼠，在踏车上奔跑，而设计这些踏车的人并不把我们的利益放在心上。

w.m: 使沦为；使陷入（较差的境地）
adj. 欢快的；兴高采烈的
把某人的利益放在心上；关心某人的利益

paras.en: So back to the frog metaphor.
paras.zh: 那么，回到青蛙的比喻。

paras.en: Are we smart enough to jump out before it’s too late?
paras.zh: 我们是否足够聪明，能在为时已晚之前跳出来？

w.m: 在为时已晚之前；趁还来得及

paras.en: You don’t even have to Google it to know the answer.
paras.zh: 你甚至不用上谷歌搜一下，就知道答案。

w.m: v. 用谷歌搜索；上网搜索

passages.name: 2025年12月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 注意力经济时代的正念与倾听
passages.genre: 议论文 · 心理与社会
passages.summary: 正念已被证明对健康有不少切实的益处，它所依据的见解是：人有能力观察体验，而不陷入其中。在注意力经济中，人类的注意力已经变成了大公司买卖的商品，而正念可以帮助我们抵御注意力经济。一些学者认为，正念也可以为他人修习；怀着慈悲心、全神贯注且不加评判地倾听他人，在这个注意力涣散的世界里是一份珍贵的礼物。

paras.en: Mindfulness has been shown to have a number of meaningful health benefits—it can help reduce anxiety and promote healing in those suffering from chronic illness.
paras.zh: 正念已被证明对健康有不少切实的益处——它能帮助慢性病患者减轻焦虑、促进康复。

paras.en: The practice is based on an insight first described in ancient Buddhist texts that human beings have the capacity to observe experience without being caught up in it.
paras.zh: 这种修习基于古代佛教典籍中最早记述的一个见解：人有能力观察体验，而不陷入其中。

paras.en: This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events.
paras.zh: 这不过是说，我们能够观察到自己产生了某种渴望、某个快乐的念头，甚至某种可怕的情绪，却不会当下就做出反应，进而放大这种感受，或让思绪一发不可收拾地陷入对往事的回想或对未来之事的预想。

w.m: 使……一发不可收拾地陷入；使……失控地陷入

paras.en: This practice of mindfulness can help calm the mind and the body as we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad.
paras.zh: 随着我们学会不以好恶或对好坏的评判去回应体验，这种正念修习能帮助身心平静下来。

paras.en: It does not make us cold or indifferent but more fully present.
paras.zh: 正念修习并不会让我们变得冷漠或无动于衷，而是让我们更全然地专注于当下。

w.m: adj. 漠不关心的；无动于衷的
adj. 专注于当下的；在场的

paras.en: One of the challenges of practicing mindfulness in our contemporary world is that there has been a profound transformation in human attention.
paras.zh: 在当今世界修习正念的挑战之一在于，人类的注意力已经发生了深刻的转变。

paras.en: The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our “attention economy” human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell.
paras.zh: 艺术家珍妮·奥德尔认为，在我们的“注意力经济”中，人类的注意力已经变成了大公司买卖的商品。

paras.en: This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment.
paras.zh: 这种经济建立在手机和社交媒体这场技术革命之上，这场革命让公司能够时时刻刻用自己的内容锁定我们的注意力。

w.h: make it possible for sb to do

paras.en: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment.
paras.zh: 大多数人使用的设备无休无止地让人从当下分心。

w.m: n. 分散注意力的事物；转移

paras.en: The result is that it can feel as though our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen.
paras.zh: 结果就是，我们可能会觉得，自己集中注意力、全然专注于当下的能力仿佛被偷走了。

paras.en: But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy and relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love.
paras.zh: 但正念可以帮助我们抵御注意力经济，细细品味那些让生活变得特别的事物，比如和所爱之人在一起。

paras.en: Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others.
paras.zh: 大多数正念研究关注的是这种修习给个人带来的益处，但一些学者断言，我们不仅可以为自己修习正念，也可以为他人修习正念。

paras.en: It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.
paras.zh: 正念能帮助我们建立更牢固、更健康的人际关系。

paras.en: The sad truth is that living in the attention economy, most of us have become bad listeners.
paras.zh: 可悲的事实是，生活在注意力经济之中，我们大多数人都已成了不善于倾听的人。

paras.en: However, just as it is possible to watch ourselves having an experience without reacting, it’s possible to watch another person have an experience without getting tied up in reactivity and judgment.
paras.zh: 然而，正如我们能够观察自己经历某种体验而不做出反应，我们也能够观察另一个人经历某种体验，而不陷入下意识的反应和评判之中。

paras.en: The gift of mindfulness is a practice of listening with compassion to others describe their experiences.
paras.zh: 正念这份礼物是这样一种修习：怀着慈悲心倾听他人讲述自己的经历。

paras.en: To give this gift means putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions.
paras.zh: 送出这份礼物，意味着收起手机、关掉社交媒体，并抛开其他常见的干扰。

w.m: n. 使人分心的事物；干扰

paras.en: It means practicing being fully present in another person’s presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.
paras.zh: 这意味着练习在他人面前全然专注于当下，全神贯注、不加评判地倾听对方，同时克制住让互动围着自己转的冲动。

w.m: 使（某事）围绕……转；使（某事）以……为中心

paras.en: If we judge the value of gifts based on their price, this gift may seem worthless, but in a distracted world, it is a precious one.
paras.zh: 如果我们根据价格来衡量礼物的价值，这份礼物也许显得一文不值；但在这个注意力涣散的世界里，它却是一份珍贵的礼物。

w.m: adj. 毫无价值的；一文不值的
adj. 注意力涣散的；分心的

passages.name: 2025年12月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 不受欢迎的建议：成因与应对
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与社会
passages.summary: 一再提出不受欢迎的建议的人，可能是出于好意，也可能是出于一种与影响他人的能力挂钩的自我价值感，借此让自己觉得有权势或能掌控局面，而他们自己未必完全意识到这一点。对这类人严厉回应，可能会带来不希望看到的结果；直截了当的拒绝也可能被对方视为威胁，甚至引发更大的冲突。关键在于既认可对方，又不过度认同；如果觉得需要，设定界限完全合理，但最好考虑到对方这样做的深层原因。

paras.en: People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help.
paras.zh: 一再提出不受欢迎的建议的人，可能是出于好意，真心想要帮忙。

w.m: adj. 不受欢迎的；不想要的
adj. 出于好意的；善意的

paras.en: Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others.
paras.zh: 另一些人这样做，则可能是出于一种与影响他人的能力挂钩的自我价值感。

paras.en: One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.
paras.zh: 一项研究发现，追求权力的倾向很强的人比倾向相反的人更有可能提出建议。

paras.en: Under the guise (外表) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control.
paras.zh: 人们可能会打着无私的幌子，受某种内驱力驱使而给你提出不受欢迎的建议，因为这样做让他们觉得自己有权势，或者能掌控局面。

w.m: adj. 不受欢迎的；不想要的
掌控（局面）；处于控制地位

paras.en: They may not be fully aware of this drive, however.
paras.zh: 不过，他们自己可能并没有完全意识到这种内驱力。

paras.en: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down.
paras.zh: 这些人还可能表现出情绪上的脆弱，而且到了成问题的程度：一下子就心烦意乱，又要过很久才能平静下来。

w.m: adj. 成问题的；有问题的
adj. 心烦意乱的；不安的

paras.en: It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations.
paras.zh: 有可能他们在童年时，情绪只有在表达得最激烈的时候才会得到认可，这促使他们对不适采取在大多数情况下都过激的反应。

w.m: 在最激烈（最响亮）的时候

paras.en: When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice.
paras.zh: 一个人为了让自己觉得更有权势而提建议时，其行为背后潜藏着焦虑，而接受建议的人往往会察觉到这种焦虑。

paras.en: It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.
paras.zh: 在这种情况下，你可能会忍不住严厉回应提建议的人，指责对方爱操纵别人，但这种做法可能会带来你不希望看到的结果。

w.m: adj. 诱人的；让人忍不住想做的
adj. 爱操纵人的；工于心计的
adj. 不希望出现的；不想要的

paras.en: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone’s feelings of self-worth, an outright (直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.
paras.zh: 如果提建议这一行为正在积极地增强某人的自我价值感，那么对方可能会把直截了当的拒绝视为威胁，进而激活其“战斗或逃跑”反应，这可能使其在寻求认可的行为上变本加厉，或者引发更大的冲突。

w.m: adj. 直截了当的；断然的
在……上变本加厉；加倍投入

paras.en: The key is to validate without over-identifying.
paras.zh: 关键在于既认可对方，又不过度认同。

paras.en: You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help.
paras.zh: 你可以让对方知道，你听到了他们的意见，也理解他们的出发点，同时又不接受这样一种可能有害的说法：没有他们的帮助，你就不可能应付得过来。

paras.en: You had better say something like, “Thanks for the idea.
paras.zh: 你最好说些类似这样的话：“谢谢你的主意。

paras.en: I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration.
paras.zh: 这件事怎么处理，我有自己的打算，不过真的很感谢你的看法，我会把它考虑在内的。

paras.en: Can I let you know when I need help in the future?”
paras.zh: 等以后我需要帮忙的时候再告诉你，可以吗？”

paras.en: If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self-regulate.
paras.zh: 如果你难以得体地设定界限，那就要优先下功夫提高自己的自我调节能力。

w.m: v. 优先考虑；优先处理

paras.en: As uncomfortable as it may make you continuously receiving unwanted advice, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely be defused much faster.
paras.zh: 尽管不断收到不受欢迎的建议可能会让你很不舒服，但如果你能以同情心回应，局面很可能会缓和得快得多。

w.m: adj. 不舒服的；不自在的
adj. 不受欢迎的；不想要的

paras.en: Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions.
paras.zh: 许多人收到不请自来的建议后，常常会因这些不受欢迎的提议而感到有压力、被冒犯，或者纯粹是心烦，尽管这通常并不是提出这类建议想要达到的结果。

w.m: adj. 预期的；想要达到的
adj. 不请自来的；未经请求的
adj. 不受欢迎的；不想要的

paras.en: Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.
paras.zh: 如果你觉得有需要，在这方面设定界限是完全合理的，而且能让你在情绪上更有安全感。

paras.en: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual’s underlying reasons for doing what they are doing, to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.
paras.zh: 设定界限时，最好考虑到对方这样做的深层原因，以免引发不必要的冲突、带来更多压力。

passages.name: 2025年12月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 团结的多个侧面与真正内涵
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与伦理
passages.summary: 人类相互依存，离不开他人，这一点从我们把自己组织成各种集体的方式中显而易见。词典对团结最简单的定义是一群人之间起凝聚作用的观点、情感、目的或利益；在日益多元的社会中，团结呈现出复杂多面的特点：它的一个侧面与社群主义原则十分契合，为维护群体的统一而牺牲个性和自主性；团结也被视为对极端强调个人主义和选择自由的一种反应。尽管团结有诸多侧面，社会理论家一直把它视为带来社会秩序与进步的关键因素，认为真正的团结不仅仅是基于共同利益的浅层关系；文章指出，团结是包容的、非强制的纽带，体现为彼此支持、相互维护，并因关心他人的福祉或公共利益而更加牢固。

paras.en: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others.
paras.zh: 作为相互依存的生命，我们离开他人便无法茁壮成长。

w.m: v. 茁壮成长；兴旺发达

paras.en: We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about.
paras.zh: 我们喜欢和这样的人共事：志同道合、与我们有共同利益，或者同样信奉我们认真对待的某项事业。

paras.en: This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families.
paras.zh: 从我们把自己组织成国家、地区、社区、组织、家庭等各种集体的方式中，这一点显而易见。

w.m: adj. 明显的；显而易见的

paras.en: Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs?
paras.zh: 你所属的群体有强烈的集体意识或共同信念吗？

paras.en: Is there interdependence among its members?
paras.zh: 群体成员之间相互依存吗？

paras.en: Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence?
paras.zh: 你认为这个群体是你人生的重要组成部分吗？

paras.en: If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.
paras.zh: 如果你的回答是肯定的，那么你正在体验一种微缩版的团结。

paras.en: What is solidarity?
paras.zh: 什么是团结？

paras.en: Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: “… a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people.”
paras.zh: 词典对它最简单的定义是：“……一群人之间起凝聚作用的观点、情感、目的或利益。”

w.m: adj. 起凝聚作用的；使统一的

paras.en: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.
paras.zh: 在我们所生活的这个日益多元的社会中，团结呈现出复杂而多面的特点，因为它在一个个独特的个体之间形成相互依存的纽带，而这些个体生活在快速变化的环境中，在复杂的劳动分工中工作。

w.m: adj. 独特的；独一无二的

paras.en: One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism (社群主义).
paras.zh: 团结的一个侧面与社群主义的原则十分契合。

paras.en: In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good.
paras.zh: 在这种情形下，个人为了服务于公共利益而放弃自身利益。

paras.en: However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences.
paras.zh: 然而，它严格坚守社会凝聚性和排他性，这限制了个人差异与偏好的表达和践行。

paras.en: Consequently, individuality and autonomy are sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.
paras.zh: 因此，为了维护群体的统一，个性和自主性遭到了牺牲。

paras.en: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice.
paras.zh: 团结也被视为对极端强调个人主义和选择自由的一种反应。

paras.en: It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.
paras.zh: 它违背了自由主义的一种观念，即个人不受约束，把社会视为一种阻碍，妨碍他们自由地做出选择、按照对自己有利的方式行事，而不顾这些选择和行为会对他人产生什么影响。

w.m: adj. 不受约束的；不受限制的

paras.en: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society.
paras.zh: 但尽管团结有诸多侧面，社会理论家一直把它视为带来社会秩序与进步的关键因素。

paras.en: They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences.
paras.zh: 他们认为，人类社会要在变得更加多元的同时存续下去，就需要以这些差异为基础，形成更多新的纽带。

paras.en: In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests.
paras.zh: 鉴于此，他们认为真正的团结不仅仅是基于共同利益的浅层关系。

paras.en: Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self.
paras.zh: 团结并不只是策略性算计的产物，即盘算它能给自己带来多少好处。

paras.en: It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle.
paras.zh: 它不是建立在“你我联手对抗全世界”这一原则之上的排他性群体。

w.m: adj. 你我联手对抗全世界的

paras.en: Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced.
paras.zh: 相反，它是包容的，也不是强制的。

w.m: adj. 包容的；包括一切的

paras.en: Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other—in recognition that one’s fate is in the fate of the other.
paras.zh: 出于团结而行动，意味着彼此支持、相互维护，因为认识到一个人的命运就寓于他人的命运之中。

paras.en: It is a bond characterized by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good.
paras.zh: 它是一种以合作实践为特征的纽带，又因关心他人的福祉或公共利益而更加牢固。

paras.en: It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.
paras.zh: 它为保护人的尊严而斗争，倾听最弱势群体的呼声，并据此采取行动。

w.m: adj. 弱势的；易受伤害的

passages.name: 2025年12月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 直面种族不公，追求真正公平
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与教育
passages.summary: 马丁·路德·金曾说，手无寸铁的真理和无条件的爱将在现实中拥有最终的决定权。作者指出，五十多年后，美国社会仍难以分清真相与幻想，争取公平的斗争是诸多重要讨论的核心，而不公已经造成了骇人的后果；我们有责任帮助学生把美国历史与时事联系起来，并为他们提供应对不公和偏见的工具。作者呼吁，尽管分裂根深蒂固，我们也应正面应对共同的问题，正视种族不公，携手打破现状，建设一个更包容的国家。

paras.en: During his acceptance speech for the Nobel Peace Prize, Martin Luther King Jr. said, “I believe that unarmed truth and unconditional love will have the final word in reality.”
paras.zh: 马丁·路德·金在诺贝尔和平奖的获奖演说中说：“我相信，手无寸铁的真理和无条件的爱，将在现实中拥有最终的决定权。”

w.m: adj. 手无寸铁的；不带武器的
拥有最终决定权；说了算

paras.en: More than five decades later, our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy, fact from fiction.
paras.zh: 五十多年过去了，我们的社会仍难以把真相与幻想、事实与虚构区分开来。

paras.en: From disputes over climate change to debates about how slavery is taught, America is at a crossroads.
paras.zh: 从围绕气候变化的争论，到关于如何讲授奴隶制的辩论，美国正处在十字路口。

w.m: 处在十字路口；面临抉择

paras.en: And the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations.
paras.zh: 而在这些至关重要的讨论中，争取公平的斗争处于核心位置。

paras.en: Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences.
paras.zh: 一项又一项研究表明，不公已经造成了骇人的后果。

w.m: adj. 骇人的；令人震惊的

paras.en: A 2020 report by Citi indicated that “Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90–$113 billion” if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.
paras.zh: 花旗集团2020年的一份报告指出，如果过去二十年里与高等教育相关的公平问题得到充分解决，“黑人学生本可以使其终生收入增加900亿至1130亿美元”。

paras.en: This statistic represents a flood of issues we’ve failed to confront as a nation.
paras.zh: 这一统计数据反映出大量问题，而作为一个国家，我们一直未能正视这些问题。

paras.en: It also highlights one truth: We’re missing out on valuable opportunities to bridge the differences that divide us.
paras.zh: 它还凸显了一个事实：我们正在错失弥合分歧的宝贵机会，而这些分歧使我们彼此分裂。

paras.en: However, by honoring King’s legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.
paras.zh: 然而，通过弘扬金的精神遗产，我们可以让国家重新走上通往真正公平的道路。

w.m: v. 尊崇；弘扬（遗产、精神）

paras.en: Students—and adults for that matter—simply cannot understand the conflicts we have today without understanding what caused them in the first place.
paras.zh: 学生——其实成年人也一样——如果不了解我们今天面临的种种冲突最初因何而起，就根本无法理解这些冲突。

w.m: （补充说明）其实……也一样；就此而言
adv. 根本；简直（加强否定）

paras.en: That means we have a responsibility to help them make connections between US history and current events.
paras.zh: 这意味着，我们有责任帮助他们把美国历史与时事联系起来。

w.m: 把……联系起来；在……之间建立联系

paras.en: It also means giving them the tools they need to address inequity and bias in their own lives.
paras.zh: 这也意味着，要为他们提供所需的工具，用来应对他们自己生活中的不公和偏见。

paras.en: Adherence to these principles, along with a commitment to truthful dialogue, can help every student better appreciate how far we’ve come and more clearly see the roads we have yet to travel.
paras.zh: 恪守这些原则，再加上坚持坦诚的对话，能帮助每个学生更好地认识到我们已经走了多远，并更清楚地看到我们还有哪些路要走。

w.m: 我们已经走了多远（取得了多大进展）

paras.en: With more truthful analysis of the need for more qualified, diverse educators, we can improve our recruiting, training, and retention strategies for schools across the country.
paras.zh: 通过更实事求是地分析对更多合格、多元化教育工作者的需求，我们就能改进全国各地学校的招聘、培训和留任策略。

w.m: adj. 实事求是的；如实的

paras.en: Unfortunately, our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，我们之间根深蒂固的分裂正在延缓这些进步。

w.m: adv. 遗憾的是；不幸的是

paras.en: A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is “more divided than ever before”.
paras.zh: 最近的一项调查发现，77%的美国人认为，这个国家“比以往任何时候都更加分裂”。

paras.en: But reports of increased polarization shouldn’t persuade us to look away from one another.
paras.zh: 但有关两极分化加剧的报道，不应让我们对彼此视而不见。

w.m: 把目光从……移开；对……视而不见

paras.en: Instead, they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on.
paras.zh: 相反，这些报道应当促使我们正面应对共同面临的问题。

paras.en: We are not, as some would suggest, living in a “post-racial society”.
paras.zh: 我们并不像有些人所说的那样，生活在“后种族社会”中。

w.m: adj. 后种族的（指种族问题已不复存在的）

paras.en: We simply cannot afford to keep our heads buried in the sand when it comes to racial inequity.
paras.zh: 在种族不公问题上，我们根本不能再把头埋在沙子里。

w.m: adv. 根本；简直（加强否定）
不能；承受不起（做某事的后果）

w.h: bury one's head in the sand
w.m: 把头埋在沙子里；逃避现实

paras.en: Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias, and how these social diseases impact the ways we treat one another, injustice will continue to haunt us.
paras.zh: 除非我们坦诚面对不宽容、偏见，以及这些社会弊病如何影响我们相互对待的方式，否则不公不义将继续困扰我们。

paras.en: But our children and our grandchildren deserve better.
paras.zh: 但我们的子女和孙辈理应享有更好的境遇。

w.m: 理应得到更好的（对待、境遇）

paras.en: On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let’s commit to working together to disrupt the status quo.
paras.zh: 在这个马丁·路德·金纪念日以及往后的日子里，让我们致力于携手合作，打破现状。

paras.en: Let’s continue to build a better, more inclusive nation—in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., “a society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience.”
paras.zh: 让我们继续建设一个更美好、更包容的国家——用马丁·路德·金的话来说，就是“一个与自身和平相处的社会，一个能够问心无愧的社会”。

passages.name: 2025年12月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 追求成功不应以失去朋友为代价
passages.genre: 议论文 · 友谊与成功
passages.summary: 作者指出，人们急于追求个人成功，往往在途中失去朋友，而这已成了常态；我们中许多人已沦为个人主义文化的牺牲品，整个社会颂扬个人成就，对“在通往成功的路上失去朋友”这一观念推崇备至。作者认为，我们必须重新学会珍视人际联系，不能对失去友谊心安理得，因为友谊是我们的依靠。成功可以追求，但单打独斗并不会让人更成功；一路上有人支持你、爱你，远比任何最终结果都重要。

paras.en: Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a shoulder to cry on, a reliable soul to confide in.
paras.zh: 许多人把友谊视为一条安抚毯：一副可以靠着哭泣的肩膀，一个可以倾诉心事的可靠之人。

w.m: 安抚毯；给人安全感的东西
可以靠着哭泣的肩膀；可以倾诉的人

paras.en: However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.
paras.zh: 然而，由于急于追求个人成功，我们往往在途中失去朋友，而这已成为这个过程的一部分。

paras.en: The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life is an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships.
paras.zh: 在追求稳定友谊的过程中，伴随日常生活而来的混乱和无休无止的动荡是一个来势汹汹的障碍。

w.m: adj. 无休止的；没完没了的
adj. 来势汹汹的；强劲的

paras.en: As students, we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones.
paras.zh: 作为学生，我们以此为借口，对失去那些曾经以为是挚爱的人满不在乎。

w.m: 对……满不在乎；对……不予理会

paras.en: Instead of viewing our lives as a race, where everyone is on their own path to some form of success, we must relearn to value the connections we make along the track.
paras.zh: 我们不应把人生视为一场赛跑——在这场赛跑中，人人都在各自的道路上奔向某种形式的成功——而必须重新学会珍视我们在跑道上建立的人际联系。

paras.en: We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.
paras.zh: 我们必须重新评估极端的个人自由带来的危害。

paras.en: Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective.
paras.zh: 极端个人主义把个人的自由置于集体之上。

paras.en: It argues, for instance, that universal healthcare, an example of collectivism, threatens the dream of many Americans.
paras.zh: 例如，它认为全民医保（集体主义的一个例子）威胁着许多美国人的梦想。

w.m: 全民医保；全民医疗保健

paras.en: Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture.
paras.zh: 我们中的许多人已经沦为个人主义文化的牺牲品。

w.m: 沦为……的牺牲品；成为……的受害者

paras.en: Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.
paras.zh: 社会往往颂扬个人成就并加以称许，依据的是这样一种假设：获胜或成功是比别人更努力的结果。

paras.en: As a society, we idolize the concept of “losing friends on the road to success”.
paras.zh: 我们整个社会都对“在通往成功的路上失去朋友”这一观念推崇备至。

paras.en: I remember hearing in high school, “Don’t worry about losing friendships; just focus on study and getting into college.
paras.zh: 我记得上高中时听人说过：“别为失去友谊而担心，只管专心学习、考上大学。

paras.en: That’s all that will matter in the long run,” a sentiment that is not unique to my experience.
paras.zh: 从长远来看，只有这些才重要。”这样的看法并非只有我一个人遇到过。

paras.en: It’s preached in many success stories, and it’s embedded in the way we see growth.
paras.zh: 许多成功故事都在宣扬这种看法，它也深植于我们看待成长的方式之中。

paras.en: Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent about the inevitable end of losing friends.
paras.zh: 励志演说家会鼓动听众对失去朋友这一必然结局心安理得。

w.m: 对……心安理得；对……满不在乎
adj. 不可避免的；必然的

paras.en: Spend too much time with friends?
paras.zh: 和朋友待在一起的时间太多了？

paras.en: You’re losing time better utilized on your achievements.
paras.zh: 你正在失去本可以更好地用来取得成就的时间。

paras.en: Invest time in your relationships?
paras.zh: 把时间投入到人际关系上？

paras.en: Invest time in your work instead.
paras.zh: 还是把时间投入到工作上吧。

paras.en: This constant need to succeed has blinded us from seeing through the whirlwind of change that accompanies our everyday lives.
paras.zh: 这种时刻都要成功的需求蒙蔽了我们的双眼，让我们看不透伴随日常生活而来的旋风般的变化。

w.m: adj. 持续不断的；始终存在的
n. 旋风；旋风般的一连串事物

paras.en: We are expected to tangibly succeed, earn awards, get higher positions, earn better grades.
paras.zh: 人们期望我们取得实实在在的成功，赢得奖项，获得更高的职位，取得更好的成绩。

w.m: adv. 实实在在地；明显地

paras.en: In order to succeed, we lose friends, and that has sadly become normalized.
paras.zh: 为了成功，我们失去朋友，而可悲的是，这已经成了常态。

w.m: adv. 可悲的是；遗憾的是
v. 使常态化；使被视为正常

paras.en: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors.
paras.zh: 我们不能对失去友谊心安理得，因为友谊是我们的依靠。

w.m: 对……心安理得；对……满不在乎
n. 依靠；精神支柱（本义为“锚”）

paras.en: Yes, pursue success.
paras.zh: 没错，去追求成功吧。

paras.en: Challenge yourself.
paras.zh: 挑战自我。

paras.en: Push limits.
paras.zh: 突破极限。

paras.en: But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.
paras.zh: 但与所有那些自封的成功学专家的说法相反，单打独斗并不会让你比借助他人帮助取得成功的人更成功，也丝毫不会让你比这样的人更优秀。

paras.en: Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else.
paras.zh: 要下功夫培养健康的人际关系，即使日程繁忙得似乎没给其他任何人留下时间，也要维系好这些关系。

paras.en: Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result.
paras.zh: 尽管我们可能正生活在一个珍视独立追求成就的社会中，但一路上有人支持你、爱你，远比任何最终结果都重要。

passages.name: 2025年6月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 家庭假政策与性别工资差距的停滞
passages.genre: 说明文 · 社会与经济
passages.summary: 20世纪80年代，美国的性别工资差距每年缩小约1个百分点，但这一趋势没有延续下去。哈佛大学学者的一项新研究认为，这种停滞可以归因于州和联邦层面推行家庭假政策：利用这些政策的主要是女性，而重返职场的女性工资增长速度低于男性。文章指出，在许多地方，女性有了孩子后薪水就开始落后于男性同行，原因包括女性承担了更多家中的无偿劳动、母亲在加薪和升职时被略过，以及离开职场的时间会让女性落后。作者还认为，即使没有休假政策，通往工资平等之路也可能陷入停滞，因为哺乳等生理因素仍会迫使女性暂停工作。

paras.en: Women have historically been paid less.
paras.zh: 历史上，女性的工资一直较低。

w.m: adv. 历史上；从历史上看
v. 付给（某人）工资；付酬

paras.en: But in the US in the 1980s, they began to catch up—fast.
paras.zh: 但在20世纪80年代的美国，女性开始迎头赶上，而且速度很快。

paras.en: During that decade, the gender pay gap closed by about one percentage point a year.
paras.zh: 在那十年间，性别工资差距每年缩小约1个百分点。

paras.en: Had that trend continued, the gender wage gap would have been closed by 2017.
paras.zh: 假如这一趋势一直延续下去，性别工资差距到2017年就已经消除了。

w.m: （省略 if 的虚拟倒装）假如……当时（做了）
（与过去事实相反的虚拟）本会……；就已经……

paras.en: But the trend didn’t continue, and the gap remains yawning.
paras.zh: 但这一趋势并没有延续下去，差距至今依然悬殊。

paras.en: According to a new study from academics at Harvard, the stagnation can be put down, perhaps counterintuitively, to the introduction of state and federal family leave policies.
paras.zh: 据哈佛大学学者的一项新研究，这种停滞可以归因于州和联邦层面推行家庭假政策，这一点或许有违直觉。

w.m: adv. 有违直觉地；出人意料地
家庭假（为生育、照顾家人等而休的假）

paras.en: The academics argue that during the 1990s, as governments began to introduce leave policies, it was mainly women who took advantage of them.
paras.zh: 这些学者认为，在20世纪90年代，随着各级政府开始推行休假政策，利用这些政策的主要是女性。

paras.en: Though the leave policies might have helped those women to stay in the workplace—instead of dropping out to have families—those who returned saw their wages had increased at lower rates than the men’s.
paras.zh: 尽管休假政策或许帮助了这些女性留在职场，而不是离职去生儿育女，但重返职场的女性发现，自己工资的增长速度低于男性。

paras.en: After family leave was introduced in the US, in fact, the rate of gender wage convergence fell to just 0.03 percentage points per year, and has remained there ever since.
paras.zh: 事实上，美国推行家庭假之后，性别工资趋同的速度降到了每年仅0.03个百分点，此后一直停留在这一水平。

paras.en: Those monitoring the process towards salary equity at work have long watched as progress slowed in many countries around the world.
paras.zh: 长期以来，追踪职场薪酬公平进程的人眼看着世界上许多国家的进展放缓。

paras.en: In fact, that progress began to reverse during the pandemic (大流行病).
paras.zh: 事实上，在疫情期间，这一进展开始倒退。

paras.en: The gender pay gap is one of the most outstanding examples of that lack of parity (平等), and still exists just about everywhere.
paras.zh: 性别工资差距是这种不平等最突出的例子之一，而且几乎在所有地方都依然存在。

paras.en: The motherhood penalty has become a shorthand for describing why: In many places, especially rich countries, women earn the same as men until they reach their childbearing years.
paras.zh: 母职惩罚已经成为描述其中原因的简略说法：在许多地方，尤其是富裕国家，女性在进入育龄期之前，挣得和男性一样多。

w.m: 母职惩罚（女性因生育而在收入等方面受到的不利影响）

paras.en: Women who have children begin to see their salaries slip behind their male counterparts’.
paras.zh: 有了孩子的女性开始眼看着自己的薪水落后于男性同行。

w.m: n. 同行；地位相当的人

paras.en: Part of this is because women take on more of the unpaid labor at home, which can eat into time available for work and energy for career advancement.
paras.zh: 部分原因在于，女性在家中承担着更多的无偿劳动，这可能会挤占她们可用于工作的时间和谋求职业发展的精力。

paras.en: But it’s also because mothers are passed over for raises and promotion, and because time out of the workplace sets women back, even if that time is taken voluntarily, and supported by company or government policy.
paras.zh: 但这也是因为，母亲们在加薪和升职时会被略过，还因为离开职场的那段时间会让女性落后，即使这段时间是她们自愿休的，并且得到了公司或政府政策的支持。

w.m: （加薪、升职时）被略过；未被考虑

paras.en: What would have happened if leave policies hadn’t been introduced?
paras.zh: 如果当初没有推行休假政策，情况又会怎样呢？

w.h: what would have happened if…had not
w.m: （对过去的虚拟）假如当初没有……，会怎样

paras.en: The study doesn’t go into that question, other than to say that if the 1980s trend had continued, we would have been at parity by now.
paras.zh: 这项研究没有深入探讨这个问题，只是说，如果20世纪80年代的那种趋势延续下去，我们现在就已经实现平等了。

w.m: 处于平等状态；实现平等

paras.en: It’s possible, however, that the journey towards wage parity would have stalled either way.
paras.zh: 不过，通往工资平等之路也有可能无论如何都会陷入停滞。

paras.en: If women’s gains in the 1980s were made through the erasure of things like bias, once those less uncontrollable problems had been addressed, there would still have been an issue with women—who are the ones to bear children and take care of them in the early weeks because of biological factors like the ability to breastfeed, forcing them to take breaks, whether or not those breaks were mandated.
paras.zh: 如果说女性在20世纪80年代取得的进步是通过消除偏见之类的因素实现的，那么一旦这些不那么难以控制的问题得到解决，女性仍会面临一个问题：由于哺乳能力等生理因素，生孩子并在最初几周照顾孩子的都是女性，这迫使她们暂停工作，无论这种暂停是不是强制规定的。

w.m: adj. 难以控制的；无法控制的
v. 强制规定；（正式）要求

passages.name: 2025年6月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 势利眼与我们的事业焦虑
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与心理
passages.summary: 我们担忧自己的事业，部分是因为钱，也有心理方面的原因：世上满是势利眼，他们凭我们身上相对较小的一部分就得出僵化的结论，如今只在乎我们以何为生，这让我们燃起了想要有所成就、给人留下深刻印象的迫切冲动。作者认为，我们对豪车、光鲜的工作和豪宅的兴趣，很大一部分与物质主义无关，而与对尊重和敬重的渴望有关；势利的根源在于，在如何判断谁有价值这件事上缺乏想象力和自信。应对势利的真正办法，是坚持认为更好或更差的人总是存在于意想不到的地方；由于我们不善于判断他人的价值，我们的根本职责仍然是对几乎每一个遇到的人都友善、厚道，怀有好奇心和想象力。

paras.en: Why are we so worried about our careers?
paras.zh: 我们为什么如此担忧自己的事业？

paras.en: Partly it’s to do with money, but there’s a psychological aspect to our fears as well.
paras.zh: 这在一定程度上与钱有关，但我们的恐惧也有心理方面的因素。

w.m: adv. 部分地；在一定程度上

paras.en: We worry because we suspect—not wrongly—that the world is full of a frightening sort of person ready to judge us ruthlessly and swiftly: a person we can call a snob.
paras.zh: 我们之所以担忧，是因为我们怀疑世上满是一种可怕的人，他们随时准备无情而迅速地评判我们——这种怀疑并没有错；这种人，我们可以称之为“势利眼”。

w.m: adj. 可怕的；令人恐惧的

paras.en: A snob is anyone who takes a relatively small part of us and uses it to come to a rigid conclusion about how much of their attention we deserve.
paras.zh: 凡是抓住我们身上相对较小的一部分，并据此得出僵化的结论、判定我们值得他们给予多少关注的人，都是势利眼。

paras.en: In the past, that might be our ancestry and royal connections.
paras.zh: 在过去，这一部分可能是我们的家世以及与王室的关系。

w.m: n. 关系；（有权势的）亲友关系

paras.en: Nowadays, the snob cares about one thing only: what we do for a living.
paras.zh: 如今，势利眼只在乎一件事：我们靠什么谋生。

paras.en: This explains why the first question we will be asked in any new social context is “What do you do?” and according to how we answer, snobs will either welcome us with broad smiles, or leave us in the cold.
paras.zh: 这就解释了为什么在任何新的社交场合，别人问我们的第一个问题都会是“你是做什么的？”，而势利眼会根据我们的回答，要么笑容满面地欢迎我们，要么冷落我们。

w.m: 冷落某人；把某人晾在一边

paras.en: And that is why we are fired up by such a desperate urge to achieve and impress.
paras.zh: 这也就是为什么我们心中会燃起如此迫切的冲动，想要有所成就、给人留下深刻印象。

w.m: adj. 迫切的；极度渴望的
v. 有所成就；实现目标
v. 给人留下深刻印象；使钦佩

paras.en: Sometimes our behaviour is mistaken for greed and vanity, but it is more than this.
paras.zh: 有时，我们的行为会被误认为是贪婪和虚荣，但它不止于此。

paras.en: A lot of our interest in fancy cars, jobs and houses has nothing to do with materialism.
paras.zh: 我们对豪车、光鲜的工作和豪宅的兴趣，很大一部分与物质主义毫无关系。

w.m: n. 物质主义；实利主义

paras.en: It has to do with a hunger for the respect and esteem that is only available in our societies through the acquisition of material goods.
paras.zh: 它与对尊重和敬重的渴望有关，而在我们的社会中，只有通过获取物质财物才能赢得这种尊重和敬重。

w.m: adj. 可获得的；可得到的

paras.en: It isn’t the goods themselves we seek; it is the love we stand to gain through our possession of them.
paras.zh: 我们追求的不是财物本身，而是通过拥有财物有望赢得的爱。

paras.en: The next time we see someone driving a Ferrari, we shouldn’t condemn them for their greed; we should pity them for the intensity of their need for love from the world.
paras.zh: 下次再看到有人开着法拉利，我们不应该谴责他们贪婪，而应该同情他们，因为他们如此强烈地需要得到世人的爱。

paras.en: At the root of snobbery is a lack of imagination and confidence about how to decide who in the world is valuable.
paras.zh: 势利的根源在于，在如何判断世上谁有价值这件事上，缺乏想象力和自信。

paras.en: The snobs are brutally misguided and slavish in their beliefs about how the superior individuals can be identified.
paras.zh: 在怎样才能识别出优秀的人这一问题上，势利眼的观念错得离谱，而且一味盲从。

w.m: adj. 误入歧途的；（判断）错误的
adj. 盲从的；毫无主见的

paras.en: For snobs, it is the already acclaimed and already successful who are the only ones worthy of respect.
paras.zh: 在势利眼看来，只有那些已经备受赞誉、已经取得成功的人，才值得尊重。

w.m: adj. 备受赞誉的；受到称赞的

paras.en: There is no room in their timid, regimented minds to imagine that someone might be clever, kind or good—and yet somehow have been overlooked entirely by society, their qualities lying hidden beneath an unfamiliar veil and having as yet discovered no obvious outlet.
paras.zh: 他们胆怯而刻板的头脑里容不下这样的想象：某个人可能聪明、友善或品行端正，却不知为何被社会完全忽视了，其优点隐藏在一层陌生的面纱之下，至今尚未找到明显的施展途径。

w.m: adj. 刻板划一的；受严格控制的
adv. 不知为何；由于某种原因

paras.en: The true answer to snobbery is not to say that there is no such thing as a better or worse person, but to insist that better or worse exist in constantly unexpected places and carry none of the outward signs of distinction.
paras.zh: 应对势利的真正办法，不是说世上根本没有更好或更差的人，而是坚持认为，更好或更差的人总是存在于意想不到的地方，而且身上没有任何显赫的外在标志。

w.m: 对……的应对办法；……的解决办法
根本没有……这样的人或事
adj. 意想不到的；出人意料的

paras.en: And because we are such poor judges of the worth of others, our ultimate duty remains to be kind, good, curious and imaginative about pretty much everyone who ever crosses our path.
paras.zh: 而且，由于我们如此不善于判断他人的价值，我们的根本职责仍然是：对几乎每一个我们遇到过的人都友善、厚道，对他们怀有好奇心和想象力。

w.m: adj. 厚道的；善待他人的
与某人相遇；被某人碰到

passages.name: 2025年6月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 政府应把公民幸福放在首位
passages.genre: 议论文 · 经济与社会
passages.summary: 作者认为，GDP增长并不是衡量一个国家表现如何的好指标，也不应成为政府的首要目标；可持续的经济是达到目的的手段，而不是目的本身。有人担心幸福如何才能衡量，但作者认为，政府的义务在于创造促进富足的条件。哲学家朱利安·巴吉尼主张关注不依赖GDP增长的“真正的财富”，作者却认为，就政府能够而且应当为公民做的事情而言，这一主张把标准定得太低，例如并不清楚它要如何治理心理疾病的流行。作者指出，要求政府把公民的“幸福”作为最高优先事项，就是要求政府把公民视为目的本身。

paras.en: GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing, and should not be the primary goal of governments.
paras.zh: GDP增长并不是衡量一个国家表现如何的好指标，也不应成为政府的首要目标。

paras.en: Unlimited growth is not sustainable and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models.
paras.zh: 无限的增长是不可持续的，经济学思想正在转向这样一种观点：我们应当在经济模式中追求可持续性。

paras.en: But while a sustainable economy is vital to our future, it is a means to an end, not an end in itself.
paras.zh: 但是，可持续的经济虽然对我们的未来至关重要，却是达到目的的手段，而不是目的本身。

paras.en: The idea that governments should focus on happiness has its critics.
paras.zh: 认为政府应当关注幸福的观点有其批评者。

paras.en: There are concerns about how happiness can be measured.
paras.zh: 有人担心幸福如何才能衡量。

paras.en: Is happiness not a fleeting and subjective psychological state?
paras.zh: 幸福难道不是一种转瞬即逝的主观心理状态吗？

w.m: adj. 转瞬即逝的；短暂的

paras.en: Don’t different people experience different levels of happiness?
paras.zh: 不同的人难道不会感受到不同程度的幸福吗？

paras.en: Even on the broadest interpretation of “happiness” as prosperity or “life satisfaction”, people want different things.
paras.zh: 即便对“幸福”作最宽泛的解读，将其理解为富足或“生活满意度”，人们想要的东西也各不相同。

paras.en: Of course, governments cannot impose life satisfaction on citizens.
paras.zh: 当然，政府无法把生活满意度强加给公民。

paras.en: But our happiness relies on collaborative efforts as a society.
paras.zh: 但我们的幸福有赖于整个社会的协作努力。

paras.en: A government’s obligation lies in creating conditions that promote prosperity.
paras.zh: 政府的义务在于创造促进富足的条件。

paras.en: And there is good reason to suppose that such conditions exist, are globally applicable, and are discoverable through research.
paras.zh: 而且，有充分的理由认为，这样的条件是存在的，在全球都适用，并且可以通过研究发现。

w.h: there is good reason to do

paras.en: In a recently published article, philosopher Julian Baggini suggests we should focus on “real wealth” for citizens, which does not depend on GDP growth.
paras.zh: 在最近发表的一篇文章中，哲学家朱利安·巴吉尼提出，我们应该关注公民的“真正的财富”，这种财富并不依赖于GDP增长。

paras.en: Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access, things that enable them to live well.
paras.zh: 关键在于使用权：人们并不需要拥有那些能让自己过上好生活的东西，而是需要能够使用它们。

w.m: n. 使用权；获取途径；v. 使用；获取
adj. 关键的；非常重要的

paras.en: Technological advances and changes in social behavior enable us to make more efficient use of the assets that we already have.
paras.zh: 技术进步和社会行为的变化，让我们能够更高效地利用已有的资产。

w.m: n. 资产；有价值的东西

paras.en: And focusing on access to the resources people need to live better lives could help reduce inequality.
paras.zh: 而且，关注人们对过上更好生活所需资源的使用权，或许有助于减少不平等。

w.m: 对……的使用权；获取……的途径

paras.en: As far as it goes, this has much in common with proposals tabled by “happiness” advocates.
paras.zh: 就其本身而言，这一主张与“幸福”倡导者提出的建议有很多共同之处。

w.m: 就其本身而言；在一定限度内

paras.en: But it sets the bar far too low for what governments can and should be doing for their citizens.
paras.zh: 但就政府能够而且应当为公民做的事情而言，它把标准定得实在太低了。

paras.en: For example, it’s not clear how a “real wealth” economy would remedy the epidemic of mental ill-health that plagues our society.
paras.zh: 例如，“真正的财富”经济要如何治理困扰我们社会的心理疾病流行问题，这一点并不清楚。

w.m: 心理疾病；心理健康不佳

paras.en: In Western countries, at least, poor mental health is more detrimental to wellbeing than poverty.
paras.zh: 至少在西方国家，心理健康状况不佳对福祉的危害比贫穷更大。

paras.en: Over and above a vastly improved provision of therapeutic mental healthcare, there are preventative measures for improving mental health that governments could and should adopt.
paras.zh: 除了要大幅改进治疗性心理保健服务的供给，政府还可以而且应当采取一些改善心理健康的预防措施。

w.m: n. 医疗保健；保健服务

paras.en: The WHO recommends establishing institutions that facilitate community participation, and educational programs and interventions that provide skills for promoting mental wellbeing.
paras.zh: 世界卫生组织建议设立促进社区参与的机构，并推行教育项目和干预措施，提供增进心理福祉的技能。

paras.en: It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified.
paras.zh: 然而，很能说明问题的是，世界卫生组织觉得有必要诉诸改善心理健康带来的经济效益，以说服各国政府相信，采取所提议措施的成本是合理的。

w.m: adj. 合理的；有正当理由的

paras.en: As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens’ continued productivity.
paras.zh: 只要政府以经济为优先事项，就只需确保公民持续具有生产力，而不必更进一步。

w.m: n. 优先事项；首要任务

paras.en: To demand that governments set the “happiness” of citizens as their highest priority is to demand that they view citizens as ends in themselves.
paras.zh: 要求政府把公民的“幸福”作为最高优先事项，就是要求政府把公民视为目的本身。

passages.name: 2025年6月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 用模拟学习推动组织变革
passages.genre: 议论文 · 管理与培训
passages.summary: 组织变革要取得成功，需要员工队伍不仅不抗拒变革，而且欣然接受变革，但讲座、培训项目和研讨会很少能有效触及处于变革核心的行为层面。文章认为，模拟能让参与者体验另类现实，促使他们重新思考现有的观念，可以为变革提供推动力，是最富成效的学习形式之一。不过，模拟必须让人感觉像现实一样，参与者还应立即运用所学，在学与做之间建立起顺畅的联系。

paras.en: Simulators are most often utilized within industries such as nuclear power, aviation and surgery where failure results in disastrous consequences.
paras.zh: 模拟器最常用于核电、航空和外科手术等失败会导致灾难性后果的行业。

paras.en: To maximize the value from a simulation learning experience, participants should immediately and directly apply their learning to a specific intervention within their organization.
paras.zh: 为了从模拟学习体验中获得最大价值，参与者应当立即把所学直接运用到所在组织内某项具体的干预措施中。

w.m: v. 使最大化；最大限度地获得

paras.en: Most organizations aspire to deploy significant change programs, only to find them nearly impossible to implement.
paras.zh: 大多数组织都渴望推行重大的变革计划，结果却发现这些计划几乎无法实施。

w.m: （表示出乎意料的结果）结果却

paras.en: That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision; it requires a workforce that not only doesn’t resist change, but embraces it.
paras.zh: 这在很大程度上是因为，成功的变革需要的不只是一个愿景；它还需要一支不仅不抗拒变革、而且欣然接受变革的员工队伍。

paras.en: To achieve success, an organization must build a transformation program that will allow change to be rapidly pulled across its departments and throughout its layers.
paras.zh: 要取得成功，组织必须打造一套转型计划，让变革能够被迅速拉动，遍及各个部门、贯穿各个层级。

paras.en: Regardless of the level of senior management commitment, unless key thought leaders at all levels embrace the change, the initiative will wither and die.
paras.zh: 无论高层管理者的投入程度如何，除非各个层级的关键思想领袖都欣然接受这项变革，否则这一举措终将枯萎、消亡。

w.m: 高层管理者；高级管理层

paras.en: To create this kind of widespread passion, learning leaders must expose the workforce to what could be, which will enable them to rethink their mental models, break free from their deep-rooted paradigms and embrace the opportunity to learn.
paras.zh: 要激发这种广泛的热情，学习负责人必须让员工队伍接触到种种可能，这将使他们能够重新思考自己的心智模式，摆脱根深蒂固的范式，并欣然抓住学习的机会。

w.m: 学习负责人（负责组织学习与培训的管理者）
v. 欣然抓住（机会）；欣然接受

paras.en: Allowing participants to enter a simulated environment provides them with the opportunity to experience alternative realities which can prompt them to rethink their current beliefs.
paras.zh: 让参与者进入模拟环境，就为他们提供了体验另类现实的机会，而这些现实可以促使他们重新思考自己现有的观念。

paras.en: Behavioral change is not easy for most adults.
paras.zh: 对大多数成年人来说，行为改变并非易事。

paras.en: Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative.
paras.zh: 讲座、培训项目和研讨会可以讲解转型在认知层面的要素，却很少能有效触及行为层面，而行为层面处于重大变革举措的核心。

paras.en: Further, under normal working conditions, managers rarely see the full effect of their employee development efforts.
paras.zh: 此外，在正常的工作条件下，管理者很少能看到自己培养员工的努力所产生的全部效果。

paras.en: Therefore, an intervention like a simulation can provide the stimulus for change.
paras.zh: 因此，像模拟这样的干预措施可以为变革提供推动力。

paras.en: An effective simulation can be better than experience as a learning tool because it accelerates time, compresses space, and, unlike reality, is specifically designed to maximize participant learning.
paras.zh: 作为学习工具，有效的模拟可以比实际经历更好，因为它能加快时间、压缩空间，而且与现实不同，它是专门为最大限度地促进参与者学习而设计的。

w.m: v. 最大限度地促进；使最大化

paras.en: Simulations provide an immersive learning experience where skills, processes and knowledge all can be highlighted in a way reality cannot.
paras.zh: 模拟提供了一种沉浸式学习体验，在这种体验中，技能、流程和知识都能以现实无法做到的方式得到突出展现。

paras.en: The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning.
paras.zh: 能够在不受限制、没有风险的模型中探索、试验并反复运用新知识，正是这种能力让模拟成为最富成效的学习形式之一。

w.m: adj. 不受限制的；无限的
adj. 富有成效的；多产的

paras.en: Well-designed simulations can enable individuals and groups to develop a deep level of understanding about how their decisions and intuitive responses to business stimuli affect their fellow participants and the organization as a whole.
paras.zh: 设计精良的模拟能让个人和团队形成深层次的理解，明白自己的决策以及对业务刺激因素的直觉反应会如何影响其他参与者和整个组织。

w.m: adj. 同伴的；同一群体的

paras.en: To reap the benefits, however, simulations must feel like reality.
paras.zh: 然而，要收获这些益处，模拟必须让人感觉如同现实。

paras.en: At the end of the successful simulation, participants must declare “this is us.”
paras.zh: 在一次成功的模拟结束时，参与者必须宣称：“这就是我们。”

paras.en: If they don’t, they will view the experience as a game, which can be difficult to apply on the job, or worse, irrelevant to everyday work tasks.
paras.zh: 否则，他们就会把这次体验看作一场游戏，而游戏可能很难运用到工作中，或者更糟糕的是，与日常工作任务无关。

paras.en: To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing.
paras.zh: 为了最大限度地从模拟中获益，参与者应当立即运用从这次体验中学到的东西，以便在学与做之间建立起顺畅的联系。

w.m: v. 最大限度地获得；使最大化

passages.name: 2025年6月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: “追随激情”这一职业建议的弊端
passages.genre: 议论文 · 职业与社会
passages.summary: 作者曾劝告身边的人“追随你的激情”，但作为社会学家研究了这一“激情原则”之后，才明白这条职业建议其实很成问题。作者发现，追随激情并不一定会带来成就感，却是使过度工作得以延续的最强大的文化力量之一；而且并非每个人都拥有同样的经济资源，出身富裕家庭的人更有条件追求激情，因此不营造公平的竞争环境就向所有人推崇这条道路，会促使社会经济不平等延续下去。此外，雇主也从中受益：他们更青睐满怀激情的求职者，部分原因是相信这些人会努力工作而不指望加薪。

paras.en: After earning a bachelor’s degree, I was determined to do what I love.
paras.zh: 获得学士学位后，我决心去做自己热爱的事。

paras.en: I headed straight to graduate school to investigate the social problems that fascinated me.
paras.zh: 我径直去读了研究生，探究那些令我着迷的社会问题。

paras.en: For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same.
paras.zh: 在将近十年的时间里，我对遇到的每一个人都说，他们也应该这样做。

paras.en: “Follow your passion,” I counseled.
paras.zh: “追随你的激情，”我劝道。

paras.en: “You can figure out the employment stuff later.”
paras.zh: “就业的事，你可以以后再想办法。”

paras.en: It wasn’t until I began to research this widely accepted career advice that I understood how problematic it really was.
paras.zh: 直到开始研究这条广为接受的职业建议，我才明白它其实有多大的问题。

w.m: adj. 有问题的；成问题的

paras.en: As a sociologist, I interviewed college students and professional workers to learn what it really meant to pursue their dreams, which I will refer to here as the passion principle.
paras.zh: 作为一名社会学家，我采访了大学生和专业人士，以了解追求自己的梦想究竟意味着什么，我在这里把这种追求称为“激情原则”。

paras.en: I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book.
paras.zh: 在为新书做研究时，我对这一原则有了一些发现，这些发现让我大为震惊。

paras.en: Surveys show the American public has long held the passion principle in high regard as a career decision-making priority.
paras.zh: 调查显示，长期以来，美国公众一直非常看重激情原则，把它视为职业决策时要优先考虑的因素。

w.m: n. 优先考虑的事；首要事项

paras.en: And its popularity is even stronger among those facing job instability.
paras.zh: 而在面临工作不稳定的人当中，这一原则甚至更受欢迎。

paras.en: Advocates of the passion principle found it compelling because they believed that following one’s passion can provide workers with both the motivation necessary to work hard and a place to find fulfillment.
paras.zh: 激情原则的拥护者认为它很有说服力，因为他们相信，追随自己的激情既能为劳动者提供努力工作所需的动力，又能为他们提供一个获得成就感的地方。

w.m: adj. 有说服力的；令人信服的

paras.en: Yet, what I found is that following one’s passion does not necessarily lead to fulfillment, but is one of the most powerful cultural forces perpetuating overwork.
paras.zh: 然而，我的发现是，追随自己的激情并不一定会带来成就感，却是使过度工作得以延续的最强大文化力量之一。

w.m: v. 使延续；使持续存在

paras.en: I also found that promoting the pursuit of one’s passion helps perpetuate social inequalities due to the fact that not everyone has the same economic resources to allow them to pursue their passion with ease.
paras.zh: 我还发现，提倡追求自己的激情会促使社会不平等延续下去，因为并非每个人都拥有同样的经济资源，能让自己轻松地追求激情。

w.m: v. 使延续；使持续存在

paras.en: While the passion principle is broadly popular, not everyone has the necessary resources to turn their passion into a stable, good-paying job.
paras.zh: 虽然激情原则广受欢迎，但并非每个人都拥有必要的资源，能把自己的激情变成一份稳定且薪酬不错的工作。

w.m: adj. 薪酬不错的；报酬好的

paras.en: Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime.
paras.zh: 出身富裕家庭的激情追求者更有条件一直等到自己热爱的工作出现，在此期间也不必为学生贷款发愁。

paras.en: They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent.
paras.zh: 他们也更有条件去做无薪实习，借此踏进行业的门槛，房租则由父母来付。

w.m: 更有条件（做某事）；处境更有利

w.h: get one's foot in the door
w.m: 踏进门槛；迈出入行的第一步

paras.en: And they often have access to parents’ social networks to help them find jobs.
paras.zh: 而且，他们往往能利用父母的社会关系网来帮自己找工作。

paras.en: Surveys revealed that working-class and first-generation college graduates, regardless of their career field, are more likely than their wealthier peers to end up in low-paying unskilled jobs when they pursue their passion.
paras.zh: 调查显示，无论从事哪个职业领域，工人阶级出身的大学毕业生和家中第一代大学毕业生在追求激情时，都比家境更富裕的同龄人更有可能最终从事低薪的非技术性工作。

w.m: adj. 非技术性的；无需技能的

paras.en: Colleges, workplaces and career counselors that promote the “follow your passion” path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.
paras.zh: 高校、工作单位和职业顾问若向所有人推崇“追随你的激情”这条道路，却不营造公平的竞争环境，就会促使怀有职业抱负的人之间的社会经济不平等延续下去。

w.m: n. 工作场所；工作单位
v. 使延续；使持续存在

paras.en: It’s not just well-off passion-seekers who benefit from the passion principle.
paras.zh: 从激情原则中受益的，不只是家境优渥的激情追求者。

w.m: adj. 富裕的；家境优渥的

paras.en: Employers of passionate workers do, too.
paras.zh: 雇用了满怀激情员工的雇主也同样受益。

w.m: adj. 满怀激情的；热情的
