paras.en: Potential employers showed greater interest in passionate applicants in part because they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay.
paras.zh: 潜在雇主对满怀激情的求职者表现出更大的兴趣，部分原因在于他们相信，这些求职者会努力工作，而不指望加薪。

w.m: adj. 满怀激情的；热情的

paras.en: Passionate workers even sacrifice a good salary, job stability and leisure time to work in a job they love.
paras.zh: 为了从事自己热爱的工作，满怀激情的员工甚至会牺牲不错的薪水、工作的稳定性和闲暇时间。

w.m: adj. 满怀激情的；热情的

passages.name: 2025年6月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 无故缺课：孩子和家庭面临挑战的信号
passages.genre: 议论文 · 教育与社会
passages.summary: 在美国，每六个孩子中就有一个一年缺课15天或以上，美国教育部长曾在公开信中指出，一年中无论出于何种原因缺课达到上学天数的10%，都是学业成绩低下的一个主要原因。作者作为社会科学家研究发现，家长请过假的缺课对孩子的学习几乎没有损害，而平均而言，哪怕只有一次无故缺课的孩子，学业表现也比没有无故缺课的同龄人差得多。作者认为，缺课（尤其是无故缺课）的意义主要在于它是一个信号，表明孩子及其家庭可能正面临诸多危机；学校的考勤政策最终会不成比例地惩罚正在应对校外危机的家庭，并向为这些家庭服务的学校施压。作者建议换一种做法：把无故缺课当作信号，据此把资源输送给最需要资源的孩子和家庭。

paras.en: Nationally, one in six children miss 15 or more days of school in a year.
paras.zh: 在全国范围内，每六个孩子中就有一个一年缺课15天或以上。

paras.en: Education officials have deplored all this missed instruction.
paras.zh: 教育官员一直对学生错过这么多教学深感痛惜。

paras.en: These chronically absent students suffer academically because of all the classroom instruction they miss out on.
paras.zh: 这些长期缺课的学生由于错过了那么多课堂教学，学业受到了损害。

paras.en: In 2015, the US secretary of education responded to this crisis, urging communities to support every student to attend every day and be successful in school.
paras.zh: 2015年，美国教育部长对这一危机作出回应，敦促各社区支持每一名学生天天到校、学业有成。

paras.en: His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement.
paras.zh: 他在公开信中指出，一年中缺课达到上学天数的10%，无论出于何种原因，也无论是请过假的还是无故的，都是学业成绩低下的一个主要原因。

paras.en: Worrying about whether children attend school makes sense.
paras.zh: 担心孩子有没有上学，是有道理的。

paras.en: After all, if students don’t show up, teachers can’t teach them.
paras.zh: 毕竟，学生不来上学，老师就没法教他们。

paras.en: But what if America’s attendance crisis is about much more than students missing class?
paras.zh: 但如果美国的出勤危机远不止是学生缺课的问题，那又会怎样呢？

paras.en: What if, instead, it is a reflection of family and community crises these students face—such as being ejected from the family apartment, fearing for their safety in their neighborhood or suffering an illness?
paras.zh: 要是它反映的其实是这些学生所面临的家庭和社区危机，比如被赶出家里的公寓、在自己住的街区为自身安全担忧，或是身患疾病，那又会怎样呢？

paras.en: As social scientists we investigated how excused and unexcused absences relate to children’s academic achievement.
paras.zh: 作为社会科学家，我们研究了请过假的缺课和无故缺课与孩子的学业成绩有何关系。

paras.en: We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children’s learning.
paras.zh: 我们发现，家长请过假的缺课对孩子的学习几乎没有损害。

paras.en: In fact, children with no unexcused absences—but 15 to 18 excused absences—have test scores equal to those of their peers who have no absences.
paras.zh: 事实上，没有无故缺课、但请过假缺课15至18次的孩子，考试成绩与一次课都没缺过的同龄人相同。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none.
paras.zh: 与此同时，平均而言，哪怕只有一次无故缺课的孩子，学业表现也比没有无故缺课的同龄人差得多。

paras.en: We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships.
paras.zh: 我们认为，无故缺课是一个强烈的信号，表明孩子和家庭面临着诸多挑战，包括经济上和医疗上的困难。

paras.en: Unexcused absences can be a powerful signal of how those out-of-school challenges affect children’s academic progress.
paras.zh: 无故缺课可以作为一个有力的信号，揭示那些校外挑战如何影响孩子的学业进展。

paras.en: Our evidence suggests unexcused absences are problematic, but for a different reason than people often think.
paras.zh: 我们的证据表明，无故缺课是个问题，但原因和人们常常以为的不一样。

w.m: adj. 有问题的；成问题的

paras.en: Absence from school, and especially unexcused absence, matters mainly as a signal of many crises children and their families may be facing.
paras.zh: 缺课，尤其是无故缺课，其意义主要在于它是一个信号，表明孩子及其家庭可能正面临诸多危机。

paras.en: It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction.
paras.zh: 缺课作为致使学生因错过教学而成绩较低的原因，意义则要小一些。

paras.en: How we choose to think of school absences matters for educational policy.
paras.zh: 我们选择如何看待缺课，这对教育政策来说很重要。

paras.en: School attendance policies typically hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss, regardless of whether they were excused or unexcused absences.
paras.zh: 学校的考勤政策通常要求学校和家庭为孩子缺课的天数负责，而不管这些缺课是请过假的还是无故的。

paras.en: These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically because they are missing classroom instruction.
paras.zh: 这些政策假定，无论出于何种原因缺课，都会因为孩子错过课堂教学而损害他们的学业。

paras.en: They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences.
paras.zh: 它们还假定，学校能够通过减少学生缺课来有效干预。

paras.en: We find neither to be the case.
paras.zh: 我们发现，这两种假定都不成立。

paras.en: As a result, these attendance policies end up disproportionately punishing families dealing with out-of-school crises in their lives and pressuring schools that serve them to get students to school more often.
paras.zh: 因此，这些考勤政策最终会不成比例地惩罚那些生活中正在应对校外危机的家庭，并向为这些家庭服务的学校施压，要求它们让学生更经常到校。

w.m: adv. 不成比例地；过度地

paras.en: We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.
paras.zh: 我们建议换一种做法：把无故缺课当作一个信号，据此将资源输送给最需要这些资源的孩子和家庭。

passages.name: 2024年12月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 团队教学：一所美国高中的新尝试
passages.genre: 说明文 · 教育与教学
passages.summary: 在亚利桑那州最大的学区梅萨学区，韦斯特伍德高中试行了一种名为团队教学的创新模式：几位教师共同负责一大批学生，每天早上一起为当天重点关注的学生制定个性化方案，这种模式正在向其他学校推广。学区管理人员希望借此填补人员缺口，提振教师士气，提高教师留任率；初步研究表明这次冒险可能会有回报，参与团队的教师报告的工作满意度更高，教师之间还能互相帮助改进教学。不过，这种模式并非人人适用，可能让排课变成一场噩梦，还存在如何考评教师等棘手问题，但就目前而言，它似乎正在奏效。

paras.en: One hundred thirty-five students, four teachers, one giant classroom: This is what 9th grade looks like at Westwood High School, in Mesa, Arizona’s largest school system.
paras.zh: 一百三十五名学生，四位教师，一间巨大的教室：在亚利桑那州最大的学区梅萨，韦斯特伍德高中的九年级就是这个样子。

paras.en: There, an innovative teaching model has taken hold, and is spreading to other schools in the district and beyond.
paras.zh: 在那里，一种创新教学模式已经站稳脚跟，并正在向学区内的其他学校乃至学区以外推广。

paras.en: Five years ago, faced with high teacher turnover and declining student enrollment, Westwood’s leaders decided to try something different.
paras.zh: 五年前，面对教师流动率高、学生入学人数下降的局面，韦斯特伍德高中的领导层决定尝试一些不同的做法。

w.m: n. 入学人数；注册人数

paras.en: Working with professors at Arizona State University’s teachers college, they piloted a classroom model known as team teaching, which allows teachers to dissolve the walls that separate their classes across physical or grade divides.
paras.zh: 他们与亚利桑那州立大学师范学院的教授合作，试行了一种名为“团队教学”的课堂模式，这种模式让教师能够打破隔开各自班级的墙，不论班级之间隔着的是物理空间还是年级界限。

paras.en: The teachers share large groups of students—sometimes 100 or more—and rotate between group instruction, one-on-one interventions, small study groups, and whatever the teachers as a team agree is a priority that day.
paras.zh: 这些教师共同负责一大批学生——有时有100名或更多——并在集体授课、一对一辅导、小型学习小组以及教师团队一致认为当天应优先处理的任何事项之间轮换。

w.m: n. （针对学生的）辅导干预；干预
pron. 任何……的事物；无论什么

paras.en: What looks at times like chaos is in fact a carefully orchestrated plan: Each morning, the Westwood teams meet to hammer out a personalized program for every student the team will focus on that day.
paras.zh: 有时看起来一片混乱的场面，其实是一项精心安排的计划：每天早上，韦斯特伍德高中的各个教师团队都会开会，为团队当天要重点关注的每一名学生敲定一套个性化方案。

w.m: adj. 精心安排的；精心策划的
敲定；（经反复商讨）制定出

paras.en: By giving teachers more opportunity to collaborate, Mesa’s administrators hoped to fill staffing gaps and boost teacher morale and retention.
paras.zh: 梅萨学区的管理人员希望通过给教师更多合作机会，来填补人员缺口，提振教师士气，提高教师留任率。

paras.en: Initial research suggests the gamble could pay off.
paras.zh: 初步研究表明，这次冒险可能会有回报。

paras.en: “Teachers are doing fantastic things, but it’s very rare a teacher walks into another room to see what’s happening,” said Andi Fourlis, superintendent of Mesa Public Schools.
paras.zh: “老师们在做着很了不起的事，但很少有老师会走进另一间教室，去看看那里的情况。”梅萨公立学校学区总监安迪·福尔利斯说。

paras.en: “Our profession is so slow to advance because we are working in isolation.”
paras.zh: “我们这个行业之所以进步如此缓慢，是因为我们都在单打独斗。”

paras.en: Of course, overhauling teaching approaches can’t fix all the frustrations teachers have, such as low pay, but early results from Mesa show team teaching may be helping to reverse low morale.
paras.zh: 当然，彻底改革教学方法并不能解决教师所有的烦恼，比如工资低，但梅萨学区的初步结果显示，团队教学可能正在帮助扭转士气低落的局面。

w.m: v. 彻底改革；全面检修
n. 令人烦恼的事；沮丧

paras.en: In a survey of hundreds of the district’s teachers, researchers found those who worked on teams reported greater job satisfaction, more frequent collaborations with colleagues, and more positive interactions with students.
paras.zh: 在一项针对该学区数百名教师的调查中，研究人员发现，参与团队的教师报告的工作满意度更高，与同事合作更频繁，与学生的互动也更积极。

paras.en: Another benefit of teams, teachers say, is that they can help each other improve their instruction.
paras.zh: 教师们说，团队的另一个好处是，他们可以互相帮助，改进教学。

paras.en: During one planning session, English teacher Jeff Hall shared a performance appraisal with a science teacher: Her recent lecture on something she called “the central dogma of biology” had bewildered him and their other teammates.
paras.zh: 在一次备课会上，英语教师杰夫·霍尔向一位科学教师说出了对她教学表现的评价：她最近讲了一堂课，内容是她所说的“生物学中心法则”，这堂课让他和团队里的其他同事都一头雾水。

w.m: n. 队友；团队中的同事

paras.en: “If the science is too confusing for me, can you imagine the frustration you feel as kids?” Hall said.
paras.zh: “如果这些科学内容对我来说太难懂了，那你能想象身为孩子会有多沮丧吗？”霍尔说。

w.m: adj. 令人困惑的；难懂的

paras.en: But the science teacher, he said, wouldn’t have known about the confusion on her own.
paras.zh: 但他说，单靠那位科学教师自己，她本来不会知道有这种困惑。

paras.en: The model is not for everyone.
paras.zh: 这种模式并非人人适用。

w.m: 并非人人适用；不是人人都适合

paras.en: Some teachers approached about volunteering for a team have said they prefer to work alone.
paras.zh: 一些教师在被问及是否愿意主动报名加入团队时表示，他们更喜欢独自工作。

paras.en: Team teaching can also be a scheduling nightmare, especially at schools like Westwood where only some staff work in teams.
paras.zh: 团队教学也可能让排课变成一场噩梦，尤其是在像韦斯特伍德高中这样只有部分教职员工以团队形式工作的学校。

w.m: n. 教职员工；全体员工

paras.en: There are also thorny questions like how to evaluate four teachers on the performance of 135 students.
paras.zh: 此外还有一些棘手的问题，比如如何根据135名学生的表现来评价四位教师。

paras.en: But for the time being, it seems to be working.
paras.zh: 但就目前而言，这种模式似乎正在奏效。

passages.name: 2024年12月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 人并无左脑型与右脑型之分
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科学与心理
passages.summary: 网上有数以百计的性格小测试，声称能确定一个人的大脑是左半边还是右半边占主导；这一观点经科普爱好者大加发挥，已经融入大众文化，但大脑并不是这样运作的。科学家的研究确实揭示出左右两个半球之间存在重要差异，但这些差异与性格毫无关系，也与一个人的认知策略更讲逻辑还是更有创造力毫无关系；人本来就没有左脑型和右脑型之分，神经科学界也从未支持过这种观点。这类观点的吸引力不难理解，但对这类网上小测试必须保持高度怀疑。

paras.en: There are hundreds of personality quizzes online that assert they can ascertain whether the right or left half of your brain is dominant.
paras.zh: 网上有数以百计的性格小测试，声称能够确定你的大脑是右半边还是左半边占主导。

w.m: 数以百计的；成百上千的
adj. 占主导地位的；占优势的

paras.en: Left-brained people are supposedly logical and excel at language and math while right-brained people are more imaginative, emotionally intelligent and skilled with spatial reasoning.
paras.zh: 据说，左脑型的人逻辑性强，擅长语言和数学；而右脑型的人则更富有想象力、情商更高，也更善于空间推理。

w.m: adj. 左脑型的；左脑占优势的
adj. 逻辑性强的；合乎逻辑的
adj. 右脑型的；右脑占优势的

paras.en: There’s just one problem: That’s not how brains work.
paras.zh: 问题只有一个：大脑并不是这样运作的。

paras.en: Popular science enthusiasts sort of took this idea and ran with it, and it’s become woven in popular culture now, and it’s not going away.
paras.zh: 科普爱好者们可以说是接过了这一观点并大加发挥，如今它已经融入了大众文化，而且不会消失。

w.m: （接过某个想法）大加发挥；采纳并推行

paras.en: Despite this enduring belief, there’s no such thing as being “right-brained” or “left-brained”.
paras.zh: 尽管这种观念经久不衰，但并没有“右脑型”或“左脑型”这回事。

w.m: adj. 经久不衰的；持久的
没有……这回事；根本不存在

paras.en: Whether you’re someone who tends more towards creativity or logic has nothing to do with one hemisphere of your brain being dominant over the other.
paras.zh: 你是更偏向创造力还是更偏向逻辑，与你大脑的一个半球比另一个半球占优势毫无关系。

paras.en: But the actual science of how the two halves of our brains work together is sometimes stranger than fiction.
paras.zh: 但关于我们大脑的两半如何协同工作，真实的科学有时比小说还要离奇。

paras.en: The human brain is divided into two hemispheres, the left and right.
paras.zh: 人脑分为两个半球：左半球和右半球。

paras.en: In all vertebrate (脊椎的) animals, the right hemisphere controls the left side of the body and vice versa.
paras.zh: 在所有脊椎动物中，右半球控制身体的左侧，反之亦然。

paras.en: And scientists have long known, thanks to the behaviors of patients who suffered brain injuries, that different areas of the brain do different things.
paras.zh: 而且，得益于脑损伤患者的行为表现，科学家们早就知道，大脑的不同区域负责不同的事情。

paras.en: But many scientists struggled with this idea, because the very suggestion that the left and right halves of the brain operate differently disrupted the idea that nature tends toward perfect symmetry.
paras.zh: 但许多科学家很难接受这一观点，因为单是提出大脑左右两半的运作方式不同，就打破了自然界趋向于完美对称的观念。

w.m: adj. 仅仅的；（用于强调）正是的

paras.en: Work by neuroscientists (神经科学家) has revealed the importance of different hemispheres of the brain for different activities.
paras.zh: 神经科学家的研究揭示了大脑不同半球对不同活动的重要性。

paras.en: However, their research quickly saw some misinterpretations in the general public: Some presumed creative people must be right-brained and logical people left-brained.
paras.zh: 然而，他们的研究很快就在普通大众中遭到了一些误读：有些人想当然地认为，有创造力的人一定是右脑型，而逻辑性强的人一定是左脑型。

w.m: v. 推测；想当然地认为

paras.en: It is proven that not only is personality unrelated to the different halves of the brain, but people aren’t really right- or left-brained to begin with.
paras.zh: 事实证明，性格不仅与大脑不同的两半无关，而且人其实本来就不是右脑型或左脑型的。

w.m: 不仅……而且（not only 置于句首时主谓倒装）

paras.en: The idea that we have left-dominant people and right-dominant people, and that this is related to personality, is categorically false.
paras.zh: 认为人有左脑主导型和右脑主导型之分，并且这与性格有关，这种观点是绝对错误的。

paras.en: That’s never been supported in the neuroscience community.
paras.zh: 这一观点从未得到神经科学界的支持。

paras.en: Neuroscientists don’t believe that and never have.
paras.zh: 神经科学家并不相信这一点，也从来没有相信过。

paras.en: What scientists learned is that there are really important differences between the left hemisphere and the right hemisphere.
paras.zh: 科学家们认识到的是，左半球和右半球之间存在着非常重要的差异。

paras.en: It’s just that they have nothing to do with personality or whether one’s cognitive strategy is more logical or free-spirited or creative.
paras.zh: 只不过，这些差异既与性格毫无关系，也与一个人的认知策略是更讲逻辑、更自由奔放还是更有创造力毫无关系。

w.m: adj. 逻辑性强的；讲逻辑的
adj. 自由奔放的；无拘无束的

paras.en: While researchers have shown the limitations of how the hemispheres of our brains influence our lives, it’s not difficult to understand the appeal of such ideas.
paras.zh: 虽然研究人员已经表明，大脑半球对我们生活的影响是有限的，但这类观点的吸引力并不难理解。

paras.en: People are endlessly fascinated by themselves and their friends, and the subtle differences in how people think about the world are really meaningful to them.
paras.zh: 人们对自己和朋友总是着迷不已，在他们看来，人与人看待世界的方式略有不同，这些细微差异真的很有意义。

w.m: adv. 无止境地；没完没了地
adj. 有意义的；意义重大的

paras.en: When you come up with an online quiz that tells us something about ourselves, we’re drawn to that.
paras.zh: 一旦你想出一个在线小测试，能告诉我们自己的一些情况，我们就会被它吸引。

paras.en: It’s irresistible.
paras.zh: 这让人无法抗拒。

w.m: adj. 无法抗拒的；极具诱惑力的

paras.en: But you have to take it with an enormous grain of salt.
paras.zh: 但你必须对它保持高度怀疑。

passages.name: 2024年12月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 美真的只在观看者眼中吗？
passages.genre: 议论文 · 美学与文化
passages.summary: “美在观看者眼中”这类说法很少有人质疑，作者认为，至少对这一假定提出异议或许是有益的。《认知》杂志最近发表的一项研究发现，人们对自然物体的审美评价非常一致，对人工制品的分歧则更大。作者由此提出，审美偏好似乎有客观依据，可能存在普遍的客观原则在起作用；但人们在建筑或艺术中以独特的方式运用这些原则，其方式可能并不具有普遍吸引力，因此体验多元文化及其人工制品很重要。

paras.en: Statements like “beauty is in the eye of the beholder (观看者)” are rarely questioned.
paras.zh: “美在观看者眼中”这类说法很少有人质疑。

w.h: beauty is in the eye of the beholder
w.m: 美在观看者眼中（谚语，意为审美因人而异）

paras.en: They’ve become so embedded in our consciousness that people think it’s absurd to think otherwise.
paras.zh: 这类说法已经深深植根于我们的意识之中，以至于人们认为持不同看法是荒谬的。

w.m: 持不同看法；不这样认为

paras.en: It might be useful, however, to at least push back on this assumption because people evaluate environments, situations, and people aesthetically.
paras.zh: 不过，至少对这一假定提出异议或许是有益的，因为人们会从审美角度评价环境、情境和人。

w.m: adv. 从审美角度；在审美上

paras.en: We may find that we still believe it is correct, but we may also find that there is a lot more to the situation than we suppose.
paras.zh: 我们可能会发现自己仍然认为这一假定是正确的，但也可能发现，情况远不像我们设想的那么简单。

paras.en: A recent study exploring aesthetic taste was published in Cognition.
paras.zh: 《认知》杂志最近发表了一项探究审美趣味的研究。

w.m: n. 认知（此处指期刊《认知》）

paras.en: The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.
paras.zh: 这项研究的结果表明，人们对自然物体的审美评价非常一致，但在人工制品（即人造物品）上分歧更大。

w.m: v. 意见一致；看法相同
adj. 人造的；人类制造的

paras.en: The study found that shared taste was most common for faces and natural landscapes, but least common among works of architecture and art.
paras.zh: 这项研究发现，共同的审美趣味在面孔和自然风景上最为常见，在建筑和艺术作品上则最为少见。

paras.en: The hypothesis is that the commonly pleasing features, like proportion or symmetry, are at work.
paras.zh: 对此的假设是，比例或对称之类普遍令人愉悦的特征在起作用。

w.m: adj. 令人愉悦的；赏心悦目的

paras.en: Preferences for natural scenes might be learned through life experiences.
paras.zh: 对自然景色的偏好可能是通过生活经历习得的。

paras.en: Factors like habitability, safety, and openness might be preferred as people develop.
paras.zh: 人们在成长过程中可能会偏爱宜居性、安全性和开阔性之类的因素。

paras.en: Some of the details of landscapes change, but the basics are more common, e.g., water, open spaces, and signs of care.
paras.zh: 风景的某些细节会有所变化，但基本要素更为普遍，比如水、开阔的空间以及有人照料的迹象。

w.m: n. 基本要素；基础（常用复数）

paras.en: Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure.
paras.zh: 与自然空间不同，人们对艺术和建筑的接触没有达到同等程度。

paras.en: So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.
paras.zh: 所以，人们的共同审美趣味也没有达到同等程度。

paras.en: It’s possible that the lower amount of agreement in the shared taste of artifacts has more to do with elements of style than with “behavioral consequences”.
paras.zh: 在人工制品的共同审美趣味上，人们的一致程度较低，这可能更多地与风格要素有关，而不是与“行为后果”有关。

w.h: have more to do with…than with
w.m: 更多地与……有关，而不是与……有关

paras.en: All of the consequences seem reasonable (or at least possible), but I think there might be an interesting philosophical conclusion that they did not draw.
paras.zh: 所有这些推论似乎都合理（或者至少是可能成立的），但我认为，或许还有一个有趣的哲学结论，是研究者没有得出的。

paras.en: It seems that there is an objective ground to our aesthetic preferences or evaluations.
paras.zh: 看来，我们的审美偏好或审美评价有客观依据。

paras.en: I am not saying this would mean beauty is completely objective, just that there could possibly be general objective principles at work, i.e., beauty is not simply in the eye of the beholder.
paras.zh: 我并不是说这就意味着美是完全客观的，只是说有可能存在一些普遍的客观原则在起作用，也就是说，美并不只在观看者眼中。

paras.en: Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world.
paras.zh: 大自然在世界各地以共通的方式展现出某些普遍的审美特征，比如光彩。

w.m: 在世界各地；遍及全世界

paras.en: It’s not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common.
paras.zh: 它并非在每个地方都一模一样，但却是共通的。

paras.en: For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.
paras.zh: 例如，不同地方的日落相似程度足以使它具有几乎普遍的吸引力。

w.m: v. 使……有正当理由；使……理所当然

paras.en: Possible universal principles of beauty—such as proportion, fittingness, radiance, and others—are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments.
paras.zh: 美可能具有的普遍原则——比如比例、适切、光彩等——都是宽泛的类别，容许各种各样的具体体现。

paras.en: When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways.
paras.zh: 人们在建筑或艺术领域参与制作人工制品时，会以独特的方式运用这些非常宽泛的概念。

w.m: adj. 独特的；独一无二的

paras.en: But the way they apply the principles may not have universal appeal.
paras.zh: 但他们运用这些原则的方式可能并不具有普遍吸引力。

paras.en: This is why it’s important to experience diverse cultures and their artifacts: doing so opens us up to different ways of approaching or constructing beauty.
paras.zh: 正因如此，体验多元文化及其人工制品才很重要：这样做能让我们接触到看待或构建美的不同方式。

w.m: 正因如此；这就是……的原因
adj. 多元的；多种多样的
使某人接触到；使某人乐于接受

paras.en: And it is always good to question our assumptions.
paras.zh: 而且，对我们的假定提出质疑总是有益的。

passages.name: 2024年12月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 城市化加速下乡村的处境与未来
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与发展
passages.summary: 随着人口增长和全球城市化不断加速，人们把大量注意力集中在城市的可持续性上，对乡村却关注甚少。乡村让人联想到紧密团结的社区和简单宁静的生活，但也存在保守思想和就业机会匮乏的问题，世界各地的乡村居民正纷纷迁出；乡村的人均碳排放量高于城市，而在城里发了财的人到乡村购置第二套住房，又推高了房价，让当地人负担不起。作者认为，乡村生活一直在不断演变，变化不可避免，而乡村的未来却没那么明朗。

paras.en: With population increases and global urbanisation ever accelerating, much attention is focused on the sustainability of our cities and scant attention is paid to the countryside.
paras.zh: 随着人口增长和全球城市化不断加速，人们把大量注意力集中在城市的可持续性上，对乡村却关注甚少。

paras.en: Rural life is associated with closely knit communities, a sense of belonging, and a simple, tranquil life.
paras.zh: 乡村生活让人联想到紧密团结的社区、归属感以及简单宁静的生活。

w.m: 与……联系在一起；使人联想到
紧密团结的；关系密切的

paras.en: Yet whilst some or all of these elements exist in the countryside, so do conservatism and a lack of employment opportunities.
paras.zh: 然而，乡村虽然存在上述部分或全部要素，但同样存在保守思想和就业机会匮乏的问题。

w.m: n. 保守思想；保守主义

paras.en: And it is mostly due to the latter that rural communities are suffering.
paras.zh: 而乡村社区之所以陷入困境，主要就是因为后者。

paras.en: Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.
paras.zh: 受城市地区经济状况改善的吸引，世界各地的乡村居民正纷纷迁出，加剧了人口稠密城市的过度拥挤，也让乡村陷入一片荒凉。

paras.en: So how can the countryside ensure its survival among these changes—or should it at all?
paras.zh: 那么，在这些变化之中，乡村怎样才能确保自身的存续？或者说，乡村究竟该不该存续下去？

paras.en: Due to both the distance between residences and facilities and often intermittent public transport, those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users.
paras.zh: 由于住所与各种设施相距较远，加之公共交通往往时断时续，住在乡村的人使用汽车更多。

w.m: adj. 时断时续的；间歇的

paras.en: Rural dwellers also use more energy maintaining their mostly detached buildings.
paras.zh: 乡村居民的建筑大多是独栋的，维护这些建筑还要耗费更多能源。

paras.en: We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match.
paras.zh: 在城市里，我们或许像箱子一样层层堆叠，但这带来了乡村无法比拟的能源效率。

paras.en: Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice.
paras.zh: 乡村的能源需求导致人均碳排放量高于城市，因此，赞同选择这样的生活方式其实是不负责任的。

paras.en: Protecting the countryside is a hot topic.
paras.zh: 保护乡村是一个热门话题。

paras.en: Those who have made their fortunes in the city often buy second homes in the countryside, visiting intermittently for a sample of a supposedly simple life.
paras.zh: 那些在城市里发了财的人常常在乡村购置第二套住房，不时去那里体验一番所谓的简单生活。

w.m: 第二套住房；第二处住所

paras.en: The side-effect of this is that house prices are pushed up due to increased demand, leaving them unaffordable for local people.
paras.zh: 这带来的副作用是，需求增加推高了房价，让当地人负担不起。

w.m: adj. 负担不起的；买不起的

paras.en: A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside.
paras.zh: 这一难题至今尚未找到解决办法，因为市场力量正进一步迫使居民离开乡村。

paras.en: For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.
paras.zh: 对那些信奉乡村保护的人来说，这种情况令人痛惜。

w.m: adj. 令人痛惜的；可悲的

paras.en: Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved.
paras.zh: 虽然把乡村理想化的看法很常见，但现实是，乡村生活一直在不断演变。

paras.en: Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people.
paras.zh: 工业化使劳动分工增多，改变了乡村人之间的社会联系。

paras.en: The internet has introduced once-foreign cultures into the countryside.
paras.zh: 互联网已把曾经陌生的文化引入乡村。

w.m: adj. 曾经陌生的；一度是外来的

paras.en: Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a “global village”.
paras.zh: 交通线路得到改善，出行也更加负担得起，这让世界变得更容易抵达，造就了一个“地球村”。

w.m: n. 负担得起；可承受性
adj. 易到达的；可进入的

paras.en: Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.
paras.zh: 考虑到这些变化，乡村不断演变无疑是不可避免的。

paras.en: Perhaps the countryside should also prepare itself for massive population increases in the future.
paras.zh: 也许乡村也应该为未来人口的大幅增长做好准备。

paras.en: With cities across the world growing rapidly, how will the current urban generation respond to the inevitable social changes of mass urbanisation?
paras.zh: 随着世界各地的城市迅速扩张，当今这一代城市人将如何应对大规模城市化带来的种种不可避免的社会变化？

paras.en: Will the longing for a simpler life become stronger, fueling a rural renaissance?
paras.zh: 对更简单生活的向往会不会变得更加强烈，从而推动乡村复兴？

paras.en: As the world continues to urbanise, the voices calling for rural preservation may well grow louder.
paras.zh: 随着世界持续城市化，呼吁乡村保护的声音很可能会越来越响亮。

paras.en: But change is inevitable.
paras.zh: 但变化是不可避免的。

paras.en: We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear.
paras.zh: 我们知道，世界将会见证新城市拔地而起、现有城市发展为特大城市，但乡村的未来却没那么明朗。

w.m: 拔地而起；从无到有地出现

passages.name: 2024年12月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 现实觉醒与社交媒体塑造的理想美
passages.genre: 议论文 · 媒体与社会
passages.summary: 在现实世界中，一场觉醒一直在进行，矛头指向多年来强加给我们的审美模式：多家媒体展示身材不符合所谓理想美的女性，一些网红也上传自己的素颜照。但在数字领域，什么样子才算美由社交媒体决定：平台的游戏化互动让用户主动参与，使公认审美规范的内化更加有效，用户还会得到编辑图片、选择滤镜等工具，用来改变外貌以符合理想美。滤镜影响着用户的心理健康；花在社交媒体上的时间让人产生追求无法企及的理想美的强烈冲动，文章认为，唯一能消除这种冲动的不是美容干预，而是心理健康护理。

paras.en: An awakening has been taking place in the physical world against the beauty model that has been dictated to us for years.
paras.zh: 在现实世界中，一场觉醒一直在进行，矛头指向多年来强加给我们的审美模式。

w.m: 把某事强加给某人；向某人规定某事

paras.en: But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.
paras.zh: 但在数字领域，什么样子才算美，却由社交媒体决定。

paras.en: The two opposing struggles are taking place in parallel.
paras.zh: 这两场相互对立的斗争正在同时进行。

paras.en: In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal.
paras.zh: 在现实世界中，这场斗争反抗的是施加在女性身上的潜在压力，这种压力要她们去迎合不切实际的理想美。

w.m: 理想美；（社会推崇的）美的标准

paras.en: As part of the struggle, various media outlets have presented women whose bodies don’t correspond to the so-called ideal.
paras.zh: 作为这场斗争的一部分，多家媒体展示了一些身材并不符合所谓理想美的女性。

w.m: adj. 各种各样的；不同的
n. 理想（标准）；完美的典范

paras.en: All those women who had previously been excluded from the covers of magazines, television series and the public agenda have become “legitimate”.
paras.zh: 过去被排除在杂志封面、电视剧和公共议程之外的所有女性，都已变得“名正言顺”。

w.m: adj. 正当的；名正言顺的

paras.en: At the same time, a group of influencers have begun to upload to social media photos of themselves without makeup, and even photos in which they highlight supposed flaws.
paras.zh: 与此同时，一群网红开始往社交媒体上传自己的素颜照，甚至上传一些突出自身所谓缺陷的照片。

w.m: n. 网红；有影响力的人

paras.en: Technology has reshaped our beauty ideal and is doing a great job communicating that message to the masses.
paras.zh: 技术重塑了我们的理想美，而且正非常出色地向大众传达这一信息。

w.m: 理想美；（社会推崇的）美的标准
做得非常出色；干得很好

paras.en: One of the bizarre legacies of the past decade is the popularity of the “cyborg look”, which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050.
paras.zh: 过去十年留下的怪异遗产之一，是“赛博格外貌”的流行，这种外貌展示了美国人在2050年会是什么模样。

w.m: n. 遗产；遗留下来的东西

paras.en: The cyborg look spread rapidly.
paras.zh: 赛博格外貌迅速流行开来。

paras.en: Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.
paras.zh: 然而如今，Instagram脸已成为新的理想美。

w.m: Instagram脸（社交媒体上流行的一种标准化美颜长相）
理想美；（社会推崇的）美的标准

paras.en: The internalization of accepted beauty norms is much more effective when there is active involvement in the learning process.
paras.zh: 如果在学习过程中主动参与，对公认审美规范的内化就会有效得多。

w.m: adj. 公认的；被普遍接受的

paras.en: The active involvement of users is reflected in the gamified (游戏化的) interaction offered by the social media platforms—the ability to like, write a comment, compare, share.
paras.zh: 用户的主动参与，体现在社交媒体平台提供的游戏化互动上，即能够点赞、写评论、作比较、分享。

paras.en: Once the desired beauty ideal has been internalized, users are given tools or features to change their appearance to suit the accepted beauty ideal, such as editing the image or choosing the ideal filter and the right background.
paras.zh: 所期望的理想美一旦内化于心，用户就会得到一些工具或功能，用来改变自己的外貌以符合公认的理想美，比如编辑图片，或者选择理想的滤镜和合适的背景。

w.m: adj. 期望的；渴望得到的
理想美；（社会推崇的）美的标准
v. 内化；使成为自身观念的一部分
adj. 公认的；被普遍接受的

paras.en: A survey conducted in the United States revealed that more than 50% filter the images before posting them.
paras.zh: 在美国开展的一项调查显示，超过50%的人在发布图片前会先加滤镜。

paras.en: And you will not be surprised to hear that the majority of them are women.
paras.zh: 你听到其中大多数是女性，也不会感到意外。

w.m: adj. 感到意外的；惊讶的

paras.en: One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side.
paras.zh: 痴迷于加滤镜带来的重大后果之一，是一种新出现的倾向：把自己当作被观察、被评价的对象，就像另一个人在一旁观察、评判那样。

w.m: 以同样的方式；就像……那样

paras.en: The effect of the filters is already far beyond amiable amusement.
paras.zh: 滤镜的影响已经远远超出了轻松愉快的消遣。

w.m: adj. 友善的；令人愉快的

paras.en: The filters and the entire game played on the networks affect the mental health of the users.
paras.zh: 滤镜以及在网络上进行的这整场游戏，影响着用户的心理健康。

paras.en: According to a study, apps like Instagram, Snapchat and Facetune allow users to achieve a level of perfection that was previously only observed in beauty magazines.
paras.zh: 据一项研究，Instagram、Snapchat和Facetune等应用让用户能够达到以前只有在美容杂志上才能看到的完美程度。

w.m: 使某人能够做；允许某人做

paras.en: Even though humanity has always cherished beauty, in the last decade our obsession with looks has reached an unprecedented peak.
paras.zh: 尽管人类一向珍视美，但在过去十年里，我们对外貌的痴迷达到了前所未有的顶峰。

w.m: adj. 前所未有的；空前的

paras.en: The time spent on social media creates an urge to achieve an impossible beauty ideal so powerful that the only thing that can fix it is not cosmetic intervention, but mental health care.
paras.zh: 花在社交媒体上的时间会让人产生一种冲动，想要达到无法企及的理想美；这种冲动如此强烈，以至于唯一能消除它的不是美容干预，而是心理健康护理。

w.m: adj. 不可能实现的；无法企及的
理想美；（社会推崇的）美的标准

passages.name: 2024年12月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 恐怖悖论：许多人为何爱看恐怖片
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与娱乐
passages.summary: 作者以外星人的视角描述人们看恐怖片的情景，引出“恐怖悖论”：许多人会主动寻求吓人的娱乐。作者的研究表明，我们人类经过进化，会从能在安全环境中体验负面情绪的情境中获得愉悦，儿童玩的捉迷藏就是一例；恐怖通过利用我们与其他动物共有的、进化而来的恐惧系统起作用，让我们得以把玩负面情绪、形成应对策略。作者认为，即使不是恐怖片的忠实粉丝，也有充分的理由看恐怖片：安然无恙地熬过一部恐怖片，很可能会带来强烈的掌控感；而且看恐怖片能让人更善于处理自己的恐惧。

paras.en: Imagine you’re an alien sent to Earth to document the behaviour of the mammals inhabiting the planet.
paras.zh: 想象一下，你是一个外星人，被派到地球来记录栖居在这颗星球上的哺乳动物的行为。

paras.en: You stumble into a movie theatre that’s showing the latest Hollywood horror film.
paras.zh: 你误打误撞走进一家电影院，那里正在放映好莱坞最新的恐怖片。

w.m: 误打误撞地进入；偶然闯入

paras.en: Several dozen humans are gathered together in a dark, undecorated room.
paras.zh: 几十个人类聚在一间黑暗、毫无装饰的屋子里。

w.m: adj. 未加装饰的；毫无装饰的

paras.en: They’re all staring at a rectangular area on which patterns of light change rapidly.
paras.zh: 他们全都盯着一块长方形区域，上面的光影图案飞快地变换着。

paras.en: They are clearly in a state of high arousal.
paras.zh: 他们显然处于高度兴奋的状态。

w.m: n. 兴奋；（生理或情绪的）唤醒

paras.en: Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.
paras.zh: 他们心率升高，偶尔紧张地四下张望，有时还会在座位上集体惊跳起来，发出尖厉的报警叫声。

paras.en: Eventually, the lights come up and the rectangular screen goes black.
paras.zh: 最后，灯光亮起，那块长方形的屏幕变黑了。

paras.en: The humans stand up and leave the room, chatting and laughing, and showing signs of pleasure.
paras.zh: 这些人类站起身，离开屋子，有说有笑，流露出愉悦的神色。

paras.en: Why do these humans voluntarily expose themselves to what appears to be a deeply unpleasant experience?
paras.zh: 这些人类为什么要自愿去经受一番看上去极不愉快的经历呢？

w.m: 使自己经受；使自己置身于
adj. 令人不快的；不愉快的

paras.en: And why do they react so strongly to those patterns of light on a screen?
paras.zh: 他们又为什么会对屏幕上那些光影图案反应如此强烈呢？

paras.en: I am fascinated with the paradox of horror—the strange fact that many people seek out scary entertainment.
paras.zh: 我对恐怖悖论很着迷，它指的是这样一个奇怪的事实：许多人会主动寻求吓人的娱乐。

w.m: n. 悖论；看似矛盾的现象

paras.en: I think the answer to the puzzle lies in human nature.
paras.zh: 我认为，这个谜题的答案在于人性。

paras.en: My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context.
paras.zh: 我的研究表明，我们人类经过进化，会从这样一些情境中获得愉悦：它们让我们能够在安全的环境中体验负面情绪。

w.m: 使某人能够；允许某人做

paras.en: You can see these elements of horror in children’s games.
paras.zh: 你可以在儿童游戏中看到这些恐怖元素。

paras.en: Take hide-and-seek, for example, which is a simulation of a predator-prey interaction.
paras.zh: 就拿捉迷藏来说，这种游戏模拟的是捕食者与猎物之间的互动。

w.m: adj. 捕食者与猎物之间的

paras.en: The kid hides and the adult pretends to be a predator, searching for the child while howling like a dangerous beast.
paras.zh: 孩子躲起来，大人则假扮捕食者，一边寻找孩子，一边像危险的野兽那样嚎叫。

paras.en: This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario.
paras.zh: 这种模拟为孩子提供了如何避免沦为猎物的关键信息；孩子们往往觉得这类活动非常令人满足，这大概是因为它让他们得以安全地体验一种潜在的灾难性情境。

w.m: adj. 关键的；至关重要的

paras.en: They find it pleasurable, and pleasure is evolution’s way of motivating us toward adaptive behaviour.
paras.zh: 他们觉得这令人愉悦，而愉悦是进化激励我们做出适应性行为的方式。

w.m: adj. 令人愉悦的；愉快的
adj. 适应性的；有助于适应的

paras.en: Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies.
paras.zh: 对许多人来说，恐怖之所以令人愉悦，是因为它让我们能够把玩负面情绪，并形成应对策略。

w.m: adj. 令人愉悦的；愉快的

paras.en: We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion.
paras.zh: 我们会了解到真正害怕是一种什么感觉，也会学会如何处理负面情绪。

paras.en: How, then, does horror work?
paras.zh: 那么，恐怖是如何起作用的呢？

paras.en: My research suggests that horror works by exploiting an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms—an evolved fear system, which we share with other animals.
paras.zh: 我的研究表明，恐怖是通过利用一套古老的生物防御机制起作用的——一种进化而来、我们与其他动物共有的恐惧系统。

paras.en: But humans are uniquely imaginative, and we use our evolved imagination to travel into virtual worlds that are full of danger.
paras.zh: 但人类有着独一无二的想象力，我们会运用进化而来的想象力，进入充满危险的虚拟世界。

w.m: adv. 独特地；独一无二地

paras.en: There are good reasons for watching a horror film, even if you’re not a loyal horror fan.
paras.zh: 即使你并不是恐怖片的忠实粉丝，看恐怖片也有充分的理由。

paras.en: If you make it through the film in one piece, you’ll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience.
paras.zh: 如果你安然无恙地熬过了这部电影，很可能会体验到一种强烈的掌控感，觉得自己成功熬过了一段骇人的经历。

paras.en: Anyway, watching a horror film makes you better at handling your own fear, and who knows when that will become critically relevant?
paras.zh: 不管怎样，看恐怖片能让你更善于处理自己的恐惧，而谁知道这种能力什么时候会变得至关重要呢？

w.m: adj. 相关的；有现实意义的

passages.name: 2024年6月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 你不只是你的工作
passages.genre: 议论文 · 职业与心理
passages.summary: 对很多人来说，工作远不只是一份差事，而是身份中起决定性作用的方面；失去工作会引发一场身份危机，其严重程度远远超过失去工作本身。作者是一名临床心理学家，她认为我们的身份比乍看之下复杂得多：除了工作，我们还可以是朋友、配偶、子女、父母或团体的一员，而且职业身份也会随时间变化。被迫换工作时，我们需要审视自己的信念；在职业发展可能把我们带入新行业的时代，挑战自我认知愈发重要，而归根结底，界定你是谁的正是你自己。

paras.en: When someone asks us “What do you do?” we nearly always reply with our occupation.
paras.zh: 别人问我们“你是做什么的？”，我们几乎总是以自己的职业作答。

paras.en: Work, for many of us, is much more than a job.
paras.zh: 对我们很多人来说，工作远不只是一份差事。

paras.en: It is the defining aspect of our identity.
paras.zh: 它是我们身份中起决定性作用的方面。

w.m: adj. 决定性的；最典型的

paras.en: For many of us it is through our job that we can define ourselves.
paras.zh: 对我们很多人来说，正是通过工作，我们才能界定自己。

paras.en: “Without my job I don’t know who I am” is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair.
paras.zh: “没有了工作，我就不知道自己是谁”——坐在办公椅上，这句话我听人说过不止寥寥几次。

w.m: n. 次；（某事发生的）时候

paras.en: Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs.
paras.zh: 的确，对于那些失去了工作或被迫换工作的来访者，这可能是我和他们一起处理的最具挑战性的方面之一。

w.m: adj. 有挑战性的；艰巨的
n. （心理咨询的）来访者；客户

paras.en: This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself.
paras.zh: 这种失去会引发一场身份危机，其严重程度远远超过失去工作本身。

paras.en: One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance.
paras.zh: 然而，我逐渐明白的道理之一是：我们的身份比我们乍看之下所认识到的要复杂得多。

paras.en: If we take the time to reflect we might recognise that as well as our work we can also identify as a friend, a spouse, a son or daughter, a parent, a member of a sports team or religious community.
paras.zh: 如果我们花时间反思一下，或许就会认识到：除了工作，我们还可以认定自己是朋友、配偶、儿子或女儿、父亲或母亲、运动队或宗教团体的一员。

w.m: 花时间（做）；不怕麻烦去做

paras.en: We may recognise that we feel and act differently in these roles and relationships than we do at work.
paras.zh: 我们也许会认识到，自己在这些角色和关系中的感受与行为，和在工作中有所不同。

paras.en: The passive daughter becomes an assertive leader at work.
paras.zh: 被动的女儿到了工作中，会变成果敢自信的领导者。

w.m: adj. 果敢自信的；坚定自信的

paras.en: Furthermore, our identities at work are not static.
paras.zh: 此外，我们在工作中的身份并非一成不变。

w.m: adj. 静止的；一成不变的

paras.en: They change over time.
paras.zh: 它们会随着时间的推移而改变。

paras.en: I myself have been a shop assistant, a waitress, a student, a graduate, and a clinical psychologist.
paras.zh: 我本人就当过店员、女服务员、学生、毕业生和临床心理学家。

paras.en: At each stage my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing.
paras.zh: 在每个阶段，我适应和发展自身职业身份的能力，对我的身心健康都至关重要。

paras.en: Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives, at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today’s volatile and ever-shifting job market.
paras.zh: 尽管我们喜欢消除生活中的不确定性，但在某种程度上，我们不得不应对不确定性，尤其是在当今动荡不定、变化不断的就业市场中。

w.m: adj. 动荡不定的；易变的

paras.en: How we see ourselves is central to the issue of our identity.
paras.zh: 我们如何看待自己，是身份问题的核心所在。

paras.en: When we tell ourselves “I’m good at starting projects but not so great at seeing them through” it can become part of our belief system.
paras.zh: 我们对自己说“我擅长启动项目，却不太擅长把项目进行到底”，这句话就可能成为我们信念体系的一部分。

paras.en: But if you have the unfortunate experience of an enforced job change, you will need to examine those beliefs to see how grounded in reality they are.
paras.zh: 但如果你不幸经历了被迫换工作，就需要审视那些信念，看看它们在多大程度上立足于现实。

paras.en: You will be required to ask yourself how helpful these beliefs are and consider personal change.
paras.zh: 你将需要问问自己，这些信念有多大帮助，并考虑做出个人改变。

paras.en: We can change our beliefs, behaviours and emotional experience at any time through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline.
paras.zh: 我们可以随时通过尝试、练习和有意识的自律，来改变自己的信念、行为和情绪体验。

paras.en: In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors, it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether we can create a new experience of our identity by changing the beliefs we hold about ourselves in order to expand our career options.
paras.zh: 在这个职业发展可能把我们带入新行业的时代，挑战自我认知愈发重要；同样愈发重要的，是探索我们能否通过改变对自己所持的信念，创造出一种新的身份体验，从而拓宽自己的职业选择。

paras.en: Ultimately it is you who define who you are.
paras.zh: 归根结底，界定你是谁的，正是你自己。

paras.en: You are only your job if you let it be so.
paras.zh: 只有你自己允许如此，你才会仅仅是你的工作。

passages.name: 2024年6月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 白手起家类真人秀强化“美国梦”信念
passages.genre: 说明文 · 媒体与社会
passages.summary: “美国梦”承诺，任何人仅凭努力和抱负就能沿着经济阶梯向上攀登，但如今的美国年轻人很难挣得比父母同龄时更多，美国的向上流动性也比不上其他工业化国家。范德比尔特大学的金恩智及其团队通过实验和调查发现，观看白手起家类真人秀的人对“美国梦”的信念更强；金恩智认为，这类娱乐媒体宣扬并延续着对向上流动的信念。问题在于，如果人们误以为个人只需努力就能为自己创造更好的生活，他们可能就不那么支持真正能够遏制不平等的政策。

paras.en: The “American Dream” promises that in the Land of Opportunity, any individual can climb the economic ladder and prosper through hard work and ambition alone.
paras.zh: “美国梦”承诺，在这片机遇之地，任何人仅凭努力和抱负，就能沿着经济阶梯向上攀登，走向富足。

w.m: 沿着经济阶梯向上攀登；提升经济地位
v. 富足起来；兴旺发达

paras.en: And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.
paras.zh: 然而，如今的美国年轻人很难挣得比父母同龄时更多，而且美国的向上流动性实际上还比不上其他工业化国家。

w.m: 向上流动（性）（指社会经济地位的提升）

paras.en: So why does the idea of the American Dream persist?
paras.zh: 那么，“美国梦”这一观念为何依然存在？

paras.en: A new study in the American Journal of Political Science identifies one factor that has been overlooked: the influence of reality TV.
paras.zh: 《美国政治学杂志》上的一项新研究找出了一个一直被忽视的因素：真人秀节目的影响。

paras.en: Reality shows have come to dominate US television over the past 20 years, notes Eunji Kim from Vanderbilt University.
paras.zh: 范德比尔特大学的金恩智指出，过去20年间，真人秀节目已逐渐在美国电视界占据主导地位。

w.m: v. 在……中占主导地位；主宰

paras.en: And the overwhelming majority of these have a “rags-to-riches” storyline: they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success.
paras.zh: 而且，其中绝大多数节目都有“白手起家”的故事情节：节目的主角是靠努力奋斗取得巨大经济成功的普通美国人。

w.m: adj. 从赤贫到巨富的；白手起家的
v. 以……为主角；以……为特色

paras.en: And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts—which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans—get a much smaller proportion of the viewership.
paras.zh: 此外，这些节目常常跻身收视率最高的节目之列，而新闻节目更真实地描绘了数百万美国人所面临的经济困境，所占的收视份额却要小得多。

w.m: adj. 收视率最高的；观看人数最多的

paras.en: Rags-to-riches stories are ubiquitous (无处不在的) on TV—but does watching these programmes actually convince people that economic mobility is easily attainable?
paras.zh: 白手起家的故事在电视上无处不在，但观看这些节目真的会让人们相信，经济流动很容易实现吗？

w.m: adj. 从赤贫到巨富的；白手起家的
经济流动（性）（指经济地位的变动）
adj. 可实现的；可达到的

paras.en: To find out, Kim’s team had participants watch a 5-minute clip from a reality show with a rags-to-riches storyline.
paras.zh: 为了弄清楚这一点，金恩智的团队让参与者观看了一段5分钟的真人秀片段，这档节目有着白手起家的故事情节。

w.m: adj. 从赤贫到巨富的；白手起家的

paras.en: Control participants watched a clip from a reality show that didn’t have a rags-to-riches story.
paras.zh: 对照组参与者观看的则是一段不含白手起家故事的真人秀片段。

w.m: adj. 从赤贫到巨富的；白手起家的

paras.en: After watching the shows, participants rated how much they agreed with four statements relating to the American Dream.
paras.zh: 看完节目后，参与者就四条与“美国梦”有关的陈述，给自己的认同程度打分。

paras.en: The results showed that those who’d watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream.
paras.zh: 结果显示，看过白手起家片段的人对“美国梦”的信念确实显著更强。

w.m: adj. 从赤贫到巨富的；白手起家的

paras.en: Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people’s existing socioeconomic beliefs.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，按党派归属将参与者分组后，这一效应在共和党人中显著，在民主党人中则不显著；这表明，这些电视节目中隐含的那类信息可能会迎合人们已有的社会经济观念。

paras.en: Kim also conducted a survey of 3,000 US residents.
paras.zh: 金恩智还对3000名美国居民开展了一项调查。

paras.en: They also rated the extent to which they believed success in life is related to various internal factors (such as ambition) and external factors (such as family wealth).
paras.zh: 这些受访者还评定了自己在多大程度上认为，人生成功与各种内在因素（如抱负）和外在因素（如家庭财富）有关。

paras.en: Finally, they read a list of TV programmes and indicated which they regularly watched.
paras.zh: 最后，他们看了一份电视节目清单，并指出自己经常收看其中哪些节目。

paras.en: Participants who were heavy or frequent viewers of rags-to-riches programmes had a stronger belief in the American Dream than those who never watched such shows.
paras.zh: 与从不收看这类节目的人相比，大量或频繁收看白手起家类节目的参与者对“美国梦”的信念更强。

w.m: adj. 从赤贫到巨富的；白手起家的

paras.en: Kim concludes that “rags-to-riches entertainment media are an important cultural force that promotes and perpetuates beliefs in upward mobility”.
paras.zh: 金恩智的结论是，“白手起家类娱乐媒体是一股重要的文化力量，宣扬并延续着对向上流动的信念”。

w.m: adj. 从赤贫到巨富的；白手起家的
向上流动（指社会经济地位的提升）

paras.en: And here’s the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.
paras.zh: 而问题就在于：如果人们误以为个人只需努力就能为自己创造更好的生活，他们可能就不那么支持那些真正能够遏制不平等的政策。

w.m: 所需的全部；只需……就够了

w.h: make a better life for oneself
w.m: 为自己创造更好的生活

paras.en: “In this era of choice, entertainment media are what captures hearts and minds,” Kim writes.
paras.zh: 金恩智写道：“在这个选择众多的时代，俘获人心的正是娱乐媒体。”

paras.en: “Its political consequences are anything but trivial.”
paras.zh: “其政治后果绝非无足轻重。”

w.m: adj. 微不足道的；无足轻重的

passages.name: 2024年6月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 环保主义者的核能之争与德国能源转型
passages.genre: 说明文 · 能源与环境
passages.summary: “环保主义者”一词过去指努力保护野生动植物和自然生态系统的人，如今其含义已演变为涵盖应对人为气候变化的需要；环保主义这两个分支之间的区别，是科学界在核能问题上产生分歧的原因：一方认为解决气候危机的唯一办法是可再生能源，另一方则认为在没有阳光、也没有风的时候，社会仍需要可用的电力来满足基本需求，而比石油、天然气和煤炭清洁得多的核能是自然而然的选择。普遍实现100%可再生能源是否可行，同样存在争议。德国2011年宣布实施能源转型，可再生能源发展迅速，但近年来进展陷入停滞：可再生能源不稳定，电网基础设施滞后，一些地方的民众还强烈抗议新建风力涡轮机。结果，自2010年以来，德国温室气体排放量下降的速度慢于欧盟平均水平。

paras.en: The term “environmentalist” can mean different things.
paras.zh: “环保主义者”这个词可以有不同的含义。

w.m: n. 环保主义者；环境保护论者

paras.en: It used to refer to people trying to protect wildlife and natural ecosystems.
paras.zh: 它过去指的是努力保护野生动植物和自然生态系统的人。

paras.en: In the 21st century, the term has evolved to capture the need to combat human-made climate change.
paras.zh: 到了21世纪，这个词的含义已经演变，涵盖了应对人为气候变化的需要。

paras.en: The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.
paras.zh: 环保主义这两个分支之间的区别，是科学界内部在核能问题上产生分歧的原因。

w.m: n. （思想、观点等的）分支；组成部分
n. 环保主义；环境保护论

paras.en: On one side are purists who believe nuclear power isn’t worth the risk and the exclusive solution to the climate crisis is renewable energy.
paras.zh: 一方是纯粹主义者，他们认为核能不值得冒这个风险，解决气候危机的唯一办法是可再生能源。

paras.en: The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers’ basic demands when the sun isn’t shining and the wind isn’t blowing.
paras.zh: 对立的一方认同可再生能源至关重要，但又表示，社会需要一定量的可用电力，以便在没有阳光、也没有风的时候满足消费者的基本需求。

paras.en: Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited.
paras.zh: 核能比石油、天然气和煤炭清洁得多，是一个自然而然的选择，在水力发电能力有限的地方尤其如此。

w.m: adj. 自然而然的；理所当然的

paras.en: Leon Clarke, who helped author reports for the UN’s Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, isn’t an uncritical supporter of nuclear energy, but says it’s a valuable option to have if we’re serious about reaching carbon neutrality.
paras.zh: 利昂·克拉克曾参与为联合国政府间气候变化专门委员会撰写报告，他并非对核能不加批判的支持者，但表示，如果我们真心想实现碳中和，有核能这个选项是很有价值的。

w.m: n. 专门委员会；专家小组
adj. 不加批判的；不加鉴别的

paras.en: “Core to all of this is the degree to which you think we can actually meet climate goals with 100% renewables,” he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“这一切的核心在于，你认为我们在多大程度上真能依靠100%可再生能源实现气候目标。”

paras.en: “If you don’t believe we can do it, and you care about the climate, you are forced to think about something like nuclear.”
paras.zh: “如果你不相信我们能做到这一点，而你又关心气候，你就不得不考虑核能之类的选项。”

paras.en: The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious.
paras.zh: 普遍实现100%可再生能源是否可行，同样存在争议。

w.m: n. 可再生性（此处指完全使用可再生能源）
adj. 有争议的；引起争论的

paras.en: Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been “100% renewable” for years.
paras.zh: 多年来，佛蒙特州伯灵顿等城市的能源一直是“100%可再生”的。

paras.en: But these cities often have small populations, occasionally still rely on fossil fuel energy and have significant renewable resources at their immediate disposal.
paras.zh: 但这些城市往往人口不多，偶尔仍要依靠化石燃料能源，而且手边就有大量可再生资源可供利用。

w.m: 供某人使用；由某人支配
adj. 近在手边的；直接的

paras.en: Meanwhile, countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities.
paras.zh: 与此同时，成功依靠可再生能源运转的国家，通常是凭借超乎寻常的水力发电能力才做到这一点。

w.m: adj. 超乎寻常的；非凡的

paras.en: Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy.
paras.zh: 德国堪称大型工业化国家进军绿色能源的最佳研究案例。

paras.en: Chancellor Angela Merkel in 2011 announced Energiewende, an energy transition that would phase out nuclear and coal while phasing in renewables.
paras.zh: 2011年，安格拉·默克尔总理宣布实施Energiewende，即一场能源转型，计划逐步淘汰核能和煤炭，同时逐步引入可再生能源。

w.m: 逐步淘汰；逐步停止使用

paras.en: Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400% since 2010, and renewables provided 46% of the country’s electricity in 2019.
paras.zh: 自2010年以来，风能和太阳能发电量增长了400%以上，2019年，可再生能源提供了该国46%的电力。

paras.en: But progress has halted in recent years.
paras.zh: 但近年来，进展陷入了停滞。

paras.en: The instability of renewables doesn’t just mean energy is often not produced at night, but also that solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day, forcing utilities to pay customers to use their electricity.
paras.zh: 可再生能源的不稳定性不仅意味着夜间往往没有能源产出，还意味着白天太阳能和风能可能让电网不堪重负，迫使公用事业公司花钱请客户用自家的电。

w.m: n. 公用事业公司（如电力公司）

paras.en: Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany’s north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas.
paras.zh: 滞后的电网基础设施难以把这些过剩的绿色能源从德国北部输送到工业集中的南部，这意味着许多工厂仍然靠煤炭和天然气运转。

paras.en: The political limit has also been reached in some places, with citizens meeting the construction of new wind turbines with loud protests.
paras.zh: 一些地方也已触及政治上的极限：民众对新建风力涡轮机报以强烈抗议。

paras.en: The result is that Germany’s greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by around 11.5% since 2010—slower than the EU average of 13.5%.
paras.zh: 结果是，自2010年以来，德国的温室气体排放量下降了约11.5%，慢于欧盟13.5%的平均降幅。

passages.name: 2024年6月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 员工为何不出面干预危险行为
passages.genre: 说明文 · 职场与安全
passages.summary: 员工都知道是非对错，但看到有人在工作场所做出危险行为时，出面干预的人并不多。影响人们是否干预的因素包括能否察觉到危险情况正开始发生、公司文化能否让人放心地说出来、是否具备有效表达的沟通技巧；此外，旁观者效应、对受罚和多干活的恐惧以及过去尝试失败的经历，也会导致人们不出面干预。称职的工人和主管都负有干预和保障安全的职责；文章认为，还应让组织里的每一个人都明白，目睹可能不安全的行为时，自己有义务出面干预。

paras.en: It is irrefutable that employees know the difference between right and wrong.
paras.zh: 员工都知道是非对错，这一点无可辩驳。

w.m: adj. 无可辩驳的；不容置疑的

w.h: know the difference between right and wrong
w.m: 知道是非对错；明辨是非

paras.en: So why don’t more employees intervene when they see someone exhibiting at-risk behavior in the workplace?
paras.zh: 那么，看到有人在工作场所做出危险行为时，为什么没有更多员工出面干预呢？

paras.en: There are a number of factors that influence whether people intervene.
paras.zh: 有几个因素会影响人们是否出面干预。

paras.en: First, they need to be able to see a risky situation beginning to unfold.
paras.zh: 首先，他们需要能够察觉到危险情况正开始发生。

paras.en: Second, the company’s culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up.
paras.zh: 其次，公司文化需要让他们觉得可以放心地说出来。

paras.en: And third, they need to have the communication skills to say something effectively.
paras.zh: 第三，他们需要具备相应的沟通技巧，能够有效地把话说出口。

paras.en: This is not strictly a workplace problem; it’s a growing problem off the job too.
paras.zh: 这并不单单是工作场所的问题；在工作之外，这一问题也日益严重。

w.m: adv. 仅仅；完全（用于否定句）
adj. 日益严重的；不断增长的

paras.en: Every day people witness things on the street and choose to stand idly by.
paras.zh: 人们每天在街上目睹各种事情，却选择袖手旁观。

paras.en: This is known as the bystander effect—the more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone in that group is to help the victim.
paras.zh: 这叫作“旁观者效应”：目睹某一事件的人越多，这群人中任何一个人去帮助受害者的可能性就越小。

paras.en: The psychology behind this is called diffusion of responsibility.
paras.zh: 这背后的心理机制称为“责任分散”。

paras.en: Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it—meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need.
paras.zh: 简单来说，人群越大，就有越多的人以为别人会处理这件事，这就意味着，在需要的时候，实际上没有人出面干预或采取行动。

w.m: 在需要的时候；在危急关头

paras.en: This crowd mentality is strong enough for people to evade their known responsibilities.
paras.zh: 这种从众心理的力量足以让人们逃避自己明知应尽的责任。

paras.en: But it’s not only frontline workers who don’t make safety interventions in the workplace.
paras.zh: 但在工作场所，不实施安全干预的并非只有一线工人。

paras.en: There are also instances where supervisors do not intervene.
paras.zh: 也存在主管不出面干预的情况。

paras.en: When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level, it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone.
paras.zh: 如果一群员工看到不安全行为在领导层面没有得到处理，这就开了一个先例：这类情况就该这样处理，从而为所有人确立了安全文化。

paras.en: Despite the fact that workers are encouraged to intervene when they observe unsafe operations, this happens less than half of the time.
paras.zh: 尽管工人们受到鼓励，看到不安全的操作时要出面干预，但出面干预的情况还不到一半。

w.h: less than half of the time

paras.en: Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening.
paras.zh: 恐惧是人们不出面干预的根本因素。

paras.en: There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they’ll have to do more work if they intervene.
paras.zh: 人们害怕受罚，害怕一旦出面干预，自己就得多干活。

paras.en: Unsuccessful attempts in the past are another strong contributing factor to why people don’t intervene—they tend to prefer to defer that action to someone else for all future situations.
paras.zh: 过去尝试失败，是导致人们不出面干预的另一个重要促成因素：今后无论遇到什么情况，他们往往都宁愿把这一行动交给别人去做。

w.m: 促成因素；起作用的因素

paras.en: On many worksites, competent workers must be appointed.
paras.zh: 在许多作业现场，都必须指派称职的工人。

paras.en: Part of their job is to intervene when workers perform a task without the proper equipment or if the conditions are unsafe.
paras.zh: 他们的部分职责，就是在工人没有适当的设备就执行任务时，或者在作业条件不安全时出面干预。

paras.en: Competent workers are also required to stop work from continuing when there’s a danger.
paras.zh: 出现危险时，称职的工人还必须阻止作业继续下去。

paras.en: Supervisors also play a critical role.
paras.zh: 主管也发挥着至关重要的作用。

w.m: adj. 至关重要的；关键的

paras.en: Even if a competent person isn’t required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them.
paras.zh: 即使不要求配备称职人员，主管也需要具备多方面的技能，不仅能识别并减轻工作场所的危害，还能在团队内部营造一种安全氛围，支持大家出面干预、彼此坦诚沟通。

w.m: 多方面的；一系列广泛的

paras.en: Beyond competent workers and supervisors, it’s important to teach everyone within the organization that they are obliged to intervene if they witness a possible unsafe act, whether they’re a designated competent person, a supervisor or a frontline worker.
paras.zh: 除了称职的工人和主管，重要的是要教育组织里的每一个人：如果目睹可能不安全的行为，那么无论自己是指定的称职人员、主管还是一线工人，都有义务出面干预。

passages.name: 2024年6月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 可变性对学习至关重要
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与学习
passages.summary: 可变性对学习新技能至关重要，因为它能让所学内容得到更好的泛化。拉维夫和同事们梳理了多个领域的150多项相关研究，发现“可变性”一词可指至少四种不同的可变性，但目前还不知道哪一种对学习最有效。对于可变性为何会影响学习和泛化，文章介绍了三种解释；拉维夫认为，理解可变性的影响对日常生活的方方面面都很重要，可变性甚至会影响人们的社交生活。

paras.en: Variability is crucially important for learning new skills.
paras.zh: 可变性对学习新技能至关重要。

paras.en: Consider learning how to serve in tennis.
paras.zh: 不妨想一想学习网球发球的情形。

paras.en: Should you always practise serving from exactly the same location on the court, aiming at the same spot?
paras.zh: 你是否应该总是在球场上完全相同的位置练习发球，并且瞄准同一个点呢？

paras.en: Although practising in more variable conditions will be slower at first, it will likely make you a better tennis player in the end.
paras.zh: 在变化更多的条件下练习，虽然起初会慢一些，但最终很可能让你成为更出色的网球选手。

paras.en: This is because variability leads to better generalisation of what is learned.
paras.zh: 这是因为可变性能让所学内容得到更好的泛化。

w.m: n. 泛化（把所学推广到新情况）；概括

paras.en: This principle is found in many domains, including speech perception and learning categories.
paras.zh: 这一原理见于许多领域，包括言语感知和类别学习。

paras.en: For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category “dog” if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.
paras.zh: 例如，如果婴儿只接触吉娃娃，而不是许多不同品种的狗，他们就很难学会“狗”这个类别。

w.m: n. 吉娃娃（一种小型犬）

paras.en: “There are over ten different names for this basic principle,” says Limor Raviv, the senior investigator of a recent study.
paras.zh: “这一基本原理有十多个不同的名称。”最近一项研究的资深研究员利莫尔·拉维夫说。

paras.en: “Learning from less variable input is often fast, but may fail to generalise to new stimuli.”
paras.zh: “从变化较少的输入中学习往往很快，但可能无法泛化到新的刺激上。”

paras.en: To identify key patterns and understand the underlying principles of variability effects, Raviv and her colleagues reviewed over 150 studies on variability and generalisation across fields, including computer science, linguistics, categorisation, visual perception and formal education.
paras.zh: 为了找出关键规律、理解可变性效应背后的原理，拉维夫和同事们梳理了150多项关于可变性与泛化的研究，这些研究来自多个领域，包括计算机科学、语言学、分类、视觉感知和正规教育。

paras.en: The researchers discovered that, across studies, the term variability can refer to at least four different kinds of variability, such as set size and scheduling.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，在不同的研究中，“可变性”一词可以指至少四种不同的可变性，例如样本集的大小和编排方式。

paras.en: “These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don’t know which is most effective for learning,” says Raviv.
paras.zh: “从来没有人直接比较过这四种可变性，这意味着我们目前还不知道哪一种对学习最有效。”拉维夫说。

paras.en: The impact of variability depends on whether it is relevant to the task or not.
paras.zh: 可变性的影响取决于它与任务是否相关。

paras.en: But according to the “Mr. Miyagi principle”, practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills.
paras.zh: 但根据“宫城先生原理”，练习看似无关的技能，实际上可能有助于学习其他技能。

w.m: 宫城先生原理（宫城先生是电影《龙威小子》中的武术师傅）

paras.en: But why does variability impact learning and generalisation?
paras.zh: 但可变性为什么会影响学习和泛化呢？

paras.en: One theory is that more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not.
paras.zh: 一种理论认为，变化更多的输入能够凸显任务的哪些方面是相关的、哪些不是。

paras.en: Another theory is that greater variability leads to broader generalisations.
paras.zh: 另一种理论认为，更大的可变性会带来更广泛的泛化。

paras.en: This is because variability will represent the real world better, including atypical (非典型的) examples.
paras.zh: 这是因为可变性能更好地反映现实世界，包括那些非典型的例子。

paras.en: A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.
paras.zh: 第三个原因与记忆的运作方式有关：训练富于变化时，学习者就不得不主动重构自己的记忆。

paras.en: “Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life.
paras.zh: “毫不夸张地说，理解可变性的影响对我们日常生活的方方面面都很重要。

paras.en: Beyond affecting the way we learn language, motor skills, and categories, it even has an impact on our social lives,” explains Raviv.
paras.zh: 除了影响我们学习语言、运动技能和类别的方式之外，可变性甚至还会对我们的社交生活产生影响。”拉维夫解释说。

paras.en: “For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community.
paras.zh: “例如，人们是在小社区还是在较大的社区长大，会影响他们的面孔识别。

paras.en: Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory.”
paras.zh: 童年时期接触的面孔较少，与面孔记忆力减弱有关。”

paras.en: “We hope this work will spark people’s curiosity and generate more work on the topic,” concludes Raviv.
paras.zh: “我们希望这项研究能激发人们的好奇心，并催生更多关于这一课题的研究。”拉维夫总结道。

w.m: v. 总结说；以……结束（讲话）

paras.en: “Our paper raises a lot of open questions.
paras.zh: “我们的论文提出了许多悬而未决的问题。

paras.en: Can we find similar effects of variability beyond the brain, for instance, in the immune system?”
paras.zh: 我们能否在大脑之外，比如在免疫系统中，发现类似的可变性效应？”

passages.name: 2024年6月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 少些讽刺，多些机智
passages.genre: 议论文 · 心理与人际关系
passages.summary: 作者认为，讽刺其实是伪装成幽默的敌意：许多被讽刺的人会觉得受了贬低，而一个人一贯以讽刺的方式行事，还可能加剧自身潜在的敌意和不安全感。作者并不是说所有讽刺都不好，但建议收敛讽刺，转而在巧妙的机智上下功夫；机智通常不带任何敌意，因此更受交流对象欣赏。

paras.en: Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common: You know them when you hear them.
paras.zh: 讽刺和爵士乐有一个出人意料的共同点：你一听就能认出它们。

paras.en: Sarcasm is mostly understood through tone of voice, which is used to portray the opposite of the literal words.
paras.zh: 讽刺主要通过语气来理解，语气用来表现与字面意思相反的含义。

paras.en: For example, when someone says, “Well, that’s exactly what I need right now,” their tone can tell you it’s not what they need at all.
paras.zh: 例如，有人说“嗯，这正是我现在需要的”时，他的语气能让你听出，这根本不是他需要的。

paras.en: Most frequently, sarcasm highlights an irritation or is, quite simply, mean.
paras.zh: 最常见的情况是，讽刺凸显某种恼怒，或者说白了，就是刻薄。

paras.en: If you want to be happier and improve your relationships, cut out sarcasm.
paras.zh: 如果你想更快乐、改善人际关系，那就戒掉讽刺吧。

paras.en: Why?
paras.zh: 为什么？

paras.en: Because sarcasm is actually hostility disguised as humor.
paras.zh: 因为讽刺其实是伪装成幽默的敌意。

paras.en: Despite smiling outwardly, many people who receive sarcastic comments feel put down and often think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible.
paras.zh: 许多人听到讽刺自己的话时，尽管表面上笑着，心里却觉得受到了贬低，而且常常认为说这些讽刺话的人粗鲁无礼，或者令人鄙视。

w.m: adj. 可鄙的；令人鄙视的

paras.en: Indeed, it’s not surprising that the word sarcasm derives from the Greek word “sarkazein,” which literally means “to tear or strip the flesh off.”
paras.zh: 的确，sarcasm（讽刺）一词源于希腊语单词“sarkazein”，这并不奇怪：该词的字面意思是“撕下或剥下皮肉”。

w.m: adv. 字面上；照字面意思

paras.en: Hence, it’s no wonder that sarcasm is often preceded by the word “cutting” and that it hurts.
paras.zh: 因此，难怪sarcasm（讽刺）前面常常冠以“cutting”（尖刻的）一词，也难怪讽刺会伤人。

paras.en: What’s more, since actions strongly determine thoughts and feelings, when a person consistently acts sarcastically, it may only serve to heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity.
paras.zh: 此外，由于行为在很大程度上决定着思想和情感，一个人如果一贯以讽刺的方式行事，可能只会加剧其潜在的敌意和不安全感。

w.m: adv. 在很大程度上；强烈地

paras.en: After all, when you come right down to it, sarcasm can be used as a subtle form of bullying—and most bullies are angry, insecure, or cowardly.
paras.zh: 毕竟，归根结底，讽刺可以用作一种隐蔽的欺凌方式，而大多数欺凌者都心怀愤怒、缺乏安全感或者懦弱。

w.h: when you come right down to it

w.m: adj. 隐蔽的；不易察觉的
n. 欺凌者；恃强凌弱者

paras.en: Alternatively, when a person stops voicing negative comments, especially sarcastic ones, they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident.
paras.zh: 反过来，一个人如果不再说负面的话，尤其是讽刺的话，可能很快就会开始感到更快乐、更自信。

paras.en: Also, other people in their life benefit even more because they no longer have to hear the emotionally hurtful language of sarcasm.
paras.zh: 而且，他们生活中的其他人受益还要更大，因为这些人不必再听那些伤人感情的讽刺话语了。

paras.en: Now, I’m not saying all sarcasm is bad.
paras.zh: 话说回来，我并不是说所有讽刺都不好。

w.m: adv. （用于引出话题或转折）话说回来；那么

paras.en: It may just be better used sparingly—like a potent spice in cooking.
paras.zh: 讽刺或许只是少用为好，就像烹饪中味道浓烈的香料一样。

w.m: adj. （味道、效力）强烈的；浓烈的

paras.en: Too much of the spice, and the dish will be overwhelmed by it.
paras.zh: 这种香料放得太多，菜就会被它的味道盖过。

paras.en: Similarly, an occasional dash of sarcastic wit can spice up a chat and add an element of humor to it.
paras.zh: 同样，偶尔来一点讽刺式的机智，能给聊天调调味，并为其增添几分幽默。

paras.en: But a big or steady serving of sarcasm will overwhelm the emotional flavor of any conversation and can taste very bitter to its recipient.
paras.zh: 但是，大份的或源源不断的讽刺会盖过任何谈话的情感味道，而且在被讽刺的人尝来，可能会非常苦涩。

paras.en: So, tone down the sarcasm and work on clever wit instead, which is usually without any hostility and thus more appreciated by those you’re communicating with.
paras.zh: 所以，收敛一下讽刺，转而在巧妙的机智上下功夫吧；机智通常不带任何敌意，因此更受与你交流的人欣赏。

paras.en: In essence, sarcasm is easy, while true, harmless wit takes talent.
paras.zh: 从本质上说，讽刺很容易，而真正的、无害的机智则需要才华。

paras.en: Thus, the main difference between wit and sarcasm is that, as already stated, sarcasm is often hostility disguised as humor.
paras.zh: 因此，机智与讽刺的主要区别在于，如前所述，讽刺往往是伪装成幽默的敌意。

paras.en: It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting.
paras.zh: 讽刺可能意在伤人，而且往往尖酸刻薄。

w.m: adj. 尖酸的；充满怨恨的

paras.en: Witty statements are usually in response to someone’s unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities.
paras.zh: 机智的话语通常是在回应某人无益的言论或行为，其用意是通过强调问题的荒谬之处，来理清和阐明问题。

w.m: adj. 无益的；没有帮助的

paras.en: Sarcastic statements are expressed in a cutting manner; witty remarks are delivered with undisguised and harmless humor.
paras.zh: 讽刺的话语以尖刻的方式表达出来；机智的话则带着不加掩饰、无害的幽默说出来。

w.m: adj. 不加掩饰的；公开的

passages.name: 2023年12月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 常遭恐惧却值得珍视的蜘蛛
passages.genre: 说明文 · 动物与生态保护
passages.summary: 蜘蛛虽是童诗、儿歌和万圣节装饰中的常客，人们对它的恐惧却很普遍，而这种恐惧似乎与对风险的理性评估无关：英国的蜘蛛几乎全都无害，农田里的蜘蛛还会捕食与人类争夺庄稼的昆虫。与研究得最多的英国蝴蝶不同，关于蜘蛛生存状况的数据很缺乏；飞虫数量大幅减少意味着蜘蛛的食物供应减少，栖息地丧失和碎片化也威胁着一些蜘蛛种类。随着再野化列入环境政策议程，人们希望蜘蛛将来能沿着野生动物走廊自行迁移、适应气候变化；作者也认为，如果更多动物爱好者认识到蜘蛛的了不起之处，那将是一件好事。

paras.en: Spiders make their presence felt in late August and through early autumn.
paras.zh: 从8月下旬一直到初秋，蜘蛛都会让人感觉到它们的存在。

w.m: 使人感觉到自己的存在；引人注意
adj. 后期的；（某月）下旬的
prep. 一直到（某时）；在整个……期间

paras.en: This is the mating season of some of the most common varieties, when male house spiders come out of hidden corners to look for females, and garden spiders reach adult size and spin their most dazzling webs.
paras.zh: 这是一些最常见的蜘蛛种类交配的季节：雄性家隅蛛会从隐蔽的角落里钻出来寻找雌蛛，园蛛则长到成年大小，织出它们最炫目的网。

w.m: 家隅蛛（常见于室内的蜘蛛）

paras.en: Yet while the spider is a familiar fixture of nursery poems or songs and Halloween decorations, its relationship with humans is complicated.
paras.zh: 然而，尽管蜘蛛是童诗、儿歌和万圣节装饰中的常客，它与人类的关系却很复杂。

w.m: n. 固定存在的人或物；常客
n. （用作定语）儿童的；托儿所

paras.en: Fear of spiders is common and has serious impacts on the lives of sufferers.
paras.zh: 对蜘蛛的恐惧很普遍，严重影响着患者的生活。

paras.en: Its prevalence appears unrelated to any rational assessment of risk.
paras.zh: 这种恐惧的普遍程度，似乎与对风险的任何理性评估都毫无关联。

paras.en: Spiders in the UK are almost all harmless.
paras.zh: 英国的蜘蛛几乎全都无害。

paras.en: Farmland species perform valuable ecosystem services, by preying on insects that are our competitors for crops.
paras.zh: 农田里的蜘蛛物种通过捕食与我们争夺庄稼的昆虫，提供宝贵的生态系统服务。

w.m: 生态系统服务（生态系统给人类带来的益处）

paras.en: But they are a constant source of human anxieties—with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the Middle Ages.
paras.zh: 但蜘蛛始终是人类焦虑的一个来源——它们在文化上与女巫和邪恶联系在一起，这种关联可以追溯到中世纪。

w.m: adj. 持续不断的；始终存在的

paras.en: Does this perhaps explain, in part, the lack of data about how spiders are faring in our age of ecological crisis?
paras.zh: 这会不会在一定程度上解释了，在我们这个生态危机时代，为什么缺乏关于蜘蛛生存状况的数据？

w.m: v. 过得（好或坏）；（生存）状况如何

paras.en: British butterflies are the most studied group of insects in the world, due to the long tradition of collecting and observing them.
paras.zh: 英国蝴蝶是世界上研究得最多的昆虫类群，因为收集和观察蝴蝶在英国有着悠久的传统。

paras.en: But spider conservationists point out that it was only in the 1980s that the classification of house spiders was properly sorted out.
paras.zh: 但蜘蛛保护人士指出，直到20世纪80年代，家隅蛛的分类才真正理清。

w.m: n. （自然）保护人士；自然资源保护主义者

paras.en: And while information about insect populations is gathered by experiments that measure the numbers hitting windscreens or traps, there have been few attempts to count spiders.
paras.zh: 而且，虽然人们通过实验来收集有关昆虫种群的信息，测算撞上挡风玻璃或落入诱捕器的昆虫数量，但迄今很少有人尝试统计蜘蛛的数量。

paras.en: The huge reductions in the numbers of flying insects can only mean a reduction in spiders’ food supply.
paras.zh: 飞虫数量大幅减少，只能意味着蜘蛛的食物供应减少。

paras.en: A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development.
paras.zh: 最近一项具有里程碑意义的研究发现，1989年至2016年间，昆虫种群数量下降了75%，人们认为，这要归咎于使用农药以及为开发而破坏野生区域。

w.m: adj. 具有里程碑意义的

paras.en: This means the overall picture for spiders is worrying, as it is for most creatures.
paras.zh: 这意味着，蜘蛛的总体状况令人担忧，大多数生物的情况也是如此。

paras.en: But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate.
paras.zh: 但保护人士最担心的，是那些因栖息地丧失和碎片化而受到威胁的种类，这种状况使它们无法迁移。

w.m: n. （自然）保护人士；自然资源保护主义者

paras.en: Of around 650 spider species regularly recorded in the UK, the majority thrive in marshes and wasteland.
paras.zh: 在英国经常有记录的约650种蜘蛛中，大多数都在沼泽和荒地里繁衍兴旺。

paras.en: Conservation efforts, often led by determined individuals, have helped some species to recover by reintroducing them to new areas.
paras.zh: 保护工作往往由意志坚定的个人牵头，已经通过把一些物种重新引入新的地区，帮助它们得到了恢复。

w.m: adj. 意志坚定的；坚决的

paras.en: With rewilding now firmly on the environmental policy agenda, the hope is that in future, spiders will be enabled to migrate by themselves, adapting to climate change by moving along wildlife corridors.
paras.zh: 如今，再野化已牢牢列入环境政策议程，人们希望将来蜘蛛能够自行迁移，沿着野生动物走廊移动，从而适应气候变化。

w.m: n. 再野化（恢复自然生态）
野生动物走廊（供野生动物迁移的生态通道）

paras.en: It seems unlikely that spiders will ever attract the same level of human enthusiasm as bees, birds or butterflies, in spite of their unique status as nature’s spinners.
paras.zh: 尽管蜘蛛作为大自然的吐丝者地位独特，但它们似乎永远不太可能像蜜蜂、鸟类或蝴蝶那样，赢得人类同等程度的热情。

w.m: adj. 独特的；独一无二的

paras.en: But as they reveal themselves in all their splendour this autumn, it would be a good thing if more animal lovers recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific.
paras.zh: 但今年秋天，在蜘蛛尽显风采之际，如果有更多动物爱好者认识到蜘蛛在种种方面实在了不起，那将是一件好事。

w.h: it would be a good thing if

passages.name: 2023年12月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 研究成果应走出学术圈与公众分享
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科研与社会
passages.summary: 研究的本意是造福社会，而研究成果必须走出研究实验室和学术期刊，研究才能充分发挥作用。然而，许多研究人员似乎满足于在学术期刊或会议上分享成果；争取终身教职的压力使社区层面的推广得不到优先考虑；很多研究人员还缺乏面向普通受众的写作能力，有些人则因种种顾虑而回避在学术界以外传播成果。作者认为，分享研究成果对研究人员和社区双方都有益，各机构、资助组织、伦理委员会和研究人员应当采取措施，推动研究成果更广泛地与公众分享。

paras.en: Research is meant to benefit society by raising public awareness and creating products and innovations that enhance development.
paras.zh: 研究的本意是通过提高公众意识、创造能促进发展的产品和创新来造福社会。

paras.en: For research to serve its full purpose, the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals.
paras.zh: 要让研究充分发挥作用，研究成果就必须走出研究实验室和学术期刊的局限。

paras.en: Findings effectively communicated can go a long way to serve the interests of the public.
paras.zh: 研究成果若能得到有效传播，就能大大有助于维护公众利益。

w.m: 大大有助于；对……大有作用
维护……的利益；符合……的利益

paras.en: They can help address social injustices or improve treatments offered to patients.
paras.zh: 这些成果能帮助解决社会不公问题，或改进为患者提供的治疗。

w.m: n. 不公正；不公平现象

paras.en: Many researchers seem to be content with sharing the results of their studies in academic journals or at conferences.
paras.zh: 许多研究人员似乎满足于在学术期刊或会议上分享自己的研究成果。

paras.en: But few journals allow everybody to read the findings.
paras.zh: 但允许所有人阅读这些研究成果的期刊寥寥无几。

paras.en: Even articles freely available are usually written in academic language incomprehensible to the average reader.
paras.zh: 即使是可以免费获取的文章，通常也是用普通读者无法理解的学术语言写成的。

w.m: adj. 无法理解的；难以理解的

paras.en: For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals.
paras.zh: 对处在终身教职考核体系中的研究人员而言，主要目标是获得终身教职，而这在一定程度上可以通过在知名期刊上发表若干篇论文来实现。

w.m: adj. 终身教职考核制的；可转为终身教职的
n. 终身教职；终身职位
使某事得以完成；使（论文）得以发表

paras.en: Pressures like this mean community-level outreach is not prioritised.
paras.zh: 诸如此类的压力意味着，社区层面的推广工作得不到优先考虑。

w.m: v. 优先考虑；把……列为优先事项

paras.en: Many researchers lack the writing skills to describe their results to a general audience.
paras.zh: 许多研究人员缺乏向普通受众描述自己研究成果的写作能力。

paras.en: They may also worry about whether the public will understand their findings, or about findings being used to influence controversial policies.
paras.zh: 他们可能还担心公众能否理解自己的研究成果，或者担心研究成果被用来影响有争议的政策。

paras.en: These concerns cause some researchers to shy away from communicating their findings outside the academic community.
paras.zh: 这些顾虑使一些研究人员回避在学术界以外传播自己的研究成果。

paras.en: Propagating research findings beyond academic publications is particularly crucial for addressing certain social disparities.
paras.zh: 将研究成果传播到学术出版物以外，对于解决某些社会差距问题尤为关键。

w.m: adj. 关键的；至关重要的

paras.en: It can help families, communities, healthcare providers, policymakers, government agencies and other stakeholders to understand and respond to crises that plague society.
paras.zh: 这样做能帮助家庭、社区、医疗服务提供者、政策制定者、政府机构和其他利益相关者认识并应对困扰社会的危机。

paras.en: The benefits of sharing findings flow both ways.
paras.zh: 分享研究成果带来的好处是双向的。

paras.en: Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research.
paras.zh: 与其他研究人员和公众交流互动，能够带来意想不到的新联系和新想法，而这些联系和想法或许能为研究指出富有成效的新方向。

paras.en: For the benefit of both researchers and the communities, the need to find innovative, accessible ways to share the work cannot be overstated.
paras.zh: 为了研究人员和社区双方的利益，寻找创新而通俗易懂的方式来分享研究工作，其必要性怎么强调都不为过。

w.m: adj. 易于理解的；易获取的

paras.en: Institutions and funding organisations should support more researchers to publish in open access journals so that the public doesn’t have to pay to read them.
paras.zh: 各机构和资助组织应该支持更多研究人员在开放获取期刊上发表论文，这样公众就不必付费阅读这些期刊了。

paras.en: Institutions and researchers should invest in partnerships that expand capacity for sharing results more broadly.
paras.zh: 各机构和研究人员应该投资于合作关系，借此增强更广泛地分享研究成果的能力。

w.m: n. 合作关系；伙伴关系

paras.en: Furthermore, ethics committees should make it mandatory for researchers to share their results with the public.
paras.zh: 此外，伦理委员会应该规定，研究人员必须与公众分享自己的研究成果。

w.h: make it mandatory for sb to do
w.m: 规定某人必须做；强制要求某人做

paras.en: Every research participant should opt in or out of receiving results, as part of the process of giving informed consent.
paras.zh: 作为表示知情同意这一过程的一部分，每位研究参与者都应选择是否接收研究成果。

w.m: 选择接受或不接受；选择加入或退出

paras.en: There could be misunderstanding of the findings presented by the researcher because of technical terms.
paras.zh: 由于有专业术语，人们对研究人员所展示的研究成果可能会产生误解。

paras.en: But this can be resolved by researchers engaging the services of professional writers or communication officers to help with translating their study into more accessible language and share it widely with media outlets and the public.
paras.zh: 但研究人员可以聘请专业写作人员或传播专员来解决这个问题，请他们帮忙把自己的研究转化为更通俗易懂的语言，并与媒体机构和公众广泛分享。

w.m: 聘请；雇用（某人提供服务）
adj. 通俗易懂的；易于理解的

paras.en: Sharing results with the people who are most affected by them makes us better researchers and ensures that our work can be used to improve people’s lives.
paras.zh: 与受研究成果影响最大的人分享成果，能让我们成为更好的研究人员，并确保我们的研究工作能用来改善人们的生活。

paras.en: Institutions and collaborators must recognise the value of doing so.
paras.zh: 各机构和合作者必须认识到这样做的价值。

passages.name: 2023年12月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 竞争：天性使然还是文化造就
passages.genre: 议论文 · 心理与文化
passages.summary: 对于竞争是后天习得的还是遗传的，心理学家长期以来一直意见不一；从心理学角度来说，竞争一直被视为人类内驱力的必然结果。但当前的人类学研究表明，这种看法可能是错误的。也常有人指出，自然选择这一概念中并没有任何内容表明竞争是实现“适者生存”的最成功策略，达尔文本人也断言他所描述的斗争可以涵盖依存与合作。人类学家玛格丽特·米德研究了几个不看重竞争的社会，最终得出结论：竞争性是人类行为中由文化造就的一个方面，它在某一特定社会中的盛行程度取决于该社会对它的重视程度。

paras.en: Psychologists have long been in disagreement as to whether competition is a learned or a genetic component of human behavior.
paras.zh: 对于竞争是人类行为中后天习得的成分还是遗传的成分，心理学家长期以来一直意见不一。

w.m: adj. 后天习得的；学来的

paras.en: Whatever it is, you cannot but recognize the effect competition is exerting in academics and many other areas of contemporary life.
paras.zh: 无论属于哪一种，你都不得不承认，竞争正在学术领域以及当代生活的其他许多领域产生影响。

w.m: pron. 无论什么；不管什么

paras.en: Psychologically speaking, competition has been seen as an inevitable consequence of human drives.
paras.zh: 从心理学角度来说，竞争一直被视为人类内驱力的必然结果。

w.m: adj. 必然的；不可避免的

paras.en: According to Sigmund Freud, humans are born screaming for attention and full of organic drives for fulfillment in various areas.
paras.zh: 按照西格蒙德·弗洛伊德的说法，人生来就哭喊着要人关注，并且充满了想在各方面得到满足的生理内驱力。

paras.en: Initially, we compete for the attention of our parents.
paras.zh: 起初，我们争夺的是父母的关注。

paras.en: Thereafter, we are at the mercy of a battle between our base impulses for self-fulfillment and social and cultural norms which prohibit pure indulgence.
paras.zh: 此后，我们便受制于一场斗争：一方是我们追求自我满足的低级冲动，另一方是禁止纯粹放纵的社会和文化规范。

w.m: n. 自我满足；自我实现

paras.en: Current work in anthropology (人类学) has suggested, however, that this view of the role of competition in human behavior may be incorrect.
paras.zh: 然而，当前的人类学研究表明，这种关于竞争在人类行为中所起作用的看法可能是错误的。

paras.en: Thomas Hobbes, one of the great philosophers of the seventeenth century, is perhaps best remembered for his characterization of the “natural world”, that is, the world before the imposition of the will of humanity, as being “nasty, brutish, and short.”
paras.zh: 托马斯·霍布斯是17世纪的伟大哲学家之一，他最为人铭记的，或许是他把“自然世界”（即人类强加自身意志之前的世界）描述为“肮脏、野蛮而短暂”。

w.m: 托马斯·霍布斯（英国哲学家）
adj. 肮脏的；令人厌恶的

paras.en: This image of the pre-rational world is still widely held, reinforced by Charles Darwin’s highly influential work, The Origin of Species, which established the doctrine of natural selection.
paras.zh: 这种关于前理性世界的图景至今仍广为接受，查尔斯·达尔文极具影响力的著作《物种起源》又强化了这一图景，该书确立了自然选择学说。

w.m: adj. 前理性的；理性出现之前的
广为接受的；普遍持有的

paras.en: This doctrine, which takes for granted that those species best able to adapt to and master the natural environment in which they live will survive, has suggested that the struggle for survival is an inherent human trait which determines a person’s success.
paras.zh: 这一学说理所当然地认为，那些最能适应并主宰自己所生活的自然环境的物种将会存活下来；它还暗示，生存斗争是人类固有的一种特性，决定着一个人能否成功。

paras.en: Darwin’s theory has even been summarized as “survival of the fittest”—a phrase Darwin himself did not coin—further highlighting competition’s role in success.
paras.zh: 人们甚至把达尔文的理论概括为“适者生存”（这个说法并非达尔文本人首创），这进一步凸显了竞争在成功中的作用。

paras.en: As has often been pointed out, however, there is nothing in the concept of natural selection that suggests that competition is the most successful strategy for “survival of the fittest.”
paras.zh: 然而，正如人们常常指出的那样，自然选择这一概念中并没有任何内容表明，竞争是实现“适者生存”的最成功策略。

paras.en: Darwin asserted in The Origin of Species that the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation.
paras.zh: 达尔文在《物种起源》中断言，他所描述的斗争应当被视为隐喻，而且很容易就可以涵盖依存与合作。

paras.en: Many studies have been conducted to test the importance placed on competition—as opposed to other values, such as cooperation—by various cultures, and generally conclude that Americans uniquely praise competition as natural, inevitable, and desirable.
paras.zh: 为了检验不同文化对竞争（相对于合作等其他价值观而言）的重视程度，人们已开展了许多研究，这些研究普遍得出结论：唯独美国人把竞争称颂为自然的、必然的、可取的。

w.m: adj. 各种各样的；不同的
adj. 必然的；不可避免的
adj. 可取的；值得拥有的

paras.en: In 1937, the world-renowned anthropologist Margaret Mead published Cooperation and Competition among Primitive Peoples, based on her studies of several societies that did not prize competition, and, in fact, seemed at times to place a negative value on it.
paras.zh: 1937年，世界著名人类学家玛格丽特·米德出版了《原始民族的合作与竞争》一书，该书基于她对几个社会的研究，这些社会并不看重竞争，事实上，有时似乎还对竞争持否定态度。

paras.en: One such society was the Zuni Indians of New Mexico, and they, Mead found, valued cooperation far more than competition.
paras.zh: 新墨西哥州的祖尼印第安人就是这样的社会之一，米德发现，他们对合作的重视远远超过对竞争的重视。

paras.en: After studying these cultures, Mead came to the final conclusion that competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior, and that its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it.
paras.zh: 研究了这些文化之后，米德最终得出结论：竞争性是人类行为中由文化造就的一个方面，它在某一特定社会中的盛行程度，取决于该社会对它的重视程度。

passages.name: 2023年12月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 选择断网也关乎特权
passages.genre: 议论文 · 网络与社会
passages.summary: 歌手兼演员赛琳娜·戈麦斯为改善心理健康，四年半没有上网，她说暂别社交媒体是她为心理健康做过的最好决定。但作者指出，社会日益数字化，主动选择不使用互联网成了一件关乎特权的事；在英国，过去两年里数字鸿沟不断加剧，导致较贫困的家庭家中没有宽带连接。作者认为，应当允许觉得社交媒体损害了自己心理健康的人断开网络，也应投入更多资源、推出更多举措，让身处数字排斥之中的人首先能够接入网络。

paras.en: Could you get by without using the internet for four and a half years?
paras.zh: 你能四年半不用互联网也过得下去吗？

paras.en: That’s exactly what singer and actress Selena Gomez has done in a bid to improve her mental health.
paras.zh: 歌手兼演员赛琳娜·戈麦斯为了改善自己的心理健康，恰恰就是这么做的。

paras.en: She has spoken extensively about the relationship between her social media usage and her mental wellbeing, recalling feeling like “an addict” when she became Instagram’s most followed user in 2016.
paras.zh: 她曾详细谈论过自己使用社交媒体的情况与心理健康状况之间的关系，还回忆说，2016年成为Instagram上关注者最多的用户时，她觉得自己像个“上瘾的人”。

w.m: adj. 受关注的；关注者多的

paras.en: “Taking a break from social media was the best decision that I’ve ever made for my mental health,” she says.
paras.zh: 她说：“暂别社交媒体，是我为自己的心理健康做过的最好决定。”

w.m: 暂时离开；从……中抽身休息

paras.en: “The unnecessary hate and comparisons went away once I put my phone down.”
paras.zh: “我一放下手机，那些不必要的恶意和比较就都消失了。”

paras.en: Ditching the web at large, however, is a far more subtle and complicated prospect.
paras.zh: 然而，要抛开整个网络，就是一个微妙、复杂得多的设想了。

paras.en: The increasing digitisation of our society means that everything from paying a gas bill to plotting a route to a friend’s house and even making a phone call is at the mercy of your internet connection.
paras.zh: 我们社会日益数字化，这意味着从缴纳燃气费到规划去朋友家的路线，甚至打电话，一切都受制于你的网络连接。

w.m: adj. 日益增长的；越来越多的

paras.en: Actively opting out of using the internet becomes a matter of privilege.
paras.zh: 主动选择不使用互联网，就成了一件关乎特权的事。

paras.en: Ms Gomez’s multi-millionaire status has allowed her to take the “social” out of social media, so she can continue to leverage her enormous fame while keeping the trolls (恶意挑衅的帖子) at bay.
paras.zh: 戈麦斯女士千万富翁的身份，让她得以把“社交”从社交媒体中剔除，这样她就可以继续利用自己的巨大名气，同时让恶意挑衅的帖子无法近身。

w.m: n. 恶意挑衅的帖子；网络喷子

paras.en: The fact that she’s still the second most-followed woman on Instagram suggests it’s entirely possible to maintain a significant web profile to promote various projects—by way of a dedicated team—without being exposed to the cruel comments, hate mail and rape or death threats.
paras.zh: 她至今仍是Instagram上关注者第二多的女性，这一事实表明，完全有可能借助一支专职团队，在网上保持可观的知名度来宣传各种项目，而不必接触那些恶毒的评论、仇恨信件以及强奸或死亡威胁。

paras.en: It goes without saying that this is fundamentally different from how the rest of us without beauty deals and films to publicise use the likes of Instagram, TikTok and Twitter, but even the concept of a digital detox (戒瘾) requires having a device and connectivity to choose to disconnect from.
paras.zh: 不用说，我们其他人既没有美妆合约，也没有电影要宣传，使用Instagram、TikTok和Twitter这类平台的方式与她的做法有着根本的不同；但即便是数字戒瘾这一概念，也要求人得先拥有设备和网络连接，才能选择与之断开。
