paras.en: One way we can check our internal biases and inconsistencies is through the social verification of knowledge, in which we test our ideas in a rigorous and systematic way to see if they make sense not just to us, but to other people.
paras.zh: 我们要检查自身内在的偏差和不一致之处，一种方法是借助知识的社会验证，即以严谨、系统的方式检验我们的想法，看它们是否不仅对我们自己说得通，对其他人也说得通。

paras.en: The outstanding example of this socially shared cognition is science.
paras.zh: 科学就是这种社会共享认知的突出范例。

w.m: adv. 在社会层面；社会性地

paras.en: That does not mean that individuals are not capable of excellent thinking, nor does it mean no individual is rational.
paras.zh: 这并不意味着个人没有能力出色地思考，也不意味着没有哪个人是理性的。

w.m: conj. 也不（后接倒装语序）

paras.en: But the extent to which individuals can do this on their own is a function of how well integrated they are with communities of systematic inquiry in the first place.
paras.zh: 但个人能在多大程度上独立做到这一点，取决于他们原本与从事系统探究的群体融合得有多好。

paras.en: You can’t learn to think well by yourself.
paras.zh: 你无法独自学会好好思考。

paras.en: In matters of science at least, those who value their common sense over methodological, collaborative investigation imagine themselves to be more free in their thinking, unbound by involvement with the group, but in reality they are tightly bound by their capabilities and perspectives.
paras.zh: 至少在科学问题上，那些把自己的常识看得比讲求方法的协作研究更重要的人，自以为思维更加自由，不会因与群体有所牵连而受到束缚；但实际上，他们被自身的能力和视角紧紧束缚着。

w.m: adj. 讲求方法的；方法上的

paras.en: We are smarter together than we are individually, and perhaps that’s just common sense.
paras.zh: 我们在一起比各自单独时更聪明，或许这本来就是常识。

passages.name: 2022年6月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 为选拔严格的美国高校正名
passages.genre: 议论文 · 教育与社会
passages.summary: 美国选拔严格的高校被指过于精英化、收费过高，而且没有为职场培养毕业生；作者认为，这些指责忽视了一个事实：这些高校仍在帮助学生做好准备，让他们能在工作中取得成功、参与公民生活、终身学习并理解世界。作者指出，政府中的一些人正在攻击这些高校，税改法案保留了对部分高校投资收益征收的新税，这项针对捐赠基金的新税抽走了助学金经费。作者还以学术研究为据，说明文科教育是极好的职业准备，并指出中低收入家庭如今比以往任何时候都更容易进入这些高校接受教育，而经济背景的多样性也让全体学生所受的教育和获得的体验得到提升。

paras.en: Selective colleges and universities in the U.S. are under fire for being too elite and too expensive, and for not training graduates for the world of work.
paras.zh: 美国选拔严格的高校正受到抨击，被指过于精英化、收费过高，而且没有为职场培养毕业生。

w.m: adj. 选拔严格的；择优录取的

paras.en: Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live.
paras.zh: 这类指责忽视了一个事实：这些院校仍在帮助学生做好准备，让他们能在工作中取得成功、深思熟虑地参与公民生活、终身学习，并理解这个世界以及与自己共同生活的人。

w.m: adj. 深思熟虑的；有思想的

paras.en: These colleges and universities must be doing something right.
paras.zh: 这些高校一定有做得对的地方。

w.m: 做对了某些事；有做得对的地方

paras.en: Applications are at record highs, and their financial aid programs make them more accessible than ever.
paras.zh: 申请数量创下历史新高，而这些高校的助学金项目也让它们比以往任何时候都更容易进入。

w.m: 处于历史最高水平；创历史新高
adj. 可进入的；可获得的

paras.en: This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation.
paras.zh: 长期以来，这种教育模式在创造机会、推动经济增长和激励创新方面一直发挥着核心作用。

paras.en: Yet, there is growing skepticism about the value of this model.
paras.zh: 然而，人们对这种模式的价值越来越怀疑。

w.m: adj. 日益增长的；越来越多的

paras.en: The recent tax reform bill is a wake-up call that our strongest colleges and universities are under assault by some in government.
paras.zh: 最近的税制改革法案敲响了警钟：我们实力最强的高校正遭到政府中一些人的攻击。

paras.en: The initial proposals would have made education unaffordable for many by taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest.
paras.zh: 最初的提案要对研究生的学费减免征税，并取消学生贷款利息的税收扣除，这本会让许多人负担不起教育费用。

paras.en: Thankfully, these provisions were ultimately stripped from the bill, but lawmakers let stand a new tax on the investment income of some colleges and universities.
paras.zh: 所幸，这些条款最终从法案中删去了，但立法者保留了一项针对部分高校投资收益的新税。

paras.en: While these attacks are motivated by misguided ideas, we need to do a better job of explaining why these claims are false and why what we do is valuable.
paras.zh: 虽然这些攻击出于错误的观念，但我们需要更好地说明，为什么这些说法不实，为什么我们所做的事情有价值。

w.m: adj. 错误的；误入歧途的

paras.en: We cannot take for granted that any of this is obvious.
paras.zh: 我们不能想当然地认为其中任何一点是显而易见的。

w.m: 想当然地认为；认为……理所当然
adj. 显而易见的；明显的

paras.en: It is often said that elite colleges and universities do not train students, particularly those who study the liberal arts, for the workforce.
paras.zh: 人们常说，精英高校没有为职场培养学生，尤其是学文科的学生。

paras.en: But this can be refuted by scholarly research.
paras.zh: 但学术研究可以驳斥这一说法。

paras.en: The data are clear: a liberal arts education is great career preparation, both for excellent lifetime earnings and for satisfaction with the work.
paras.zh: 数据清楚地表明：无论是要获得丰厚的终生收入，还是要对工作感到满意，文科教育都是极好的职业准备。

w.m: adj. 极好的；（收入）优厚的

paras.en: This education develops the skills of critical thinking, rigorous analysis of data and facts, communication with the written and spoken word, understanding of cultural differences and issues, and the ability to keep learning.
paras.zh: 这种教育培养的是批判性思维、严谨分析数据和事实、用书面语和口语交流、理解文化差异和文化问题的技能，以及持续学习的能力。

paras.en: In fact, liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field.
paras.zh: 事实上，文科毕业生在能想到的每一个领域都表现得极为出色。

w.m: adj. 能想到的；可以想象的

paras.en: Access to an education at selective colleges and universities is now more available than ever to low- and middle-income families.
paras.zh: 如今，中低收入家庭比以往任何时候都更容易获得在选拔严格的高校接受教育的机会。

w.m: 获得……的机会；进入……的途径
adj. 选拔严格的；择优录取的

paras.en: We have built endowments from donations by alumni (校友) and parents who understand and appreciate our mission to provide access and opportunity, and a significant portion of the returns from these endowments is used to fund financial aid.
paras.zh: 我们利用校友和家长的捐款建立了捐赠基金，这些捐赠者理解并赞赏我们提供入学途径和机会的使命；这些基金的收益中，有相当大一部分用于为助学金提供资金。

w.m: n. 入学途径；（获得某物的）机会

paras.en: Ironically, the new tax on endowments drains financial aid funds from the very schools most able to offer opportunity to those who have earned a spot but cannot otherwise afford this education.
paras.zh: 讽刺的是，这项针对捐赠基金的新税，恰恰从这样一些学校抽走了助学金经费：它们最有能力为那些已赢得入学名额、但没有资助就负担不起这种教育的人提供机会。

w.m: 赢得名额；赢得一席之地

paras.en: Beyond the virtue of access to those who have earned a place at these schools, the diversity of economic backgrounds enhances the education and experience of all of our students.
paras.zh: 除了让那些已赢得这些学校入学名额的人能够入学这一好处之外，经济背景的多样性还让我们全体学生所受的教育和获得的体验都得到提升。

w.m: n. 入学机会；进入的途径
赢得名额；赢得一席之地

passages.name: 2021年12月 第3套 Passage Two
passages.title: 文化差异绝大部分与国别无关
passages.genre: 议论文 · 文化与社会
passages.summary: 说起来自别处的人，我们似乎不可避免地会根据其原籍国来描述他们的特点，但新近发表的研究表明，这类概括是错误的。三位研究人员分析了几十年来基于价值观的调查，发现文化价值观的差异只有16%到21%能用国家之间的差异来解释；年龄等人口统计因素和长期失业率等环境因素与文化价值观的相关性都高于国籍，而职业和社会经济地位的相关性最强。文章指出，我们对国家的关注可能会掩盖各国内部的巨大差异；在大多数情况下，我们最好依据收入等制约人们生活的因素来识别人，而不是依据地图上的界线。

paras.en: Look at the people around you.
paras.zh: 看看你周围的人。

paras.en: Some are passive, others more aggressive.
paras.zh: 有的人消极被动，有的人则更为强势。

w.m: adj. 强势的；积极进取的

paras.en: Some work best alone, others crave companionship.
paras.zh: 有的人独自工作时表现最好，有的人则渴望有人陪伴。

paras.en: We easily recognize that there is great variation among the individuals who live near us.
paras.zh: 我们很容易认识到，住在我们附近的人个体差异很大。

paras.en: Yet, when we speak of people from elsewhere, we seem to inevitably characterize them based on their country of origin.
paras.zh: 然而，说起来自别处的人，我们似乎不可避免地会根据他们的原籍国来描述其特点。

w.m: adv. 不可避免地；必然地

paras.en: Statistics specialists, when they speak of national averages, often make the same mistake.
paras.zh: 统计专家在谈到全国平均水平时，常常犯同样的错误。

paras.en: Newly published research shows how erroneous such overviews are.
paras.zh: 新近发表的研究表明，这类概括有多么错误。

w.m: adj. 已发表的；已出版的

paras.en: Three researchers analyzed decades of values-based surveys and found that only between 16% and 21% of the variation in cultural values could be explained by differences between countries.
paras.zh: 三位研究人员分析了几十年来基于价值观的调查，发现文化价值观的差异只有16%到21%能用国家之间的差异来解释。

paras.en: In other words, the vast majority of what makes us culturally distinct from one another has nothing to do with our homeland.
paras.zh: 换句话说，让我们在文化上彼此有别的因素，绝大部分都与我们的祖国毫无关系。

paras.en: To determine what factors really are associated with culture, the authors combined data from 558 prior surveys that each measured one or more of Hofstede’s cultural dimensions.
paras.zh: 为了确定哪些因素真正与文化相关，作者们合并了此前558项调查的数据，这些调查每项都测量了霍夫斯泰德文化维度中的一项或多项。

paras.en: These are traits, such as individualism and masculinity, that describe work-related cultural values.
paras.zh: 这些维度是个人主义、男性化之类的特征，描述的是与工作相关的文化价值观。

paras.en: (They are not a measure of visible cultural traits, such as food or dress.)
paras.zh: （这些维度衡量的并不是食物、服饰之类看得见的文化特征。）

paras.en: Though the validity of Hofstede’s dimensions has been questioned, they have the singular benefit of having been in use for decades, which allows for historical and international comparisons.
paras.zh: 尽管霍夫斯泰德文化维度的有效性受到过质疑，但它们有一个独特的优势：已经使用了几十年，这使历史比较和国际比较成为可能。

paras.en: The researchers found that both demographic factors, such as age, and environmental factors, such as long-term unemployment rates, were more correlated with cultural values than nationality.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，无论是年龄等人口统计因素，还是长期失业率等环境因素，与文化价值观的相关性都高于国籍。

w.m: adj. 人口统计的；人口的

paras.en: Occupation and socio-economic status were the most strongly correlated, suggesting that our values are more economically driven than we usually give them credit for.
paras.zh: 职业和社会经济地位的相关性最强，这表明我们的价值观比我们通常认为的更受经济驱动。

w.m: adj. 受……驱动的；由……推动的
认为某人（某物）具有（某种特点）

paras.en: The evidence implies that people with similar jobs and incomes are more culturally alike, regardless of where they live.
paras.zh: 这些证据意味着，职业和收入相近的人，无论住在哪里，在文化上都更为相似。

paras.en: Vas Taras, the lead author of the study, puts it this way: “Tell me how much you make and I will make a pretty accurate prediction about your cultural values.
paras.zh: 该研究的第一作者瓦斯·塔拉斯是这样说的：“告诉我你挣多少钱，我就会对你的文化价值观做出相当准确的预测。

paras.en: Tell me what your nationality is and I probably will make a wrong prediction.”
paras.zh: 告诉我你的国籍是什么，我很可能会做出错误的预测。”

paras.en: Taras says our erroneous belief that countries are cultures has caused businesses to teach their employees useless or even harmful ways of interacting with their international peers.
paras.zh: 塔拉斯说，我们以为国家就是文化，这种错误的看法已经导致企业教员工用一些无用甚至有害的方式与国际同行打交道。

paras.en: Chinese and American lawyers might be trained to interact based on the assumption that the Chinese person is less individualistic, even though their similar socio-economic situations make it probable they are actually quite alike in that regard.
paras.zh: 中国律师和美国律师可能会接受培训，基于中方个人主义倾向更弱这一假设来打交道，尽管双方相近的社会经济状况使他们在这方面实际上很可能相当相似。

paras.en: The country, as the unit of authority, is often a convenient way of generalizing about a population.
paras.zh: 国家作为权力单位，常常是笼统描述某一人群的便捷方式。

w.m: 笼统地描述；概括地谈论
n. 人群；（某一地区的）全体居民

paras.en: However, our focus on countries can mask broad variations within them.
paras.zh: 然而，我们对国家的关注可能会掩盖各国内部的巨大差异。

paras.en: In the majority of cases we would be better off identifying people by the factors that constrain their lives, like income, rather than by the lines surrounding them on a map.
paras.zh: 在大多数情况下，我们最好依据收入等制约人们生活的因素来识别人，而不是依据地图上环绕他们的那些线条。

passages.name: 2021年12月 第3套 Passage One
passages.title: 自动化冲击就业，须为未来早作规划
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科技与就业
passages.summary: 作者认为，自动化正在极大地重塑我们的工作方式，越来越多地取代工作岗位，留下的优质新岗位却太少；一份报告显示，制造业流失的工作岗位中只有13%是贸易造成的，其余都源于技术进步。抵制自动化是徒劳的，人们却执意无视它的危险，没能向前看；而劳动年龄男性中每六人就有一人没有工作，女性劳动参与率也已回落，可见作者并没有夸大这种危险。作者呼吁，要让每个人都有经济保障，就需要开始思考如何正当合理地应对自动化。

paras.en: The subject of automation and its role in our economy has taken hold in American public discourse.
paras.zh: 自动化及其在我国经济中的作用这一话题，已在美国的公共讨论中扎下根来。

paras.en: Technology broadly and automation specifically are dramatically reshaping the way we work.
paras.zh: 宽泛地说是技术，具体地说是自动化，正在极大地重塑我们的工作方式。

paras.en: And we need to have a plan for what’s still to come.
paras.zh: 而且，我们需要为今后还将发生的事情做好规划。

w.m: 为……做好规划；为……制订计划
将要发生的；即将到来的

paras.en: We don’t have to look further than our own communities to see the devastating impact of automation.
paras.zh: 要看到自动化造成的毁灭性影响，我们只需看看自己所在的社区就够了。

w.h: not have to look further than
w.m: 只需看看……就够了；不必舍近求远
adj. 毁灭性的；破坏力极大的

paras.en: From automated warehouses to cashierless grocery stores to neighborhood libraries that offer self-checkout lanes instead of employing real people—automation is increasingly replacing jobs and leaving too few good new jobs behind.
paras.zh: 从自动化仓库到无人收银的杂货店，再到设置自助借书通道而不雇用真人的社区图书馆——自动化正越来越多地取代工作岗位，留下的优质新岗位却太少。

w.m: adj. 无收银员的；无人收银的
自助结账通道（在图书馆指自助借书通道）

paras.en: The statistics in manufacturing are staggering.
paras.zh: 制造业的统计数据令人震惊。

w.m: adj. 令人震惊的；惊人的

paras.en: Despite the widespread fears about trade, a recent report showed that just 13 percent of jobs lost in manufacturing are due to trade—the rest of the losses have been due to advances in technology.
paras.zh: 尽管人们普遍对贸易心存担忧，但最近的一份报告显示，制造业流失的工作岗位中只有13%是贸易造成的——其余的流失都源于技术进步。

paras.en: That is why more people are criticizing the ever-increasing role of technology in our economy.
paras.zh: 正因如此，越来越多的人对技术在我国经济中日益扩大的作用提出批评。

w.m: 这就是……的原因；正因如此
adj. 不断增长的；日益扩大的

paras.en: Our country is manufacturing more than ever before, but we are doing it with fewer workers.
paras.zh: 我国的制造业产量比以往任何时候都多，但我们用的工人却更少了。

paras.en: However, it’s not just factories that are seeing losses—software and information technology are also having a dramatic impact on jobs most people think are secure from the forces of a rapidly changing economy.
paras.zh: 然而，出现岗位流失的不只是工厂——软件和信息技术也正在对一些工作岗位产生巨大影响，而大多数人认为，这些岗位不会受到快速变化的经济力量冲击。

w.m: v. 经历；出现（某种情况）

paras.en: Something transformative is happening in America that is having an adverse effect on American families.
paras.zh: 美国正在发生一场深刻的变革，这场变革正对美国家庭产生不利影响。

w.m: adj. 引起变革的；变革性的

paras.en: Whether policymakers and politicians admit it or not, workers have made clear their feelings about their economic insecurity and desire to keep good jobs in America.
paras.zh: 无论政策制定者和政界人士承认与否，工人们都已清楚地表明了自己对经济上缺乏保障的感受，以及让好工作留在美国的愿望。

paras.en: So why are people so insistent on ignoring the perils of automation?
paras.zh: 那么，人们为什么如此执意无视自动化的危险呢？

paras.en: They are failing to look ahead at a time when planning for the future is more important than ever.
paras.zh: 在为未来做规划比以往任何时候都更重要的当下，他们却没能向前看。

paras.en: Resisting automation is futile: it is as inevitable as industrialization was before it.
paras.zh: 抵制自动化是徒劳的：它就像此前的工业化一样不可避免。

paras.en: I sincerely hope that those who assert that automation will make us more effective and pave the way for new occupations are right, but the reality of automation’s detrimental effects on workers makes me skeptical.
paras.zh: 有些人断言，自动化会让我们更有成效，并为新的职业铺平道路，我真心希望他们是对的；但自动化对工人造成有害影响这一现实，让我心存怀疑。

paras.en: No one can currently say where the new jobs are coming from or when, and any sensible company or country should prepare for all alternatives.
paras.zh: 目前，谁也说不清新的工作岗位会从哪里来、什么时候来，任何明智的公司或国家都应该为各种可能的情况做好准备。

w.m: n. 可能的情况；可供选择的事物

paras.en: I’m not overstating the danger: look at what’s happened to the labor force.
paras.zh: 我并没有夸大这种危险：看看劳动力队伍都发生了什么就知道了。

paras.en: According to economic research, one in six working-age men, 25–54, doesn’t have a job.
paras.zh: 根据经济研究，在25至54岁的劳动年龄男性中，每六人就有一人没有工作。

w.m: adj. 劳动年龄的；适龄工作的

paras.en: Fifty years ago, nearly 100 percent of men that age were working.
paras.zh: 五十年前，这一年龄段的男性中有近100%都在工作。

paras.en: Women’s labor force participation, meanwhile, has slipped back to the level it was at in the late 1980s.
paras.zh: 与此同时，女性的劳动参与率已回落到20世纪80年代末的水平。

w.m: adj. （某一时期）末期的；后期的

paras.en: American families and prominent business leaders are aware that there’s a big problem with automation.
paras.zh: 美国家庭和知名商界领袖都意识到，自动化存在一个大问题。

paras.en: The value of a college degree is diminishing, and our upward mobility is declining.
paras.zh: 大学学位的价值正在降低，我们的向上流动性也在下降。

w.m: 向上（社会）流动性；地位上升的机会

paras.en: If we want an economy that allows everyone to be economically secure, we need to start thinking about how we can rightfully address automation.
paras.zh: 如果我们想要一个能让每个人都有经济保障的经济体系，就需要开始思考如何正当合理地应对自动化。

passages.name: 2021年12月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 道德型领导缓解员工特权心态的负面影响
passages.genre: 说明文 · 职场与管理
passages.summary: 最近一项研究显示，劳动者中有一小部分人在某种程度上受到特权心态的影响，而且这部分人所占的比例还在不断上升：他们无论自身能力和业绩水平如何，都始终认为自己理应得到特殊待遇和丰厚回报，再加上自我价值感过高，为雇主工作时就没那么卖力。研究结果表明，缓解员工特权心态负面影响的，恰恰是道德型领导：这类领导者传达非常直接、明确的期望，标准始终如一，会指出员工过高的应得感有些扭曲，并说明员工获得想要的回报必须达到的具体、客观的标准。研究人员提醒说，没有哪一种单一的应对方法是完美的解决办法，但道德型领导至少是朝正确方向迈出的关键一步。

paras.en: According to a recent study, a small but growing proportion of the workforce is affected to some degree by a sense of entitlement.
paras.zh: 根据最近的一项研究，劳动者中有一小部分人在某种程度上受到特权心态的影响，而且这部分人所占的比例还在不断上升。

w.m: 特权心态；（自认为）理应享有特权的心理

paras.en: Work is less about what they can contribute and more about what they can take.
paras.zh: 对他们而言，工作与其说关乎自己能贡献什么，不如说关乎自己能索取什么。

w.m: 与其说关乎……不如说关乎

paras.en: It can lead to workplace dysfunction and diminish their own job satisfaction.
paras.zh: 这种心态可能导致职场运转失常，并降低他们自身的工作满意度。

w.m: n. 运转失常；功能失调

paras.en: I’m not referring to employees who are legitimately dissatisfied with their employment conditions due to, say, being denied fair pay or flexible work practices.
paras.zh: 我指的不是那些有正当理由对雇佣条件感到不满的员工，比如说，他们是因为得不到公平的薪酬或灵活的工作方式而不满。

paras.en: I’m talking about those who consistently believe they deserve special treatment and generous rewards.
paras.zh: 我说的是那些始终认为自己理应得到特殊待遇和丰厚回报的人。

paras.en: It’s an expectation that exists irrespective of their abilities or levels of performance.
paras.zh: 无论他们的能力或业绩水平如何，这种期望都存在。

paras.en: As a result of that discrepancy between the privileges they feel they’re owed and their actual performance, and of their inflated sense of self-worth, they don’t work as hard for their employer.
paras.zh: 由于自认为应得的特权与实际业绩之间存在这种落差，再加上自我价值感过高，他们为雇主工作就没那么卖力。

paras.en: They prefer instead to slack off.
paras.zh: 相反，他们宁愿偷懒懈怠。

paras.en: It’s a tendency which many scholars believe begins in childhood due to parents who overindulge their kids.
paras.zh: 许多学者认为，这种倾向始于童年，原因是父母过度溺爱孩子。

w.m: v. 过度溺爱；过分纵容

paras.en: This leads them to expect the same kind of spoilt treatment throughout their adult lives.
paras.zh: 这导致他们成年以后也一直期望得到同样的娇惯待遇。

paras.en: And yet despite how these employees feel, it’s obviously important for their manager to nonetheless find out how to keep them motivated.
paras.zh: 然而，不管这些员工作何感想，对他们的经理来说，弄清楚如何让他们保持积极性显然仍然很重要。

paras.en: And, by virtue of that heightened motivation, performing well.
paras.zh: 并且凭借这种增强的积极性，让他们保持良好的表现。

paras.en: The research team from several American universities surveyed more than 240 individuals.
paras.zh: 来自美国几所大学的研究团队调查了240多人。

paras.en: They sampled managers as well as team members.
paras.zh: 他们抽样调查的对象既有经理，也有团队成员。

w.m: v. 抽样；抽取……作为样本

paras.en: Employee entitlement was measured by statements such as “I honestly feel I’m just more deserving than others.”
paras.zh: 员工特权心态用诸如“说实话，我觉得自己就是比别人更有资格”这样的陈述来衡量。

w.m: n. 特权心态；（自认为）应得的权利
adj. 应得的；值得（回报）的

paras.en: The respondents had to rate the extent of their agreement.
paras.zh: 受访者需要评定自己在多大程度上同意这些说法。

paras.en: Employee engagement, meanwhile, was assessed with statements like “I really throw myself into my work.”
paras.zh: 而员工敬业度则用“我真的全身心投入工作”之类的陈述来评估。

w.m: adv. 另一方面；与此同时
全身心投入；积极投身于

paras.en: The findings revealed ethical leadership is precisely what alleviates the negative effects of employee entitlement.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，缓解员工特权心态负面影响的，恰恰是道德型领导。

w.m: adj. 道德的；合乎道德的
n. 领导（方式）；领导能力
n. 特权心态；（自认为）应得的权利

paras.en: That’s because rather than indulging employees or neglecting them, ethical leaders communicate very direct and clear expectations.
paras.zh: 这是因为道德型领导者既不纵容员工，也不忽视员工，而是传达非常直接、明确的期望。

w.m: adj. 道德的；合乎道德的

paras.en: They also hold employees accountable for their behaviors and are genuinely committed to doing the right thing.
paras.zh: 他们还要求员工为自己的行为负责，并真心致力于做正确的事。

paras.en: Additionally, these leaders are consistent in their standards.
paras.zh: 此外，这些领导者的标准始终如一。

paras.en: They’re also less likely to deviate in how they treat employees.
paras.zh: 在对待员工的方式上，他们出现偏差的可能性也更小。

paras.en: This means, when confronted by an entitled team member, an ethical leader is significantly disinclined to accommodate their demands.
paras.zh: 这意味着，道德型领导者在面对有特权心态的团队成员时，会明显不愿迁就对方的要求。

w.m: adj. 有特权心态的；自认为理应享有特权的
adj. 道德的；合乎道德的

paras.en: He or she will instead point out, constructively and tactfully, exactly how their inflated sense of deservingness is somewhat distorted.
paras.zh: 相反，领导者会以建设性而又得体的方式，确切地指出对方过高的应得感在哪些方面有些扭曲。

w.m: 应得感；觉得自己理应得到回报的心理

paras.en: He or she will then go further to explain the specific, and objective, criteria the employee must meet to receive their desired rewards.
paras.zh: 接着，领导者还会进一步说明，这名员工必须达到哪些具体而客观的标准，才能获得自己想要的回报。

w.m: v. 达到；满足（标准、要求）
adj. 想要的；渴望得到的

paras.en: This shift away from unrealistic expectations is successful because entitled employees feel more confident that ethical leaders will deliver on their promises.
paras.zh: 这种摆脱不切实际期望的转变之所以成功，是因为有特权心态的员工更加确信，道德型领导者会兑现承诺。

w.m: adj. 有特权心态的；自认为理应享有特权的
adj. 道德的；合乎道德的

paras.en: This occurs because they’re perceived to be fair and trustworthy.
paras.zh: 之所以会这样，是因为这些领导者被视为公平、值得信赖的人。

paras.en: The researchers, however, exercise caution by warning that no one single response is the perfect remedy.
paras.zh: 然而，研究人员保持谨慎，提醒说没有哪一种单一的应对方法是完美的解决办法。

w.m: n. 解决办法；补救办法

paras.en: But there’s no denying ethical leadership is at least a critical step in the right direction.
paras.zh: 但不可否认的是，道德型领导至少是朝正确方向迈出的关键一步。

w.m: adj. 道德的；合乎道德的
n. 领导（方式）；领导能力
adj. 关键的；至关重要的
朝正确方向迈出的一步

passages.name: 2021年12月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 从电视到社交网络：理性受到威胁
passages.genre: 议论文 · 媒体与文化
passages.summary: 早在万维网问世很久以前，趋向理性与启蒙的潮流就已受到威胁：正如波兹曼所指出的，电视的兴起带来了从印刷文化到影像文化、从理性到情感的转变；电视还把现代生活的许多方面降格为娱乐、煽情和商业。万维网最初是一种纯文本媒介，被视为追求知识的工具，在十多年里开辟出一个威胁电视对社会掌控的另类空间。然而，社交网络此后让万维网变成了电视价值观的殖民地：它奖励情感诉求而非理性诉求，让我们热衷于博取观众的即时认可，并削弱我们的好奇心。

paras.en: The trend toward rationality and enlightenment was endangered long before the advent of the World Wide Web.
paras.zh: 早在万维网问世很久以前，趋向理性与启蒙的潮流就已受到威胁。

paras.en: As Neil Postman noted in his 1985 book Amusing Ourselves to Death, the rise of television introduced not just a new medium but a new discourse: a gradual shift from a typographic (印刷的) culture to a photographic one, which in turn meant a shift from rationality to emotions, exposition to entertainment.
paras.zh: 正如尼尔·波兹曼在1985年出版的《娱乐至死》一书中所指出的，电视的兴起带来的不只是一种新媒介，还有一种新的话语方式：从印刷文化逐渐转向影像文化，这进而意味着从理性转向情感、从阐释转向娱乐。

paras.en: In an image-centered and pleasure-driven world, Postman noted, there is no place for rational thinking, because you simply cannot think with images.
paras.zh: 波兹曼指出，在一个以图像为中心、受享乐驱动的世界里，理性思维毫无容身之地，因为人根本无法用图像来思考。

paras.en: It is text that enables us to “uncover lies, confusions and overgeneralizations, and to detect abuses of logic and common sense.”
paras.zh: 正是文字使我们能够“揭穿谎言、糊涂观念和以偏概全之论，并识破对逻辑和常识的滥用”。

w.m: n. 以偏概全；过度概括

paras.en: It also enables us “to weigh ideas, to compare and contrast assertions, to connect one generalization to another.”
paras.zh: 文字还使我们能够“权衡各种观点，比较和对照各种论断，把一种概括与另一种概括联系起来”。

paras.en: The dominance of television was not confined to our living rooms.
paras.zh: 电视的主导地位并不局限于我们的客厅。

paras.en: It overturned all of those habits of mind, fundamentally changing our experience of the world, affecting the conduct of politics, religion, business, and culture.
paras.zh: 电视颠覆了所有那些思维习惯，从根本上改变了我们对世界的体验，影响了政治、宗教、商业和文化的运作方式。

paras.en: It reduced many aspects of modern life to entertainment, sensationalism, and commerce.
paras.zh: 它把现代生活的许多方面都降格为娱乐、煽情和商业。

paras.en: “Americans don’t talk to each other; they entertain each other,” Postman wrote.
paras.zh: “美国人彼此之间不交谈，而是互相娱乐。”波兹曼写道。

paras.en: “They don’t exchange ideas; they exchange images.
paras.zh: “他们不交流思想，而是交换图像。

paras.en: They do not argue with propositions; they argue with good looks, celebrities and commercials.”
paras.zh: 他们不用命题来论辩，而是用好看的外表、名人和广告来论辩。”

paras.en: At first, the web seemed to push against this trend.
paras.zh: 起初，万维网似乎在抵制这一潮流。

paras.en: When it emerged towards the end of the 1980s as a purely text-based medium, it was seen as a tool to pursue knowledge, not pleasure.
paras.zh: 它在20世纪80年代即将结束时作为一种纯文本媒介出现，当时被视为追求知识而非享乐的工具。

w.m: adj. 以文本为基础的；纯文字的

paras.en: Reason and thought were most valued in this garden—all derived from the project of the Enlightenment.
paras.zh: 在这片园地里，理性和思想最受重视——这一切都源自启蒙运动的事业。

paras.en: Universities around the world were among the first to connect to this new medium, which hosted discussion groups, informative personal or group blogs, electronic magazines, and academic mailing lists and forums.
paras.zh: 世界各地的大学属于最早接入这一新媒介的一批，这一媒介为讨论组、内容翔实的个人或团体博客、电子杂志以及学术邮件列表和论坛提供了平台。

w.m: adj. 内容翔实的；信息丰富的

paras.en: It was an intellectual project, not about commerce or control, created in a scientific research center in Switzerland.
paras.zh: 它是一项智识事业，无关商业或控制，创建于瑞士的一个科学研究中心。

paras.en: And for more than a decade, the web created an alternative space that threatened television’s grip on society.
paras.zh: 而且在十多年里，万维网开辟出一个另类空间，威胁着电视对社会的掌控。

paras.en: Social networks, though, have since colonized the web for television’s values.
paras.zh: 然而，此后社交网络已经让万维网变成了电视价值观的殖民地。

w.m: v. 将……变为殖民地；占领

paras.en: From Facebook to Instagram, the medium refocuses our attention on videos and images, rewarding emotional appeals—‘like’ buttons—over rational ones.
paras.zh: 从Facebook到Instagram，这种媒介把我们的注意力重新集中到视频和图像上，奖励的是情感诉求——“点赞”按钮——而非理性诉求。

paras.en: Instead of a quest for knowledge, it engages us in an endless zest (热情) for instant approval from an audience, for which we are constantly but unconsciously performing.
paras.zh: 它不是让我们追求知识，而是让我们无休止地热衷于博取观众的即时认可；我们一直在为这些观众表演，只是自己并未意识到。

w.m: adv. 无意识地；不自觉地

paras.en: (It’s telling that, while Google began life as a PhD thesis, Facebook started as a tool to judge classmates’ appearances.)
paras.zh: （很能说明问题的是，Google最初是一篇博士论文，而Facebook起初是用来评判同学长相的工具。）

w.m: 很能说明问题的是；耐人寻味的是

paras.en: It reduces our curiosity by showing us exactly what we already want and think, based on our profiles and preferences.
paras.zh: 它根据我们的个人资料和偏好，向我们展示的恰恰是我们本来就想要的东西、本来就持有的想法，以此削弱我们的好奇心。

paras.en: The Enlightenment’s motto (座右铭) of ‘Dare to know’ has become ‘Dare not to care to know.’
paras.zh: 启蒙运动的座右铭“敢于求知”，已经变成了“敢于不想求知”。

passages.name: 2021年12月 第1套 Passage Two
passages.title: 食品“不含声明”标签的危害
passages.genre: 议论文 · 食品与消费
passages.summary: 近年来，消费者越来越要求了解食品里有什么，食品生产商便推出新标签来满足这一需求、争取竞争优势，甚至开始用所谓的“不含声明”标签标注食品里“没有”什么。作者认为，这类标签利用消费者对食品的恐惧和误解，可能让公司暂时获得营销优势，但从长远来看会适得其反，有可能侵蚀消费者对整个食品行业的信任，使大家的销量都下降；这种做法还传递出不欢迎农业和食品加工创新的信息，最终会导致效率降低、消费者的选择减少、食品更加昂贵。作者警告，如果任由这种做法继续下去，我们所有人都会是输家。

paras.en: In recent years, the food industry has increased its use of labels.
paras.zh: 近年来，食品行业越来越多地使用标签。

paras.en: Whether the labels say ‘non-GMO (非转基因的)’ or ‘no sugar’ or ‘zero carbohydrates’, consumers are increasingly demanding more information about what’s in their food.
paras.zh: 无论标签上写的是“非转基因”“无糖”还是“零碳水化合物”，消费者都越来越要求获得更多信息，了解自己所吃的食品里有什么。

paras.en: One report found that 39 percent of consumers would switch from the brands they currently buy to others that provide clearer, more accurate product information.
paras.zh: 一份报告发现，39%的消费者会放弃目前购买的品牌，转而选择能提供更清晰、更准确产品信息的其他品牌。

paras.en: Food manufacturers are responding to the report with new labels to meet that demand, and they’re doing so with an eye towards giving their products an advantage over the competition, and bolstering profits.
paras.zh: 食品生产商正推出新标签来回应这份报告，以满足这一需求；而他们这样做，是着眼于让自己的产品比竞争对手更具优势，并提高利润。

w.m: 比……更有利的条件；对……的优势
n. 竞争对手（总称）；竞争

paras.en: This strategy makes intuitive sense.
paras.zh: 这一策略从直觉上讲得通。

paras.en: If consumers say they want transparency, tell them exactly what is in your product.
paras.zh: 如果消费者说想要透明度，那就确切地告诉他们你的产品里有什么。

paras.en: That is simply supplying a certain demand.
paras.zh: 这只不过是在满足某种需求。

paras.en: But the marketing strategy in response to this consumer demand has gone beyond articulating what is in a product, to labeling what is NOT in the food.
paras.zh: 但为回应消费者的这一需求而制定的营销策略，已经超出了清楚说明产品里有什么的范围，发展到标注食品里“没有”什么。

w.m: v. 清楚说明；明确表达

paras.en: These labels are known as “absence claims” labels, and they represent an emerging labeling trend that is detrimental to both the consumers who purchase the products and the industry that supplies them.
paras.zh: 这类标签被称为“不含声明”标签，它们代表着一种新兴的标注趋势，而这种趋势既有损于购买这些产品的消费者，也有损于供应这些产品的行业。

w.m: 不含声明（标明产品不含某种成分）

paras.en: For example, Hunt’s put a “non-GMO” label on its canned crushed tomatoes a few years ago—despite the fact that at the time there was no such thing as a GMO tomato on the market.
paras.zh: 例如，几年前，Hunt’s在其罐装番茄碎上贴了“非转基因”标签，尽管当时市场上根本没有转基因番茄这种东西。

paras.en: Some dairy companies are using the “non-GMO” label on their milk—another label that creates unnecessary fear around food—despite the fact that all milk is naturally GMO-free.
paras.zh: 一些乳品公司正在自家牛奶上使用“非转基因”标签（这又是一个让人对食品产生不必要恐惧的标签），尽管所有牛奶天然就不含转基因成分。

w.m: adj. 不含转基因成分的

paras.en: While creating labels that play on consumer fears and misconceptions about their food may give a company a temporary marketing advantage over competing products on the grocery aisle, in the long term this strategy will have just the opposite effect: by injecting fear into the discourse about our food, we run the risk of eroding consumer trust in not just a single product, but the entire food business.
paras.zh: 虽然制作标签来利用消费者对食品的恐惧和误解，可能会让一家公司在超市货架上暂时获得胜过竞争产品的营销优势，但从长远来看，这种策略将产生恰恰相反的效果：我们在有关自己所吃食品的讨论中注入恐惧，就会冒侵蚀消费者信任的风险，而受到侵蚀的不只是消费者对某一种产品的信任，而是对整个食品行业的信任。

w.m: 利用（他人的恐惧、弱点等）

paras.en: Eventually, it becomes a question in consumers’ minds: Were these foods ever safe?
paras.zh: 最终，消费者心里会产生一个疑问：这些食品曾经安全过吗？

w.m: adv. 曾经；（用于疑问句）究竟

paras.en: By purchasing and consuming these types of products, have I already done some kind of harm to my family or the planet?
paras.zh: 购买和食用这类产品，我是不是已经对家人或地球造成了某种伤害？

paras.en: For food manufacturers, it will mean damaged consumer trust and lower sales for everyone.
paras.zh: 对食品生产商来说，这将意味着消费者信任受损，大家的销量都会下降。

paras.en: And this isn’t just supposition.
paras.zh: 而这并不只是猜测。

paras.en: A recent study found that absence claims labels can create a stigma around foods even when there is no scientific evidence that they cause harm.
paras.zh: 最近的一项研究发现，“不含声明”标签可能会使食品蒙上污名，即使并没有科学证据表明这些食品会造成危害。

paras.en: It’s clear that food manufacturers must tread carefully when it comes to using absence claims.
paras.zh: 显然，说到使用“不含声明”，食品生产商必须谨慎行事。

paras.en: In addition to the likely negative long-term impact on sales, this verbal trick sends a message that innovations in farming and food processing are unwelcome, eventually leading to less efficiency, fewer choices for consumers, and, ultimately, more costly food products.
paras.zh: 这种文字把戏除了很可能对销量造成长期的负面影响，还传递出这样的信息：农业和食品加工领域的创新不受欢迎，这终将导致效率降低、消费者的选择减少，并最终使食品更加昂贵。

paras.en: If we allow this kind of labeling to continue, we will all lose.
paras.zh: 如果我们任由这种标注做法继续下去，我们所有人都会是输家。

passages.name: 2021年12月 第1套 Passage One
passages.title: 用社交媒体筛查求职者：利弊与分寸
passages.genre: 议论文 · 职场与社交媒体
passages.summary: 社交媒体无处不在，用它来筛查求职者的做法并不少见：2018年的一项调查发现，近70%的雇主会在录用求职者之前用社交媒体筛查他们。但这种筛查可能暴露年龄、种族、宗教等受保护特征方面的信息，使招聘决定带有偏见；做法不当时，还可能被视为不道德甚至违法。另一方面，社交媒体也是相关信息的宝贵来源，恰当地使用社交媒体筛查有助于避免雇到有害的员工。作者认为，这种筛查必须做到专业而负责，雇主在使用之前，为了遵守所有法律，咨询管理层和法务团队必不可少。

paras.en: Social media is absolutely everywhere.
paras.zh: 社交媒体绝对是无处不在。

paras.en: Billions of people use social media on a daily basis to create, share, and exchange ideas, messages, and information.
paras.zh: 数十亿人每天都用社交媒体来创建、分享和交流想法、消息与信息。

paras.en: Both individuals and businesses post regularly to engage and interact with people from around the world.
paras.zh: 个人和企业都会定期发帖，以便与世界各地的人建立联系、互动交流。

paras.en: It is a powerful communication medium that simultaneously provides immediate, frequent, permanent, and wide-reaching information across the globe.
paras.zh: 它是一种强大的传播媒介，能在全球范围内同时提供即时、频繁、永久且覆盖面广的信息。

w.m: adj. 强大的；有影响力的
adj. 覆盖面广的；影响广泛的

paras.en: People post their lives on social media for the world to see.
paras.zh: 人们把自己的生活发布在社交媒体上，让全世界都能看到。

w.m: 让全世界看到；公之于众

paras.en: Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, and countless other social channels provide a quick and simple way to glimpse into a job candidate’s personal life—both the positive and negative sides of it.
paras.zh: Facebook、Twitter、LinkedIn以及无数其他社交渠道，提供了一种快速简便的方式，让人得以窥见求职者的个人生活——无论是积极的一面还是消极的一面。

w.m: n. 脸书（社交媒体平台）

paras.en: Social media screening is tempting to use as part of the hiring process, but should employers make use of it when researching a potential candidate’s background?
paras.zh: 把社交媒体筛查用作招聘流程的一部分，是很诱人的做法；但雇主在调查潜在人选的背景时，应该利用它吗？

w.m: adj. 诱人的；有吸引力的

paras.en: Incorporating the use of social media to screen job candidates is not an uncommon practice.
paras.zh: 引入社交媒体来筛查求职者，这种做法并不少见。

paras.en: A 2018 survey found that almost 70% of employers use social media to screen candidates before hiring them.
paras.zh: 2018年的一项调查发现，近70%的雇主会在录用求职者之前，用社交媒体筛查他们。

paras.en: But there are consequences and potential legal risks involved too.
paras.zh: 但这其中也涉及一些后果和潜在的法律风险。

w.m: adj. 涉及的；牵涉在内的

paras.en: When done inappropriately, social media screening can be considered unethical or even illegal.
paras.zh: 如果做法不当，社交媒体筛查可能会被视为不道德，甚至违法。

w.m: adj. 不道德的；不合伦理的

paras.en: Social media screening is essentially scrutinising a job candidate’s private life.
paras.zh: 社交媒体筛查本质上就是在仔细审视求职者的私生活。

w.m: v. 仔细审视；详细审查

paras.en: It can reveal information about protected characteristics like age, race, nationality, disability, gender, and religion, and that could bias a hiring decision.
paras.zh: 它可能会暴露受保护特征方面的信息，比如年龄、种族、国籍、残疾、性别和宗教，而这可能使招聘决定带有偏见。

w.m: v. 使有偏见；使有偏向

paras.en: Pictures or comments on a private page that are taken out of context could ruin a perfectly good candidate’s chances of getting hired.
paras.zh: 私人页面上的图片或评论一旦被断章取义，就可能毁掉一位完全合格的求职者被录用的机会。

paras.en: This process could potentially give an unfair advantage to one candidate over another.
paras.zh: 这一过程有可能让一位求职者比另一位求职者占有不公平的优势。

paras.en: It creates an unequal playing field and potentially provides hiring managers with information that can impact their hiring decision in a negative way.
paras.zh: 它会造成不平等的竞争环境，还可能向招聘经理提供一些信息，而这些信息可能会对其招聘决定产生负面影响。

w.m: adj. 不平等的；不公平的

paras.en: It’s hard to ignore social media as a screening tool.
paras.zh: 社交媒体作为一种筛查工具，让人很难忽视。

paras.en: While there are things that you shouldn’t see, there are some things that can be lawfully considered—making it a valuable source of relevant information too.
paras.zh: 虽然有些内容是你不该看的，但也有一些内容可以合法地加以考虑——这也使社交媒体成为相关信息的一个宝贵来源。

paras.en: Using social media screening appropriately can help ensure that you don’t hire a toxic employee who will cost you money or stain your company’s reputation.
paras.zh: 恰当地使用社交媒体筛查，有助于确保你不会雇到会让你破财或玷污你公司声誉的有害员工。

w.m: v. 使损失（金钱等）；使付出代价

paras.en: Consider the lawful side of this process and you may be able to hire the best employee ever.
paras.zh: 考虑这一过程合法的一面，你也许就能雇到有史以来最好的员工。

w.m: adv. （用于最高级后）有史以来；迄今

paras.en: There is a delicate balance.
paras.zh: 这其中存在着一种微妙的平衡。

w.m: adj. 微妙的；需小心处理的

paras.en: Screening job candidates on social media must be done professionally and responsibly.
paras.zh: 在社交媒体上筛查求职者，必须做到专业而负责。

paras.en: Companies should stipulate that they will never ask for passwords; they should also be consistent, document decisions, consider the source used and be aware that other laws may apply.
paras.zh: 公司应该明确规定，自己绝不会索要密码；还应该保持一致、把决定记录在案、考虑所用的来源，并意识到其他法律也可能适用。

w.m: adj. 一致的；始终如一的

paras.en: In light of this it is probably best to look later in the process and ask human resources for help in navigating it.
paras.zh: 鉴于此，最好的做法可能是在流程后期再去查看，并请人力资源部门帮忙应对这一流程。

w.m: v. 应对；处理（复杂情况）

paras.en: Social media is here to stay.
paras.zh: 社交媒体会一直存在下去。

w.m: 会一直存在；已被普遍接受

paras.en: But before employers use social media to screen job candidates, consulting with management and legal teams is essential in order to comply with all laws.
paras.zh: 但在雇主用社交媒体筛查求职者之前，为了遵守所有法律，咨询管理层和法务团队必不可少。

w.m: adj. 必不可少的；至关重要的

passages.name: 2021年6月 第2套 Passage Two
passages.title: 交通拥堵的启示：技术与监管
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科技与社会
passages.summary: 汽车重塑了我们的城市，导航应用能帮少数幸运的司机绕开拥堵，可一旦人人都掌握完备的信息，拥堵只会蔓延到那些看似能绕行的小路上。作者由此得出两点启示：技术的承诺永远不会像我们希望的那样充分兑现，而自发组织也不会把我们带到想去的地方；可以预见，自动驾驶汽车所许诺的那些大得多的进步，也会面临类似的局限。作者最后指出，交通给我们的启示是：鲁莽而不受控制的变革伤害我们和造福我们的可能性一样大，要有更美好的未来，深思熟虑的监管必不可少。

paras.en: The car has reshaped our cities.
paras.zh: 汽车重塑了我们的城市。

paras.en: It seems to offer autonomy for everyone.
paras.zh: 它似乎能给每个人带来自主权。

paras.en: There is something almost delightful in the detachment from reality of advertisements showing mass-produced cars marketed as symbols of individuality and of freedom when most of their lives will be spent making short journeys on choked roads.
paras.zh: 广告展示批量生产的汽车，将其作为个性与自由的象征来推销，而这些汽车一生中的大部分时间都将用于在拥堵的道路上短途行驶；这种广告脱离现实，几乎有几分令人愉快。

w.m: adj. 令人愉快的；讨人喜欢的
adj. 批量生产的；大规模生产的

paras.en: For all the fuss made about top speeds, cornering ability and acceleration, the most useful gadgets on a modern car are those which work when you’re going very slowly: parking sensors, sound systems, and navigation apps which will show a way around upcoming traffic jams.
paras.zh: 尽管人们对最高时速、过弯能力和加速性能大做文章，现代汽车上最有用的装置却是那些在你开得很慢时起作用的东西：泊车传感器、音响系统，以及能指出如何绕开前方交通拥堵的导航应用。

w.m: 对……大做文章；对……大惊小怪
绕开……的路线；绕开……的办法
adj. 即将到来的；前方的

paras.en: This seems to be one of the few areas where the benefit of sharing personal information comes straight back to the sharer: because these apps know where almost all the users are, and how fast they are moving almost all the time, they can spot traffic congestion (堵塞) very quickly and suggest ways round it.
paras.zh: 在少数几个领域里，分享个人信息的好处会直接回到分享者自己身上，这似乎就是其中之一：由于这些应用几乎随时都知道几乎所有用户身在何处、移动速度有多快，它们能很快发现交通拥堵，并建议绕开拥堵的路线。

paras.en: The problem comes when everyone is using a navigation app which tells them to avoid everyone else using the same gadget.
paras.zh: 当人人都在用导航应用、而应用又让他们避开其他所有使用同样装置的人时，问题就来了。

paras.en: Traffic jams often appear where no one has enough information to avoid them.
paras.zh: 交通拥堵往往出现在谁都没有足够信息加以避开的地方。

paras.en: When a lucky few have access to the knowledge, they will benefit greatly.
paras.zh: 少数幸运儿能获得这些信息时，就会大大受益。

paras.en: But when everyone has perfect information, traffic jams simply spread onto the side roads that seem to offer a way round them.
paras.zh: 但如果人人都掌握完备的信息，交通拥堵只会蔓延到那些看似能绕开拥堵的小路上。

paras.en: This new congestion teaches us two things.
paras.zh: 这种新的拥堵给了我们两点启示。

paras.en: The first is that the promises of technology will never be realised as fully as we hope; they will be limited by their unforeseen and unintended consequences.
paras.zh: 第一点是，技术的承诺永远不会像我们希望的那样充分兑现；它们会受制于其未曾预见、也非本意的后果。

w.m: adj. 未预见到的；意料之外的
adj. 非有意的；非本意的

paras.en: Sitting in a more comfortable car in a different traffic jam is pleasant but hardly the liberation that once seemed to be promised.
paras.zh: 坐在一辆更舒适的车里、陷在另一场交通拥堵中，固然惬意，却很难说是当初似乎许诺过的那种解放。

w.m: adj. 令人愉快的；惬意的

paras.en: The second is that self-organisation will not get us where we want to go.
paras.zh: 第二点是，自发组织不会把我们带到想去的地方。

w.h: get sb where they want to go
w.m: 把某人带到想去的地方；使某人如愿

paras.en: The efforts of millions of drivers to get ahead do not miraculously produce a situation in which everyone does better than before, but one in which almost everyone does rather worse.
paras.zh: 数百万司机力图抢先，这些努力并不会奇迹般地造就一个人人处境都胜过从前的局面，而是会造就一个几乎人人处境都差了不少的局面。

paras.en: Central control and collective organisation can produce smoother and fairer outcomes, though even that much is never guaranteed.
paras.zh: 集中控制和集体组织能够带来更顺畅、更公平的结果，尽管就连这一点也从来无法保证。

paras.en: Similar limits can be foreseen for the much greater advances promised by self-driving cars.
paras.zh: 可以预见，自动驾驶汽车所许诺的那些大得多的进步，也会面临类似的局限。

paras.en: Last week, one operated by the taxi company Uber struck and killed a woman pushing her bicycle across a wide road in Arizona.
paras.zh: 上周，出租车公司优步运营的一辆自动驾驶汽车在亚利桑那州撞死了一名推着自行车横穿一条宽阔马路的女子。

paras.en: This was the first recorded death involving a car which was supposed to be fully autonomous.
paras.zh: 这是有记录以来首起与本应完全自动驾驶的汽车有关的死亡事故。

w.m: adj. 有记录的；记录在案的
adj. 自主的；（汽车）自动驾驶的

paras.en: Experts have said that it suggests a “catastrophic failure” of technology.
paras.zh: 专家表示，这表明技术出现了“灾难性故障”。

paras.en: Increasingly, even Silicon Valley has to acknowledge the costs of the intoxicating (令人陶醉的) hurry that characterises its culture.
paras.zh: 就连硅谷也越来越不得不承认，其文化特有的那种令人陶醉的匆忙是有代价的。

w.m: adj. 令人陶醉的；令人兴奋的
v. 是……的特征；使……具有特色

paras.en: What traffic teaches us is that reckless and uncontrolled change is as likely to harm us as it is to benefit us, and that thoughtful regulation is necessary for a better future.
paras.zh: 交通给我们的启示是：鲁莽而不受控制的变革伤害我们和造福我们的可能性一样大；要有更美好的未来，深思熟虑的监管必不可少。

w.m: adj. 鲁莽的；不计后果的
adj. 不受控制的；失控的
adj. 深思熟虑的；周到的
adj. 必要的；必不可少的

passages.name: 2021年6月 第2套 Passage One
passages.title: 绘画不只是艺术，更是学习工具
passages.genre: 议论文 · 艺术与学习
passages.summary: 我们常认为画画需要天赋，这源于我们把绘画主要归为一种艺术形式，而不是一种学习工具；有人认为，正因为如此，许多成年人放弃了画画。人类画画已有73,000年，在很多方面天生就适合画画；有研究人员认为涂画能激活大脑的默认回路，研究也已表明，心不在焉的涂画和写生都能对记忆和视觉感知产生积极影响。因此，作者认为应该把绘画看作一种帮助我们更好地观察和理解世界的工具。

paras.en: We often think of drawing as something that takes inborn talent, but this kind of thinking stems from our misclassification of drawing as, primarily, an art form rather than a tool for learning.
paras.zh: 我们常常把绘画看作一件需要天生才能的事，但这种想法源于我们错误地把绘画主要归为一种艺术形式，而不是一种学习工具。

w.m: adj. 天生的；与生俱来的

paras.en: Researchers, teachers, and artists are starting to see how drawing can positively impact a wide variety of skills and disciplines.
paras.zh: 研究人员、教师和艺术家正开始认识到，绘画能给多种多样的技能和学科带来怎样的积极影响。

w.m: 多种多样的；各种各样的

paras.en: Most of us have spent some time drawing before, but at some point, most of us stop drawing.
paras.zh: 我们大多数人以前都花过一些时间画画，但到了某个阶段，大多数人就不再画了。

w.m: 在某个时候；到了某个阶段
停止做某事；不再做某事

paras.en: There are people who don’t, obviously, and thank God for that: a world without designers and artists would be a very shabby one indeed.
paras.zh: 显然，也有人并没有停止画画，这真是谢天谢地：没有设计师和艺术家的世界，确实会非常寒碜。

paras.en: Some argue that so many adults have abandoned drawing because we’ve miscategorized it and given it a very narrow definition.
paras.zh: 有人认为，之所以有这么多成年人放弃了画画，是因为我们把它归错了类，给它下了一个非常狭隘的定义。

paras.en: In his book, Stick Figures: Drawing as a Human Practice, Professor D. B. Dowd argues that we have misfiled the significance of drawing because we see it as a professional skill instead of a personal capacity.
paras.zh: D.B.多德教授在《火柴人：作为人类实践的绘画》一书中认为，我们把绘画的意义归错了类，因为我们把它看作一种专业技能，而不是一种个人能力。

paras.en: We mistakenly think of “good” drawings as those which work as recreations of the real world, as realistic illusions.
paras.zh: 我们错误地把“好”的画看作那些能够再现真实世界、构成逼真幻象的画。

paras.en: Rather, drawing should be recategorized as a symbolic tool.
paras.zh: 相反，应该把绘画重新归类为一种符号工具。

paras.en: Human beings have been drawing for 73,000 years.
paras.zh: 人类画画已有73,000年。

paras.en: It’s part of what it means to be human.
paras.zh: 画画是人之所以为人的一部分。

w.h: what it means to be human
w.m: 人之所以为人；作为人的意义

paras.en: We don’t have the strength of chimpanzees (黑猩猩) because we’ve given up animal strength to manipulate subtle instruments, like hammers, spears, and—later—pens and pencils.
paras.zh: 我们之所以没有黑猩猩那样的力气，是因为我们放弃了动物的力量，以便操作精巧的工具，比如锤子、长矛，以及后来的钢笔和铅笔。

paras.en: The human hand is an extremely dense network of nerve endings.
paras.zh: 人手是一张极其密集的神经末梢网络。

paras.en: In many ways, human beings are built to draw.
paras.zh: 在很多方面，人类天生就适合画画。

w.m: 生来适合（做）；天生就是为了……

paras.en: Some researchers argue that doodling (涂画) activates the brain’s so-called default circuit—essentially, the areas of the brain responsible for maintaining a baseline level of activity in the absence of other stimuli.
paras.zh: 一些研究人员认为，涂画会激活大脑中所谓的默认回路——本质上就是在没有其他刺激时，负责让大脑活动保持在基准水平的那些脑区。

w.m: 在没有……的情况下；缺少……时

paras.en: Because of this, some believe that doodling during a boring lecture can help students pay attention.
paras.zh: 正因为如此，有些人认为，听枯燥的讲座时涂画能帮助学生集中注意力。

paras.en: In one study, participants were asked to listen to a list of names while either doodling or sitting still.
paras.zh: 在一项研究中，研究人员要求参与者听一串名字，同时要么涂画，要么静坐不动。

paras.en: Those who doodled remembered 29 percent more of the names than those who did not.
paras.zh: 涂画的人记住的名字比没有涂画的人多29%。

paras.en: There’s also evidence that drawing talent is based on how accurately someone perceives the world.
paras.zh: 还有证据表明，绘画天赋基于一个人感知世界的准确程度。

paras.en: The human visual system tends to misjudge size, shape, color, and angles, but artists perceive these qualities more accurately than non-artists.
paras.zh: 人类的视觉系统往往会错判大小、形状、颜色和角度，而艺术家对这些特性的感知比非艺术家更准确。

paras.en: Cultivating drawing talent can become an essential tool to improve people’s observational skills in fields where the visual is important.
paras.zh: 在视觉因素很重要的领域，培养绘画天赋可以成为一种必不可少的工具，用来提高人们的观察技能。

w.m: adj. 必不可少的；极其重要的

paras.en: Rather than think of drawing as a talent that some creative people are gifted in, we should consider it as a tool for seeing and understanding the world better—one that just so happens to double as an art form.
paras.zh: 我们不应把绘画看作某些富有创造力的人天生擅长的一种才能，而应把它看作一种工具，用来更好地观察和理解世界——只是这种工具恰好还兼作一种艺术形式。

w.m: adj. 富有创造力的；有创意的
在……方面有天赋；天生擅长

paras.en: Both absent-minded doodling and copying from life have been shown to positively affect your memory and visual perception, so complain loudly the next time your school board slashes the art department’s budget.
paras.zh: 无论是心不在焉地涂画，还是对着实物写生，都已被证明能对你的记忆和视觉感知产生积极影响，所以下次你们学校董事会大幅削减美术部门的预算时，就大声抗议吧。

w.m: 学校董事会；学区教育委员会
